summary: Target-level revision of cyclotomic arithmetic, unit and Galois limits, classical main conjectures, the all-prime Brumer–Stark proof and the Kurihara–Kolster comparison. There are 68 mathematical targets, with explicit dyadic Kummer/unit proof plans and exact Part II supplier contracts. The generic completed algebra and Fitting carriers are imported. I.8/I.9/L0 retain their separate owner; their finite-to-infinite consumer correction is specified in the handoff. Complete means planned under Protocol §0, not accepted, closed, implemented, or that the requested supplier extensions already exist.

nodes.title: The cyclotomic Z_p-extension
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field inside a fixed algebraic closure K̄, p a prime, and q = p for odd p, q = 4 for p = 2. Let K(μ_{p^∞}) ⊆ K̄ be the field generated over K by all p-power roots of unity and G_∞(K) = Gal(K(μ_{p^∞})/K). The p-adic cyclotomic character χ_cyc : Gal(K̄/K) → Z_p^× (σ(ζ) = ζ^{χ_cyc(σ) mod p^n} for ζ ∈ μ_{p^n}) factors through a continuous injective homomorphism G_∞(K) → Z_p^× with open image. Let Δ_K ⊆ G_∞(K) be its torsion subgroup, which is finite and is the preimage of the torsion of Z_p^× (μ_{p−1} for odd p, {±1} for p = 2). The cyclotomic Z_p-extension of K is K_∞ := K(μ_{p^∞})^{Δ_K}. Its group Γ_K := Gal(K_∞/K) is torsion-free procyclic, and the composite κ := ⟨χ_cyc⟩ of χ_cyc with the projection Z_p^× = μ × (1 + qZ_p) → 1 + qZ_p identifies Γ_K with an open subgroup of 1 + qZ_p; in particular Γ_K ≅ Z_p (non-canonically). K_∞ is the unique subfield of K(μ_{p^∞}) that is Galois over K with group isomorphic to Z_p.
hypotheses: K is a number field and K̄ a fixed algebraic closure; every field below is a subfield of K̄.
p is a prime; q = p if p is odd and q = 4 if p = 2.
κ is the restriction of ⟨χ_cyc⟩ to Γ_K; it is injective with open image in 1 + qZ_p.
proofSteps: Mathlib cyclotomicCharacter supplies the algebraic homomorphism and its action on roots of unity. Each reduction modulo p^n factors through a finite cyclotomic extension, hence is continuous for the Krull topology. The inverse-limit topology gives continuity, and the action on all roots proves injectivity on G_∞(K).
The image is open: Gal(K(μ_{p^n})/K) has index at most [K : Q] in (Z/p^n)^×, using the irreducibility of cyclotomic polynomials over Q (Mathlib IsCyclotomicExtension) and K ∩ Q(μ_{p^n}).

Z_p^× = μ × (1 + qZ_p) with 1 + qZ_p ≅ Z_p torsion-free, so an open subgroup U of Z_p^× has finite torsion and U/U_tors ≅ Z_p; an open subgroup of Z_p^× has a unique quotient isomorphic to Z_p (Sharifi Lemma 3.1.7).
Define K_∞ as the fixed field of Δ_K and identify Γ_K = G_∞(K)/Δ_K by the infinite Galois correspondence (Mathlib InfiniteGalois.fixedField_fixingSubgroup, InfiniteGalois.normalAutEquivQuotient).

Any closed subgroup giving a Z_p quotient contains Δ_K. Its image in G_∞(K)/Δ_K ≅ Z_p must be zero: every nonzero closed subgroup has a finite quotient, which cannot be Z_p. The subgroup therefore equals Δ_K.
acceptance: For K = Q and p odd, Q_∞ is the fixed field of μ_{p−1} ≅ Gal(Q(μ_p)/Q) inside Q(μ_{p^∞}), and κ : Γ_Q ≅ 1 + pZ_p is an isomorphism.
For K = Q and p = 2, Q_∞ is the maximal real subfield of Q(μ_{2^∞}) and κ : Γ_Q ≅ 1 + 4Z_2.

nodes.title: Layers, norms and the exponent shift
nodes.statement: With K_∞/K as in cyclotomic-zp-extension and n ≥ 0, the n-th layer K_n is the fixed field of Γ_K^{p^n}; it is the unique subextension of K_∞/K of degree p^n, Gal(K_n/K) ≅ Γ_K/Γ_K^{p^n} is cyclic of order p^n, K_0 = K, K_n ⊆ K_m for n ≤ m and K_∞ = ⋃_n K_n. For m ≥ n the relative norm N_{K_m/K_n} on elements and on ideals and the restriction Gal(K_m/K) → Gal(K_n/K) are compatible and transitive. The layer index is not the cyclotomic exponent: for K = Q and odd p, Q_n ⊆ Q(μ_{p^{n+1}}); for p = 2, Q_n ⊆ Q(μ_{2^{n+2}}). Every statement of this roadmap indexes towers by the Z_p-layer n, and a source indexed by the cyclotomic exponent is translated by this shift.
hypotheses: K_∞/K is the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of cyclotomic-zp-extension.
n, m are natural numbers.
proofSteps: Closed subgroups of Γ_K ≅ Z_p are 0 and the p^nZ_p; apply the infinite Galois correspondence.
Use Algebra.norm for element norms and Ideal.relNorm for relative ideal norms; prove their tower transitivity and compatibility with principal ideals before descending to ideal classes.
For K = Q, Q(μ_{p^{n+1}}) has Galois group (Z/p^{n+1})^× ≅ μ_{p−1} × Z/p^n for odd p, whose quotient by the torsion is Z/p^n; for p = 2, (Z/2^{n+2})^× ≅ {±1} × Z/2^n.
acceptance: [K_n : K] = p^n for every n.
For K = Q, p odd and n ≥ 1, Q_n ≠ Q(μ_{p^n}) since [Q(μ_{p^n}) : Q] = p^{n−1}(p − 1).

nodes.title: The full cyclotomic group and its decomposition
nodes.statement: For a number field K and prime p, let G_∞(K) = Gal(K(μ_{p^∞})/K) with the cyclotomic character κ_full : G_∞(K) → Z_p^× (injective, open image; an isomorphism for K = Q). For c ∈ κ_full(G_∞(K)) put σ_c = κ_full^{-1}(c). Let Δ_K be the torsion subgroup of G_∞(K). For p odd, Z_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1 + pZ_p) has factors of coprime (supernatural) orders, so G_∞(K) = Δ_K × Γ'_K canonically with Γ'_K = κ_full^{-1}(1 + pZ_p), restriction Γ'_K → Γ_K is an isomorphism, and Δ_K ≅ Gal(K(μ_p)/K); the Teichmüller character ω : Δ_K → μ_{p−1} is the restriction of κ_full. For p = 2 the projection Z_2^× → {±1} defines ω on all of G_∞(K) with kernel Gal(K(μ_{2^∞})/K(i)); G_∞(K) ≅ Δ_K × Γ_K still holds, non-canonically, but Δ_K = G_∞(K) ∩ {±1} can be trivial while K(i) ≠ K (K = Q(√−2)), so Δ_K need not be Gal(K(i)/K); if K has a real place, Δ_K = {±1} ≅ Gal(K(i)/K). Characters of G_∞(K) that are nontrivial on the torsion, such as powers of ω for odd p, do not factor through Γ_K.
hypotheses: K is a number field, p a prime, q as in cyclotomic-zp-extension.
proofSteps: κ_full is the restriction of Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter to K(μ_{p^∞}); injectivity and openness as in cyclotomic-zp-extension.
For odd p, a closed subgroup of μ_{p−1} × (1 + pZ_p) is the product of its prime-to-p and pro-p parts. For p = 2, G_∞(K)/Δ_K ≅ Z_2 is free pro-2, so the extension splits non-canonically.
The example K = Q(√−2): the elements of Z_2^× fixing ζ_8 + ζ_8^3 are those ≡ 1, 3 mod 8, a torsion-free subgroup of index 2.
For K = Q, surjectivity onto Z_p^× follows from the irreducibility of every cyclotomic polynomial over Q.
acceptance: For K = Q: κ_full is an isomorphism G_∞(Q) ≅ Z_p^×, σ_c(ζ) = ζ^c for ζ ∈ μ_{p^∞}, and σ_{−1} is complex conjugation.

nodes.title: Ramification and splitting in the cyclotomic tower
nodes.statement: Let K_∞/K be the cyclotomic Z_p-extension. (a) Every place not above p is unramified in K_∞/K. (b) Every prime above p ramifies in K_∞/K, and there is n_0 ≥ 0 such that every prime of K_{n_0} above p is totally ramified in K_∞/K_{n_0}. (c) No finite prime splits completely: for every finite place v of K the decomposition group D_v ⊆ Γ_K is open, so only finitely many places of K_∞ lie above v; for v ∤ p, D_v is the closure of the subgroup generated by the Frobenius, which has infinite order. (d) Complex conjugations lie in Δ_K, so every real place of K splits completely in K_∞; if K is totally real, K_∞ is totally real. (e) For K = Q, p odd and a prime ℓ ≠ p, D_ℓ is topologically generated by κ^{-1}(⟨ℓ⟩) with ⟨ℓ⟩ = ℓ·ω(ℓ)^{-1}. (f) If L/K is finite Galois of degree prime to p, then L ∩ K_∞ = K and Gal(L K_n/K_n) ≅ Gal(L/K) for every n.
hypotheses: K is a number field, p a prime, K_∞/K the cyclotomic Z_p-extension.
proofSteps: (a): a place v ∤ p is unramified in K(μ_{p^∞}) because p-power cyclotomic extensions are unramified away from p (Tau Ceti GlobalNumberFields Layer 10, cyclotomic ramification).

At each v | p, base change of the cyclotomic extension of Q_p to the finite field K_v remains infinite and eventually totally ramified. Its inertia has nonzero, hence open, image in Γ_K. Finitely many such places give a common n_0 (Sharifi Lemma 3.1.10 and Proposition 3.1.11, pp. 77–78).
For v ∤ p, κ(Frob_v) = ⟨Nv⟩ has infinite order: a positive rational integer Nv > 1 cannot be a p-adic root of unity. Thus D_v is nonzero and open in Z_p. At v | p use the preceding inertia argument.
(d): χ_cyc(c) = −1 is torsion, so c|_{K(μ_{p^∞})} ∈ Δ_K and fixes K_∞.
(e): the arithmetic Frobenius at ℓ acts on μ_{p^∞} by ζ ↦ ζ^ℓ, so its image under κ is ⟨ℓ⟩.
(f): [L ∩ K_∞ : K] divides both [L : K] and a power of p.
acceptance: For p = 3 and ℓ = 2: ⟨2⟩ = −2 ∈ 1 + 3Z_3 has v_3(−2 − 1) = 1, so it topologically generates 1 + 3Z_3 and 2 is inert in every layer of Q_∞/Q.
p is totally ramified in Q_∞/Q (n_0 = 0) and Q_∞ is totally real.
Sharifi Proposition 3.1.11: no finite prime splits completely in F_cyc/F.

nodes.title: The Iwasawa algebra, its coordinate, twists and change of generator
nodes.statement: Let Λ_K = Z_p[[Γ_K]] be the completed group algebra of Γ_K (owned by Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9 and PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras Layer 1). For a topological generator γ of Γ_K, put u = κ(γ) ∈ 1 + qZ_p and let ι_γ : Z_p[[T]] ≅ Λ_K be the continuous isomorphism with T ↦ γ − 1. (i) Change of generator: if γ' = γ^c with c ∈ Z_p^×, then ι_γ^{-1} ∘ ι_{γ'} sends T to (1 + T)^c − 1, its inverse sends T to (1 + T)^{c^{-1}} − 1, u' = u^c, and characteristic ideals are transported along this isomorphism. (ii) Twists: for n ∈ Z the continuous ring automorphism Tw_n of Λ_K with γ ↦ κ(γ)^n γ (T ↦ u^n(1 + T) − 1 in the coordinate) satisfies M(n) ≅ M ⊗ Z_p(n) as Λ_K-modules, char(M(n)) = Tw_{−n}(char M), Tw_0 = id and Tw_n ∘ Tw_m = Tw_{n+m}. (iii) The involution ι : γ ↦ γ^{-1} (T ↦ (1 + T)^{-1} − 1) gives M^ι, used for Pontryagin duals. (iv) The augmentation Λ_K → Z_p has kernel (T).
hypotheses: Γ_K is the Galois group of the cyclotomic Z_p-extension, with κ as in cyclotomic-zp-extension.
c ∈ Z_p^×; n ∈ Z.
proofSteps: Import the completed group algebra and its power-series coordinate for a procyclic pro-p group (ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 9; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras Layer 1).
Change of generator: γ' − 1 = (1 + T)^c − 1 in the γ-coordinate, a continuous automorphism of Z_p[[T]].

Twist: γ ↦ κ(γ)^n γ extends by continuity and the universal property of the completed group algebra; on M ⊗ Z_p(n) the element γ acts as κ(γ)^n γ, hence the formula for characteristic ideals (Kolster Lemma 1.2).
Characteristic ideals and the transport of μ and λ under coordinate changes are imported from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras Layer 4.
acceptance: For M = Z_p(n) (Λ_K acting through κ^n), char(M) = (T − (u^n − 1)).

nodes.title: The kernel of passage to a finite layer
nodes.statement: For n ≥ 0 and a topological generator γ of Γ_K, the projection π_n : Λ_K → Z_p[Gal(K_n/K)] = Z_p[Γ_K/Γ_K^{p^n}] is surjective with kernel the principal ideal (ω_n), ω_n = γ^{p^n} − 1 = (1 + T)^{p^n} − 1; the ideal does not depend on γ. Hence Λ_K = lim_n Λ_K/(ω_n), and for a compact Λ_K-module M the Γ_K^{p^n}-coinvariants are M/ω_n M. The ideals (T^{p^n}) and (T^n) are different from (ω_n) for n ≥ 1.
hypotheses: Γ_K ≅ Z_p with generator γ; n ≥ 0.
proofSteps: Z_p[Γ/Γ^{p^n}] = Z_p[x]/(x^{p^n} − 1) with x = image of γ.
The completed group algebra is the limit of the finite group algebras, and γ^{p^n} − 1 corresponds to (1 + T)^{p^n} − 1 under ι_γ (Sharifi Remark 2.4.3).
Changing γ to γ^c multiplies ω_n by a unit, because (1 + T)^{cp^n} − 1 = ((1 + T)^{p^n} − 1)·(unit) for c ∈ Z_p^×.
ω_n is a distinguished polynomial of degree p^n (Tau Ceti TauCeti.Polynomial.isDistinguishedAt_one_add_X_pow_sub_one at main; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §4.3).
acceptance: n = 0: ω_0 = T, the augmentation ideal.
ω_1 = Σ_{i=1}^{p} C(p,i) T^i has the term pT, so ω_1 ∉ (T^p).

nodes.title: The arithmetic completed action on Galois groups and limits
nodes.statement: Let E/K be a Galois extension inside K̄ with K_∞ ⊆ E and X = Gal(E/K_∞) abelian pro-p. For σ ∈ Γ_K and any lift σ̃ ∈ Gal(E/K), x ↦ σ̃xσ̃^{-1} is independent of the lift, continuous, and defines a continuous action of Γ_K on X; it extends uniquely to a continuous Λ_K-module structure on the compact Z_p-module X. Likewise, for an inverse system (M_n) of finite Z_p[Gal(K_n/K)]-modules with equivariant transition maps, lim_n M_n is a compact Λ_K-module. Continuous equivariant homomorphisms between such modules are Λ_K-linear, and the two constructions agree under the inverse limit of Artin maps (class-field-identification).
hypotheses: E/K Galois, K_∞ ⊆ E, Gal(E/K_∞) abelian pro-p; or (M_n) an inverse system of finite modules over the layers.
proofSteps: Independence of the lift: two lifts differ by an element of the abelian group X, which acts trivially on X by conjugation.
Continuity of the action map Γ_K × X → X follows from continuity of multiplication in Gal(E/K).
A compact Z_p-module with a continuous Γ_K-action is a module over each Z_p[Γ_K/U] on the finite quotients X/V; pass to the limit (Sharifi §2.3, the completed group ring as limit of group rings).
Λ_K-linearity of continuous equivariant maps: they commute with the dense subalgebra Z_p[Γ_K].

nodes.title: The equivariant Iwasawa algebra of an abelian tower over a totally real field
nodes.statement: Let k be totally real, F/k a finite abelian extension, F_∞ = F·k_∞ the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of F, and G = Gal(F_∞/k) (abelian profinite). Then G ≅ G_tors × Γ' with G_tors finite and Γ' ≅ Z_p closed (non-canonically), Γ_F = Gal(F_∞/F) is open in G, and Λ_{F∞} := Z_p[[G]] ≅ Z_p[G_tors][[T]] is a reduced noetherian finite free Z_p[[Γ']]-algebra, a finite product of complete local rings. Its total quotient ring Q(Λ_{F∞}) (localisation at all non-zerodivisors) is a finite product of fields. An element x ∈ Λ_{F∞} is a non-zerodivisor iff ψ(x) ≠ 0 in O_ψ[[T]] for every character ψ of G_tors. For n ≥ 0 the projection Λ_{F∞} → Z_p[Gal(F_n/k)] is surjective with kernel (γ_F^{p^n} − 1), γ_F a generator of Γ_F; for k ⊆ F' ⊆ F restriction Λ_{F∞} → Λ_{F'_∞} is surjective. The sharp involution, character evaluations and invertible fractional Λ_{F∞}-submodules of Q(Λ_{F∞}) (determinant lines) are imported from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras Layers 5–6. When p divides #G_tors the character idempotents of G_tors do not lie in Λ_{F∞} (character-decomposition-integrality).
hypotheses: k totally real, F/k finite abelian, F_∞ the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of F, G = Gal(F_∞/k).
p any prime, p = 2 included.
proofSteps: G is abelian and has an open subgroup Z_p. Its prime-to-p part is finite, and its pro-p part is a finitely generated Z_p-module of rank one. The structure theorem gives G ≅ G_tors × Z_p; the quotient by torsion splits because Z_p is a free Z_p-module.
Z_p[[G_tors × Γ']] = Z_p[G_tors][[T]] by the coordinate of iwasawa-algebra-coordinate; it is finite free over Z_p[[Γ']].

Reducedness: Q_p[G_tors] is semisimple, so Z_p[G_tors] is reduced, and a power-series ring over a reduced noetherian ring is reduced; a reduced noetherian ring has a total quotient ring that is a finite product of fields.
Non-zerodivisors are detected after the injective character map Λ_{F∞} → ∏_ψ O_ψ[[T]] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6 character evaluation).
Finite levels: Gal(F_n/k) = G/Γ_F^{p^n}; apply finite-level-kernel to Γ_F.
acceptance: Kurihara §4.1: Λ_{F∞} = Z_p[[Gal(F_∞/k)]] and its total quotient ring carry g_{F∞/k,S}.

nodes.title: Integral character decomposition and its failure at p
nodes.statement: Let Δ be a finite abelian group and O a finite extension of Z_p containing the values of all characters of Δ. (i) The character map O[Δ] → ∏_{ψ ∈ Δ̂} O, x ↦ (ψ(x)), is injective with finite cokernel; it is an isomorphism iff p ∤ #Δ. (ii) If p ∤ #Δ, then O[Δ][[T]] = ∏_ψ O[[T]], and Fitting ideals, characteristic ideals and determinant lines of finitely generated modules decompose character by character. (iii) If p | #Δ, an element of the total quotient ring with all ψ-components in O[[T]] need not lie in O[Δ][[T]]; an identity of integral group-ring ideals proved after the scalar extension to ∏_ψ O[[T]] must be descended separately, for instance through the character group rings R_Ψ and their component decomposition, or through height-one localisation together with an appropriate reflexivity or invertibility theorem. Height-one agreement alone is not a descent criterion for arbitrary ideals.
hypotheses: Δ finite abelian, O ⊇ Z_p containing the character values.
proofSteps: Injectivity: Q_p[Δ] ⊗ Frac(O) is semisimple with the ψ as its simple factors (Tau Ceti CharacterTheory Layer 3 idempotents).
If p ∤ #Δ the idempotents e_ψ = (#Δ)^{-1} Σ ψ(δ)^{-1}δ are integral; conversely, if the map is an isomorphism then e_{trivial} = (#Δ)^{-1}Σδ is integral, forcing p ∤ #Δ.
Decomposition of Fitting and characteristic ideals over a product ring is componentwise (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4 character decomposition, L6 character group rings).
(iii) the example e = (1 + σ)/2 for Δ = Z/2, p = 2.
acceptance: Δ = Z/2, p = 2: cokernel of Z_2[Δ] → Z_2 × Z_2 has order 2.

sources.match: Defines character group rings R_Ψ as images of O[G] in ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O_ψ, finite-index subrings of products of DVRs, and the component decomposition O[G] = ∏ O[G_p]_χ.
Uses that for #G prime to p the idempotents lie in Z_p[G], which is then a maximal order, a product of DVRs O_ρ.
Relates Fitting ideals of a module and its dual only when the p-part of the group is cyclic, illustrating that p-power order groups need separate integral arguments.

nodes.title: Class-group towers and their limits
nodes.statement: Let K_∞/K be the cyclotomic Z_p-extension with layers K_n, and S a finite set of finite places of K. Put A_n = Cl(O_{K_n}) ⊗ Z_p (the p-part) and A_{n,S} = Cl(O_{K_n,S}) ⊗ Z_p, the quotient of A_n by the classes of the primes above S. For m ≥ n let N_{m,n} : A_m → A_n be induced by the ideal norm and j_{n,m} : A_n → A_m by extension of ideals; N_{m,n} ∘ j_{n,m} is multiplication by p^{m−n} and j_{n,m} ∘ N_{m,n} is the norm element ν_{m,n} = Σ_{σ ∈ Gal(K_m/K_n)} σ. The unramified class module is X_∞ := lim_n A_n along the N_{m,n}, a compact Λ_K-module; X'_{∞,S} := lim_n A_{n,S}; and A_∞ := colim_n A_n along the j_{n,m}, a discrete p-primary Λ_K-module. The same constructions apply to T-smoothed ray class groups Cl^T and to any tower of finite subextensions of an infinite abelian extension (for example the ray tower K(p^∞𝔣) of an imaginary quadratic field), always with norm transition maps.
hypotheses: K a number field, p a prime, K_∞/K cyclotomic; S a finite set of finite places of K.
Transition maps of inverse limits are norms; of direct limits, extension of ideals.
proofSteps: Ideal norm and extension of ideals descend to class groups and to S-class groups (Mathlib ClassGroup; Ideal.relNorm; Tau Ceti ray class groups for Cl^T).

The composite identities follow from N_{K_m/K_n}(𝔞O_{K_m}) = 𝔞^{[K_m:K_n]} for an ideal 𝔞 of K_n, and from the fact that the extension to K_m of the norm of an ideal 𝔄 of K_m is Π_{σ ∈ Gal(K_m/K_n)} σ(𝔄).
The Λ_K-module structures come from arithmetic-compact-action (inverse limit) and from the discrete Γ_K-action (direct limit).
acceptance: K = Q: A_n = 0 for every n and every p, so X_∞ = 0.

Takes h² = lim Cl_{K'}(p) and h¹ = lim (O_{K'}[1/p]^× ⊗ Z_p) over the finite subextensions K' of the ray tower K(p^∞𝔣), with norm transition maps.
Uses the minus parts of A_{K∞} = colim A_{K_n} and of the T-smoothed class groups along the cyclotomic tower of a CM field.

nodes.title: Unit and S-unit towers
nodes.statement: With K_n as above and S a finite set of places of K, put E_n = O_{K_n}^× ⊗_Z Z_p and E_{n,S} = O_{K_n,S}^× ⊗_Z Z_p. Because these unit groups are finitely generated, E_n and E_{n,S} are finitely generated Z_p-modules equal to the p-adic completions of O_{K_n}^× and O_{K_n,S}^×; their torsion is μ_{p^∞}(K_n). The norm maps N_{K_m/K_n} induce transition maps, and E_∞ := lim_n E_n, E_{∞,S} := lim_n E_{n,S} are compact Λ_K-modules. For an arbitrary infinite abelian extension with finite subextensions K', the analogous limit lim_{K'} (O_{K'}[1/p]^× ⊗ Z_p) along norms is defined the same way.
hypotheses: K_n are the layers of the cyclotomic Z_p-extension; S a finite set of places.
proofSteps: Dirichlet's S-unit theorem gives finite generation (Mathlib NumberField.Units.rank for units; S-units through the valuation sequence).
For a finitely generated abelian group B, B ⊗ Z_p = lim B/p^m B.
Norms are Galois-equivariant, so the limits are Λ_K-modules by arithmetic-compact-action.

nodes.title: Semilocal principal units and the global-to-local map
nodes.statement: For a number field E and a prime p, let U(E) = ∏_{v | p} U^1(E_v), the product of the principal units of the completions at the places above p. The canonical map (O_{E_v}^×)^∧_p → U^1(E_v) from the pro-p completion is an isomorphism (the prime-to-p roots of unity die), so the global units define ι_E : O_E^× ⊗ Z_p → U(E); Ē(E) := ι_E(O_E^× ⊗ Z_p) is closed. Along the cyclotomic tower, U_n = U(K_n), local norms define U_∞ = lim_n U_n, ι_n is compatible with norms, and Ē_∞ = lim_n Ē(K_n). For S ⊇ S_p, the pro-p completions ℱ_n = ∏_{v | p} (K_{n,v}^×)^∧_p receive the S-units.
hypotheses: E a number field, p a prime; U^1(E_v) = 1 + 𝔪_v.
proofSteps: Use the local-field unit filtration and Teichmüller splitting from TauCetiRoadmap LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1 to prove O_{E_v}^× = μ_{q_v−1} × U^1(E_v) with U^1 pro-p. At the pins TauCeti.unitsPrincipal only handles Z_p; the newer library has a general unitFiltration, so import its available filtration and supply only the completion and norm compatibility still needed here.
ι_E is the composite of O_E^× ⊗ Z_p → ∏ (O_{E_v}^×)^∧_p with this identification; its image is compact, hence closed.
Local norms are compatible with global norms under the diagonal embeddings.

nodes.title: Leopoldt's conjecture and the Leopoldt defect
nodes.statement: For a number field E and a prime p, Leopoldt's map is ι_E : O_E^× ⊗_Z Z_p → U(E) = ∏_{v|p} U^1(E_v) of semilocal-principal-units. Its kernel is a torsion-free Z_p-module (the torsion μ_{p^∞}(E) of the source embeds), and the Leopoldt defect is δ(E, p) := rank_{Z_p} ker ι_E = (r_1(E) + r_2(E) − 1) − rank_{Z_p} Ē(E). Leopoldt's conjecture for (E, p) is the proposition δ(E, p) = 0, equivalently injectivity of ι_E. This is the strong (field-level) conjecture; the weak Leopoldt property of a Z_p-extension (weak-leopoldt) asks only that δ(K_n, p) stay bounded. The equivalence with the nonvanishing of the p-adic regulator and the logarithmic formulation are comparisons that import this definition.
hypotheses: E a number field, p a prime.
proofSteps: ker ι_E ∩ torsion = 0 because roots of unity of p-power order embed into each E_v.
rank_{Z_p}(O_E^× ⊗ Z_p) = r_1 + r_2 − 1 by Dirichlet's unit theorem (Mathlib NumberField.Units.rank).
acceptance: δ(Q, p) = 0 for every p.
δ(E, p) = 0 for E imaginary quadratic or real quadratic.

nodes.title: Maximal abelian pro-p extensions with prescribed ramification
nodes.statement: Inside K̄, for an algebraic extension E of K and a set S of places of K: M_S(E) is the maximal abelian pro-p extension of E unramified outside the places above S (an archimedean place is unramified when it stays real; for p = 2 real places may ramify only if they lie in S); L(E) := M_∅(E) is the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension; L'_S(E) is the maximal subextension of L(E) in which every place above S splits completely. Put 𝔛_S(E) = Gal(M_S(E)/E), X(E) = Gal(L(E)/E) and X'_S(E) = Gal(L'_S(E)/E). Each satisfies the universal property: every abelian pro-p extension of E with the stated condition lies in it, uniquely. If E is Galois over K, so are M_S(E), L(E), L'_S(E), and for E = K_∞ the groups are compact Λ_K-modules (arithmetic-compact-action). The unramified module X and the S-ramified module 𝔛_S are different objects and are never interchanged in a main conjecture.
hypotheses: K a number field, p a prime, E/K algebraic inside K̄, S a set of places of K.
proofSteps: Compositum of abelian pro-p extensions with the condition again satisfies it, so the maximal one exists (inside K̄).
Galois stability: a K-conjugate of an S-ramified abelian pro-p extension of E is again one when E/K is Galois.

Finite levels are described by class field theory (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layers 11–12): Gal(M_S(E)/E) for E a number field is the pro-p completion of the ray class groups of conductor supported on S.
acceptance: E = Q, S = ∅: L(Q) = Q, so X(Q) = 0.
E = Q, S = {p, ∞}, p odd: M_S(Q) = Q_∞ and 𝔛_S(Q) ≅ Z_p.

sources.locator: Remark 3.2.5, Proposition 3.2.6, Remark 3.2.9 and Definition 3.2.10, pp. 79–80

Identifies X'_∞ with the Galois group of the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension of F_∞ in which the primes above p split completely.
Introduces L_∞, L'_∞ and the maximal abelian pro-p extension M^S_∞ unramified outside S with X_S = Gal(M^S_∞/F_∞), the standard Iwasawa module.

nodes.title: Class-field identification of the Iwasawa modules
nodes.statement: Let K_∞/K be cyclotomic and n_0 as in tower-ramification. (a) The inverse limit of Artin maps gives a canonical isomorphism of Λ_K-modules X(K_∞) ≅ lim_n Gal(L(K_n)/K_n) ≅ lim_n A_n = X_∞ (the second by class field theory at each layer). (b) For S ⊇ S_p, X'_S(K_∞) ≅ lim_n A_{n,S}. (c) For any S, 𝔛_S(K_∞) ≅ lim_n 𝔛_S(K_n) under restriction, and 𝔛_S(K_n) is the pro-p completion of the ray class groups of K_n with conductor supported on S. (d) For n ≥ n_0, L(K_n) ∩ K_∞ = K_n, and the maps (X_∞)_{Γ^{p^n}} → A_n are controlled by the inertia groups at the primes above p (the exact sequence with ker Σ^{(m)} and coker Σ^{(m)}).
hypotheses: K_∞/K the cyclotomic Z_p-extension; S a finite set of places of K.
proofSteps: Every S-ramified abelian pro-p extension of K_∞ is a union of such extensions of the layers (Sharifi Proposition 3.2.6).
Artin reciprocity at each layer, compatible with norm and restriction (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layers 11–12).
For (d): beyond n_0 the primes above p are totally ramified in K_∞/K_n, so no nontrivial unramified extension of K_n lies in K_∞ (Sharifi (3.2.1)).
acceptance: Sharifi Corollary 3.2.7: the inverse limit of Artin maps identifies X_∞ with the Galois group of the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension of F_∞.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.2.6 and Corollary 3.2.7, p. 79; Proposition 3.2.11 and (3.2.1), p. 80; Propositions 3.2.19–3.2.20, p. 83
sources.match: Proves that Gal(L_∞/F_∞) is the inverse limit of the Gal(L_n/F_n), identifies X_∞ with the unramified Galois group, gives the control sequence through inertia at p, and the S-split analogues.
Identifies X_∞ and X'_∞ as Galois groups over F_∞ and states that they are finitely generated torsion Λ-modules.

nodes.title: The global–local unit sequence
nodes.statement: Let K∞/K be cyclotomic, S=S_p∪S∞, and use wide ordinary class groups X=lim Cl(K_n)(p). Put Σ_n=∏_{v real of K_n} μ_2 if p=2, and Σ_n=0 otherwise; let Σ∞=lim Σ_n under the local norm (product over places above v). At every finite layer the exact sequence is 0→D_n→E_n→U_n⊕Σ_n→𝔛_S(K_n)→Cl(K_n)(p)→0, where D_n=H_2(G_S(K_n),Z_p); the image of E_n is its compact local closure. The S-unit version replaces E_n by E_{n,S_p}, U_n by ℱ_n=∏_{v|p}(K_{n,v}^×)^∧_p, and the last term by the p-split class group. Compact norm limits and weak Leopoldt give 0→E∞→U∞⊕Σ∞→𝔛_S(K∞)→X→0 and the analogous S-unit sequence. E∞ is also canonically isomorphic to lim of the images in U_n alone, and is finitely generated over Λ as a submodule of U∞. Thus Σ∞ may be omitted precisely when p is odd or K has no real places; if p=2 then Σ∞≅(Λ/(2))^{r_1(K)}. For μ_{2p}⊆K, the separate discrete Kummer sequence is 0→O_{K∞}^×⊗D→H¹(G_S(K∞),μ_{p∞})→A∞→0, using ordinary direct-limit classes; its Pontryagin dual is 0→A∞^∨(1)→𝔛_S(K∞)→(O_{K∞}^×⊗D)^∨(1)→0. All duals here are contragredient.
hypotheses: K∞/K cyclotomic, p any prime, S=S_p∪S∞. Wide classes require real sign factors at p=2.
For the last Kummer-dual sequence μ_{2p}⊆K; do not identify discrete unit direct limits with compact norm limits.
proofSteps: Apply global Artin reciprocity and Poitou–Tate to finite completed units. With T=∅ in NSW 10.3.13 the local product contains principal p-units and μ_2 at real places; its cokernel maps to the ordinary wide class group. With T=S_p use completed local multiplicative groups and S_p-classes. Infinity is already in S, not inverted as an additional finite prime.

Take norms everywhere. Inverse limits of exact systems of compact abelian groups are exact, including the images of the finite-layer maps. Weak Leopoldt gives lim D_n=H_2(H_S,Z_p)=0. This proves injectivity of E∞ into the augmented local product and identifies E∞ with the inverse limit of its augmented closures (NSW 10.3.24).

To remove signs only from the unit-closure comparison, let K_n^0=ker(E_n→U_n). Then 2K_n^0⊆D_n at p=2, since all signs have exponent two. Consequently lim K_n^0 is killed by 2. But E∞[2]=0: each finite-layer element of order at most two is ±1, and its norm across a quadratic layer is 1. Hence lim K_n^0=0. Compact limit exactness now gives E∞≅lim image(E_n→U_n). The odd-p/no-real case has no sign term from the outset.

The real places split completely throughout the cyclotomic tower. Identify their sign groups at layer n with F_2[Γ/Γ_n]^{r_1(K)}. The local norm is the group-ring projection (sum in additive notation), so Σ∞ is the completed module (Λ/(2))^{r_1(K)}. This does not assert that Σ∞ injects into 𝔛_S; global unit signatures remain in the sequence.
By local finite generation in iwasawa-finiteness, U∞ is a finitely generated Λ-module. The injective E∞→U∞ and noetherianity give finite generation of E∞, without Leopoldt at each layer.

For the discrete Kummer sequence, take roots of elements with ideal a^{p^m}; eventual total ramification above p makes their valuations divisible by p^m at a later layer, so the target is ordinary A∞, not only p-split classes. Kummer exactness and Pontryagin duality give the stated sequence with its twist (Sharifi 3.3.9–3.3.14).
acceptance: For K = Q(μ_p), p odd, (b) is the sequence 0 → ℰ_∞ → 𝒰_∞ → 𝔛_∞ → X_∞ → 0 of Sharifi's AWS notes (2.5.1), and its plus part is the L1 sequence 0 → E^+/C^+ → U^+/C^+ → X^+ → Y^+ → 0 after dividing by cyclotomic units.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.5.4, p. 29; Proposition 3.3.6, p. 86; Proposition 3.3.9, Corollary 3.3.10, p. 86–88; Corollary 3.3.14, p. 89
sources.match: Gives the class-field exact sequences relating global units, semilocal units and the p-ramified and unramified Galois groups at finite level, their inverse limits along the cyclotomic tower, and the Kummer-dual sequence for F ⊇ μ_{2p}.
States the exact sequence 0 → ℰ_∞ → 𝒰_∞ → 𝔛_∞ → X_∞ → 0 with injectivity on the left by weak Leopoldt.

Gives the augmented finite sequence, specifies real local μ_2, and identifies compact norm limits of units with local closures using weak Leopoldt. The p-only comparison is derived above using exponent two and absence of 2-torsion in E∞.

nodes.title: Finite generation and torsion of the arithmetic modules
nodes.statement: For the cyclotomic Z_p-extension K_∞/K and finite S ⊇ S_p: (a) X(K_∞) = X_∞ and X'_S(K_∞) are finitely generated torsion Λ_K-modules; (b) 𝔛_S(K_∞) is a finitely generated Λ_K-module; (c) A_∞^∨ is finitely generated torsion, pseudo-isomorphic to X_∞^ι, and has no nonzero finite Λ_K-submodule; (d) U_∞ is finitely generated over Λ_K; finite generation of E_∞ is the subsequent corollary of global-local-unit-sequence, after the weak-Leopoldt identification. This order avoids using unit injectivity to prove weak Leopoldt. Iwasawa's growth formula for #A_n is imported from IntegralIwasawaTheory L2 and PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4.
hypotheses: K_∞/K cyclotomic; S finite containing S_p.
proofSteps: Control sequence (3.2.1) of class-field-identification shows (X_∞)_{Γ^{p^m}} has bounded Z_p-rank and finite-index image in A_m; compact Nakayama (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L5) gives finite generation, and boundedness of ranks gives torsion (Sharifi Proposition 3.2.11).
Duality between inverse and direct limits (Sharifi Proposition 3.2.14, Corollary 3.2.15).
𝔛_S is finitely generated because its Γ-coinvariants are finitely generated over Z_p (Sharifi Theorem 3.3.3 proof).

For each p-adic completion k and its local tower k∞, local reciprocity identifies A∞ = lim_n (k_n^×)^∧_p with the abelianization of the kernel of the local pro-p Galois quotient onto Γ. Its Γ-coinvariants embed in (k^×)^∧_p, which is finitely generated over Z_p, because H_2(Γ,Z_p)=0. Compact Nakayama gives finite generation over Z_p[[Γ]]. The inverse-limit principal units are a submodule of A∞, so are finitely generated by noetherianity. Inducing from the finitely many open decomposition groups and taking their product proves finite generation of U∞ (NSW §11.2, pp. 731–735). This argument uses neither global unit injectivity nor strong Leopoldt.
acceptance: For K = Q, X_∞ = 0; for K = Q(μ_p) with p regular, X_∞ = 0.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.2.11, p. 80; Proposition 3.2.14 and Corollary 3.2.15, p. 82; Proposition 3.2.19, p. 83
sources.match: Proves that X_∞ is finitely generated and torsion, that A_∞^∨ is pseudo-isomorphic to X_∞^ι and has no nonzero finite submodule, and the analogues for X'_∞ and A'_∞.
Records that X_∞ and X'_∞ are finitely generated Λ-torsion and that X_S is finitely generated.

sources.locator: §11.2, pp. 731–735, opening reciprocity/Nakayama argument and principal-unit valuation sequences
sources.match: Supplies finite generation of local multiplicative norm limits; principal-unit limits are their submodules. The arithmetic semilocal induction is performed here.

nodes.title: Weak Leopoldt for the cyclotomic tower
nodes.statement: Let K∞/K be cyclotomic, Γ=Gal(K∞/K), Λ=Z_p[[Γ]], S⊇S_p∪S∞ finite, H_S=Gal(K_S/K∞), and D=Q_p/Z_p with trivial Galois action. The following equivalent conditions hold: the defects δ(K_n,p) are bounded; H_2(H_S,Z_p)=0; H²(H_S,D)=0; and 𝔛_S(K∞) is finitely generated over Λ, has rank r_2(K), and has no nonzero finite Λ-submodule. For μ_{2p}⊆K the sharper bound is δ(K_n,p)≤λ(X′_{S_p}(K∞)). Real places may ramify at p=2. H² is ordinary continuous cohomology of the discrete trivial module D, with restriction/inflation in the tower; its dual is compact homology with corestriction. Vanishing of this particular H² does not assert cd_2(H_S)≤2 when K has real places. Strong Leopoldt at the individual layers is not assumed.
hypotheses: K a number field, p any prime, S⊇S_p∪S∞ finite, K_S maximal extension unramified outside S.
Coefficients Z_p in compact homology and D with trivial action in discrete cohomology; real dyadic ramification is allowed.
proofSteps: The finite-layer Poitou–Tate/Kummer sequence identifies H_2(G_S(K_n),Z_p) with the kernel of completed global units into the augmented local product (NSW 10.3.13); it is Z_p-torsion-free by the global duality theorem used in NSW 8.7.7. The defect equals its Z_p-rank. This is a finite-layer statement, independent of any inverse-limit unit identification.

Use compact Nakayama to obtain finite generation of 𝔛_S from finite generation of the finite-layer abelian pro-p Galois group. The R02.4 Part II truncated ordinary Euler formula is χ₂(G_S)=−r₂ even for p=2 with real places; finite-layer H²(G_S,D) is divisible by the torsion-free compact homology statement. The PMIL L5 homological Λ criterion, NSW 5.6.17, identifies H₂(H_S,Z_p)=0 with rank r₂ and absence of finite submodules. Hochschild–Serre then identifies H₂(G_S(K_n),Z_p) with 𝔛_S^{Γ_n}; its ranks are bounded by the Z_p-rank of the maximal discrete Λ-submodule. The compact-support Euler theorem with the hypothesis p odd or no real places is not being applied to the real dyadic case.

Conversely, bounded defects make lim_n H_2(G_S(K_n),Z_p) a finitely generated Z_p-module. For odd p or totally imaginary K this limit is Λ-free by the homological freeness criterion NSW 5.6.15(ii), hence zero. When p=2 and K has real places, adjoin i. For the imaginary subgroup H′_S of index two the same H_2 is Λ-free. The group H²(H_S,D) is divisible, since the finite-layer H_2 groups are torsion-free; cor∘res=2 implies cor:H²(H′_S,D)→H²(H_S,D) is onto. Its dual injects H_2(H_S,Z_2) into the Λ-free imaginary group. A Λ-free module has no nonzero Λ-stable submodule finite over Z_2, so that limit is zero (NSW 10.3.22, pp. 639–640).

To establish boundedness in the cyclotomic case, descend from a finite base extension containing μ_{2p}. Over that tower K∞ contains μ_{p∞}. Global duality identifies the dual H_2 with the Tate–Shafarevich H² for μ_{p∞}. Poitou–Tate and Kummer identify this with colim_{n,m} Cl_S(K_n)/p^m, where the m-transition is multiplication by p; it is colim_n Cl_S(K_n)⊗D=0 because each class group is finite. Thus H_2=0 (NSW 10.3.25). No real cohomological-dimension bound enters.

The explicit δ_n≤λ(X′_{S_p}) bound follows instead by adjoining p-power roots of units whose local images are sufficiently p-divisible; the resulting extensions split above p and give quotients (Z/p^m)^{δ_n} of X′_{S_p}. The torsion module structure bounds their rank by λ (Sharifi 3.3.4).
acceptance: K totally real: 𝔛_S(K_∞) is Λ_K-torsion.
K imaginary quadratic: rank_Λ 𝔛_S(K_∞) = 1.

sources.match: States weak Leopoldt as boundedness of defects in a Z_p-extension, proves that it gives rank_Λ 𝔛_∞ = r_2(F), and proves it for the cyclotomic Z_p-extension with the bound δ_n ≤ λ(X'_∞) when μ_{2p} ⊆ F.
Cites Iwasawa for: for the cyclotomic Z_p-extension, X_S has no nontrivial finite Λ-submodule and Λ-rank r_2, so it is torsion iff F is totally real.
Proves the equivalent homological, defect and module formulations, including the adjoining-i restriction/corestriction argument at real dyadic places, and proves cyclotomic vanishing.

nodes.title: Minus class modules of CM towers and their duals
nodes.statement: Let K be a CM field, K^+ its maximal real subfield, j complex conjugation, and K_∞/K cyclotomic (a CM field with real subfield K^+_∞). For p odd, A_n^- is the −1-eigenspace of j on A_n = Cl(K_n) ⊗ Z_p, and A_∞^- = colim A_n^-, X_∞^- = lim A_n^-. For p=2 the negative eigenspace still exists but does not define an exact direct-summand functor; use the norm-kernel convention: A_n^- := ker(N_{K_n/K_n^+} : A(K_n) → A(K_n^+)), A_∞^- := colim_n A_n^-, with Pontryagin dual (A_∞^-)^∨ a compact Λ-module; the quotient convention M/(1 + j)M is a different functor and is compared with the norm kernel only up to explicit finite kernels and cokernels killed by 2. For p odd, the maps A_n^- → A_∞^- are injective and X_∞^- has no nonzero finite Λ-submodule; For p=2 and K∞=F∞(i) with F totally real (the tower used by Federer–Kolster), (A∞^-)^∨ is finitely generated torsion and has no nonzero finite Λ-submodule. At finite layers A_n^-⊆A_n^{j=−1} has cokernel ker(Cl(F_n)(2)→Cl(K_n)(2)), of order at most two. At the direct limit this cokernel vanishes. No no-finite-submodule claim for arbitrary dyadic CM towers lacking μ_4 is imported from Kolster.
hypotheses: K a CM field, p a prime, K_∞/K cyclotomic; for p = 2 the norm-kernel convention is fixed.
The dyadic no-finite-submodule conclusion is for K∞=F∞(i), F totally real; the norm-kernel construction itself is defined for every CM tower.
proofSteps: For p odd, multiplication by (1 − j)/2 is an idempotent projector on Z_p-modules, and the eigenspace decomposition commutes with norms and extension maps.
Injectivity of j_n^- and absence of finite submodules for p odd (Sharifi Propositions 3.4.1, 3.4.2).

For the dyadic conclusion use Kummer and Hochschild–Serre, with D trivial and J=Gal(K∞/F∞): if V=O_{K∞}^×⊗D, V is divisible and J acts trivially: a CM unit x has x/Jx a root of unity by Kronecker, and taking a square root in the 2-divisible roots of unity of K∞ makes x real modulo roots of unity, so H¹(J,V with sign action)=V/2V=0. Thus 0→V[2]→H¹(G_S(K∞),μ_{2∞})^{J=−1}→A∞^{J=−1}→0 is exact. Hochschild–Serre on D has kernel H¹(J,D)=Z/2 and zero obstruction H²(J,D)=0, hence dualizes to an injection of the dual of the middle term into 𝔛_S(F∞)(−1), with finite cokernel Z/2. The dual of A∞^{J=−1} is a submodule of this module, which is finitely generated torsion and has no finite Λ-submodule by weak Leopoldt.

At finite levels the wide Hilbert class field of F_n is totally real, hence disjoint from K_n; global class field theory makes the norm Cl(K_n)(2)→Cl(F_n)(2) surjective. As j∘N=1+J, its restriction to the negative eigenspace has kernel A_n^- and image ker j. The transfer kernel embeds in H¹(J,O_{K_n}^×). A norm-one CM unit is a root of unity, and (J−1)μ=μ², so this H¹ has order at most two. Taking direct limits gives a cokernel of order at most two between norm-minus and negative-eigen class modules. Its dual would be a finite submodule of (A∞^{J=−1})^∨, so it is zero. This proves the desired identification and no-finite-submodule theorem, with finite-layer errors accounted for.
acceptance: For K = Q(μ_p), p odd, X_∞^- is the minus part of the classical module of RJW and Sharifi §3.4.

sources.match: For a CM field and odd p, shows that A_n^- → A_∞^- is injective and that X_∞^- has no nonzero finite Λ-submodule.

nodes.title: Uniform bound for capitulation in a Z_p-tower
nodes.statement: For the cyclotomic Z_p-extension K∞/K of a number field there is a constant C such that #ker(Cl(K_n)(p)→Cl(K_m)(p))≤C for every n≤m≤∞. The same holds for S-class groups when S⊇S_p∪S∞ is fixed and finite. These are extension maps, including the map to the discrete direct limit; no injectivity of ordinary finite-layer class groups is asserted.
hypotheses: K∞/K the cyclotomic Z_p-extension; class groups are ordinary wide groups; S-version as stated.
proofSteps: Choose a layer n0 after all ramified primes are totally ramified. The class-field control description writes Cl(K_n)(p)=Xnr/ν_{n,n0}Y with Y a finite-index Λ-submodule of Xnr, and extension maps are multiplication by ν_{m,n}.

Pass from Y to its quotient by its maximal finite Λ-submodule. Once n1 is large enough, ν_{m,n} is injective on this quotient for all m≥n≥n1, by the elementary-module structure and disjointness of the relevant cyclotomic factors from its height-one support.

The remaining kernels come only from the fixed finite submodule and the fixed finite-index changes; their orders have a uniform bound. The finitely many lower layers add a fixed factor. Passing to the direct limit proves the m=∞ case. Apply the same argument to S-split class modules for the S-version (NSW 11.1.9).
acceptance: The bound is independent of both the starting and ending layers; a separate bound for each n would not imply the unit square-class rank estimate.

sources.match: Proves uniform bounds for ordinary and S-class capitulation kernels, including the infinite layer, using the finite submodule and the ν control maps.

uses.how: bounds 2-ranks of H¹(Γ_n,E) uniformly in n

nodes.title: Real unit square classes in the cyclotomic tower
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p=2, d=[F:Q], F∞/F cyclotomic, K∞=F∞(i), J=Gal(K∞/F∞), Γ=Gal(F∞/F), Λ=Z_2[[Γ]], and D=Q_2/Z_2. Define ℰ_R=colim_n O_{F_n}^×/{±1}, W_F=ℰ_R/2ℰ_R and C_F=W_F^∨ with the contragredient action. If V=O_{K∞}^×⊗D, the Kummer map x mod 2↦x⊗(1/2 mod Z_2) identifies W_F with V[2]. J acts trivially on V. The compact module C_F is finitely generated over F_2[[Γ]] with rank d. As a torsion Λ-module char_Λ(C_F)=(2^d); it may have finite Λ-submodules, so freeness is not asserted. For Γ_n=Gal(F∞/F_n), dim_F2 W_F^{Γ_n}=d·2^n+O(1).
hypotheses: F totally real, K∞=F∞(i) contains all 2-power roots of unity; units are ordinary units, not 2-units.
W_F is a discrete direct-limit quotient; C_F has its compact Pontryagin-dual topology.
proofSteps: For a CM unit x, x/Jx has every complex absolute value one, hence is a root of unity by Kronecker. Since μ(K∞) is 2-divisible, choose a root of unity ζ with ζ²=x/Jx; then x/ζ is real. Consequently O_{K∞}^×=μ(K∞)·O_{F∞}^× and the quotients by all roots of unity agree canonically with ℰ_R. Tensoring with D kills μ(K∞), and torsion-freeness gives V[2]≅ℰ_R/2ℰ_R. This is an equality at the infinite level; the finite Hasse unit-index errors must not be assumed zero at every layer.
For Γ_n, 0→μ_2→O_{F∞}^×→ℰ_R→0 shows ℰ_R^{Γ_n}/(O_{F_n}^×/{±1}) has order at most two. It is finitely generated torsion-free of rank d·2^n−1 by the unit theorem.

The invariant-principal-ideal argument in uniform-capitulation gives 0→B_n→H¹(Γ_n,O_{F∞}^×)→I∞^{Γ_n}/I_{F_n}, where #B_n is uniformly bounded and the last group has 2-rank at most s=#S_2(F∞), independently of n after a fixed initial layer. Thus H¹(Γ_n,ℰ_R)[2] has uniformly bounded F_2-dimension; removing μ_2 changes this bound by at most one.
Apply Γ_n-invariants to 0→ℰ_R→×2ℰ_R→W_F→0: 0→ℰ_R^{Γ_n}/2→W_F^{Γ_n}→H¹(Γ_n,ℰ_R)[2]→0. This proves dim W_F^{Γ_n}=d·2^n+O(1), in particular finite dimension for n=0.

Compact Nakayama gives finite generation of C_F over F_2[[Γ]]. The one-variable module structure theorem says dim(C_F)_{Γ_n}=rank(C_F)·2^n+O(1). Comparison gives rank d. Localizing over Λ at (2) turns C_F into a length-d module over its residue field, while every other height-one localization vanishes; hence char(C_F)=(2^d).
acceptance: A finite-layer sign group cannot replace this radical: the proof needs the uniform O(1) bound and all tower invariants.
The characteristic factor is determined by the F_2[[Γ]] rank; the construction does not assert an injection of the real sign module into the ramified Galois module.

sources.locator: Proposition 11.1.9, p. 730; §11.2, p. 731, compact Nakayama method
sources.match: The uniform capitulation bound and compact Nakayama support the new explicit square-class growth proof above; the rank conclusion is a derivation here, not a quotation of this source.
Supplies the ordinary-unit Kummer radical over the cyclotomic tower. The CM-unit and mod-two calculation above isolates its real correction term.
Uses real unit square classes; provides the finite-level cohomological check on the correction factor.

uses.how: C_F is the exact Kummer correction with characteristic factor 2^[F:Q]
supplies the height-one dyadic factor without an unsupported real-inertia freeness assertion

nodes.title: Galois cohomology of the real unit limit at p = 2
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p = 2, F_n^+ the layers of the cyclotomic Z_2-extension F_∞^+ = F_∞ of F (Kolster's tower), U^+_∞ = lim→ U(F_n^+) the direct limit of the unit groups and ℰ = U^+_∞/μ_2 its torsion-free quotient, Γ = Gal(F_∞/F). Then H¹(Γ, ℰ) ≅ B ⊕ (Q_2/Z_2)^r with B finite and H²(Γ, ℰ) ≅ (Q_2/Z_2)^{r−1} for some r with 1 ≤ r ≤ d, d the number of dyadic places of F_∞; consequently #H¹(Γ, μ_2 ⊗ ℰ) = 2^{s+r−1} with 2^s = #(B/2B) = #B[2], and μ_2 ⊗ ℰ_F has order 2^{[F:Q]−1}, ℰ_F being the free part of the unit group of F. These are the inputs of Kolster's Theorem 1 relating K_2(O_F)(2) to the minus class module.
hypotheses: F totally real, p = 2.
proofSteps: Let E=O_{F∞}^× and I∞ be the discrete group of fractional ideals obtained by extension. Hilbert 90 and 0→E→F∞^×→P∞→0 identify H¹(Γ,E)=P∞^Γ/P_F. Mapping to I∞^Γ/I_F has finite kernel ker(Cl(F)(2)→Cl(F∞)(2)), bounded by uniform-capitulation. After an eventual-total-ramification base layer, I∞^Γ/I_F is D^{s0}, with s0 the number of ramified primes, and its image in the class direct limit is the subgroup D∞ generated by the invariant ramified ideal products. Thus H¹(Γ,E) is cofinite with corank r=s0−corank(D∞). The finitely many initial ramification indices change only finite groups.

Yamashita §2, Lemma 3 and sequence (2), and §§3–4 compute H²(Γ,E). The local unit-idele H² direct limit is D^{s0}; the quotient idele/unit limit has corank corank(Cl(F∞)(2)^Γ)+1. Together with the D∞ term this gives corank H²=s0−corank(D∞)−1=r−1. Inflation sends a finite cyclic norm class x to x² in the next layer; this proves 2-divisibility, so H²(Γ,E)≅D^{r−1}. Hence r≥1 and r≤s0≤#S_2(F∞).

The exact sequence 0→μ_2→E→ℰ→0, and cd_2(Γ)=1 for finite 2-primary coefficients, give H²(Γ,ℰ)≅H²(Γ,E) and a finite quotient comparison in H¹. Therefore H¹(Γ,ℰ)≅B⊕D^r with B finite. This use of cd_2(Γ)=1 does not imply vanishing of H² with the torsion-free discrete coefficient ℰ.

From 0→ℰ→×2ℰ→ℰ/2ℰ→0, H¹(Γ,ℰ/2ℰ) is an extension of H¹(Γ,ℰ)/2 by H²(Γ,ℰ)[2]. Its order is #B/2B·2^{r−1}. The fixed real units have rank [F:Q]−1, giving #ℰ^Γ/2=2^{[F:Q]−1}. Fixed units modulo μ_2 can differ from finite-layer free units by a group of order at most two, which does not change their free rank; it is the rank, not a falsely asserted equality of these groups, that is used.
acceptance: Kolster 1989, proof of Theorem 1, p. 250.

sources.match: Quotes Iwasawa's description of H^i(Γ, ℰ) for the free part of the direct limit of real units and derives the order of H¹(Γ, μ_2 ⊗ ℰ) and the factor 2^{[F:Q]−1}.

sources.locator: §2, Lemma 3 and sequence (2), p. 77; §3, Lemmas 4, 5, 7, pp. 78–79; §4, Theorem and proof, p. 79
sources.match: Provides a direct original proof of the H² structure and divisibility. The H¹ corank is derived above from the invariant-ideal sequence; this replaces reliance on the unread Iwasawa 1983 original.

nodes.title: Equivariant L-values and Stickelberger elements
nodes.statement: Let k be a totally real field, H/k a finite abelian extension with G = Gal(H/k), and Σ, Σ' disjoint finite sets of places of k with Σ ⊇ S_∞. For a character χ : G → C^× let L(χ, s) = ∏_v (1 − χ(v)Nv^{−s})^{−1} be its primitive Hecke L-function (χ(v) = 0 when χ is ramified at v; meromorphic continuation from AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4), and L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ, s) = L(χ, s) ∏_{v ∈ Σ∖S_∞} (1 − χ(v)Nv^{−s}) ∏_{v ∈ Σ'} (1 − χ(v)Nv^{1−s}). The Stickelberger element Θ^{H/k}_{Σ,Σ'}(s) ∈ C[G] is the unique element with χ(Θ^{H/k}_{Σ,Σ'}(s)) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ^{-1}, s) for every χ ∈ Ĝ, that is Θ(s) = Σ_χ L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ^{-1}, s) e_χ with e_χ = (#G)^{-1} Σ_σ χ(σ)σ^{-1}. For an integer j ≥ 1, Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(1 − j) lies in Q[G] (Siegel–Klingen). Write Θ_Σ = Θ_{Σ,∅}, and θ_S := Θ_{S}(0) when S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram(H/k). Frobenius elements are arithmetic: Frob_v acts on residue fields by x ↦ x^{Nv}. This general analytic definition is the one that IntegralIwasawaTheory I.6 specialises to CM extensions at s = 0.
hypotheses: k totally real; H/k finite abelian (H need not be CM); Σ ⊇ S_∞ and Σ' finite, disjoint.
s ∈ C away from the poles of the L-functions; values at s = 1 − j, j ≥ 1, are finite.
proofSteps: Define Θ(s) through the idempotents e_χ ∈ C[G] (Tau Ceti CharacterTheory Layer 3); uniqueness because the χ separate C[G].
The continued L-functions and their Euler factors are imported from AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4.

Rationality at s = 1 − j: Gal(Q̄/Q)-equivariance of the values L(χ, 1 − j) (Siegel–Klingen, AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3/siegel-klingen-rationality) makes Θ(1 − j) fixed by the action on coefficients.
acceptance: For k = Q, H = Q(μ_m) and Σ = S_∞ ∪ {ℓ | m}: Θ_Σ(0) = Σ_{a ∈ (Z/m)^×} (1/2 − a/m) σ_a^{-1} with 0 < a < m, which equals ½N_G − θ_{Q(μ_m)} for Stickelberger's θ = m^{-1} Σ a σ_a^{-1}.

sources.match: Defines L(χ, s) with χ(𝔭) = 0 at ramified primes, the Σ-depleted Σ'-smoothed L-function and the Stickelberger element Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(s) by χ(Θ(s)) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ^{-1}, s), and records Siegel–Klingen–Shintani rationality of Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(0).
Defines θ_{M/k,S}(s) = Σ_ψ L_S(s, ψ^{-1}) ε_ψ with ε_ψ = (#G)^{-1}Σ ψ(σ)σ^{-1}, its rationality and the Sinnott–Kurihara module Θ(K/k).
Defines Stickelberger's element θ_F = m^{-1} Σ a σ_a^{-1} of Q(μ_m), the normalisation compared in the acceptance item.

nodes.title: Restriction, depletion and smoothing of Stickelberger elements
nodes.statement: With notation of stickelberger-elements: (a) for H ⊆ H' finite abelian over k and Σ ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram(H'/k), restriction π : C[Gal(H'/k)] → C[Gal(H/k)] sends Θ^{H'}_{Σ,Σ'}(s) to Θ^{H}_{Σ,Σ'}(s); (b) for v ∉ Σ ∪ Σ' unramified in H, Θ_{Σ ∪ {v},Σ'}(s) = (1 − Frob_v^{-1} Nv^{−s}) Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(s) and Θ_{Σ,Σ' ∪ {v}}(s) = (1 − Frob_v^{-1} Nv^{1−s}) Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(s); (c) for v ramified in H with inertia I_v and decomposition group G_v, adding v to Σ multiplies Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(s) by (1 − σ_v^{-1} e_v Nv^{−s}), e_v = (#I_v)^{-1} N I_v, σ_v ∈ G_v a Frobenius coset representative (independent of the choice); at s = 0 on Θ^# this is the factor (1 − σ_v e_v); (d) if H is CM with complex conjugation c, then cΘ_{Σ,Σ'}(0) = −Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(0) whenever #Σ ≥ 2 (that is, [k : Q] ≥ 2 or Σ contains a finite place); smoothing does not help: for k = Q, Σ = {∞} the trivial character contributes ζ(0)∏_{v∈Σ'}(1 − Nv) ≠ 0; (e) for S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_p ∪ S_ram(H_∞/k), the elements θ^{H_n/k}_S along the cyclotomic tower H_∞ = ⋃ H_n are compatible under restriction and define θ_{H∞/k,S} := lim_n θ^{H_n/k}_S ∈ Q(Λ_{H∞}) once the Deligne–Ribet integrality of smoothed-integrality is applied.
hypotheses: As in stickelberger-elements; in (e), S contains all places above p and all places ramified in H_∞/k.
proofSteps: (a): Artin formalism: a character of Gal(H/k) inflated to Gal(H'/k) has the same primitive L-function, and Σ contains every prime ramified in H' (AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4).
(b): compare Euler factors character by character; χ(Frob_v^{-1}) = χ^{-1}(Frob_v).
(c): χ(e_v) = 1 if χ is unramified at v and 0 otherwise, so χ(1 − σ_v^{-1} e_v Nv^{−s}) is the Euler factor 1 − χ^{-1}(v)Nv^{−s} of L(χ^{-1}, s) at v, or 1 when χ is ramified at v (DK (7) for Θ^#).

(d): L(χ, 0) = 0 for every totally even χ ≠ 1 (order of vanishing [k : Q] at 0), and ζ_{k,Σ}(0) = 0 exactly when #Σ ≥ 2; the smoothing factors 1 − Nv do not vanish, so Θ lies in the (1 − c)-part exactly under #Σ ≥ 2.
(e): apply (a) at each layer; the limit lies in Q(Λ_{H∞}) because a smoothed limit is integral (smoothed-integrality) and the smoothing factors are non-zerodivisors.
acceptance: Kurihara §3.1, p. 16: θ_{K∞/k,S} ∈ Z_p[[Gal(K_∞/k)]] after T-smoothing.

sources.match: Gives the ramified Euler-factor identity (7), the effect of the smoothing set on Θ_{S,T}, and that complex conjugation acts as −1 on Θ_{S,T}.
Uses the restriction-compatible Stickelberger elements of the layers K_n and their limit θ_{K∞/k,S} in Q(Λ_{K∞}).

nodes.title: Deligne–Ribet–Cassou-Noguès integrality
nodes.statement: Let H/k be finite abelian with k totally real, S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram(H/k), and T a finite set of finite places disjoint from S such that no nontrivial root of unity of H is ≡ 1 modulo every prime of H above T (condition (1) of Dasgupta–Kakde; it holds if T contains two primes of different residue characteristics or one prime of residue characteristic > [k : Q] + 1). Then (a) Θ_{S,T}(0) = ∏_{v ∈ T}(1 − Frob_v^{-1}Nv) θ_S lies in Z[G]; (b) Ann_{Z[G]}(μ(H)) θ_S ⊆ Z[G] (Kurihara (4)); (c) for H CM and any prime p, with disjoint Σ, Σ′ satisfying (A1)–(A5) of keystone-fitting-theorem, including Σ ≠ ∅, torsion-free O^×_{H,S∞,Σ′}, all p-ramified primes in Σ and all other ramified primes in Σ′, and t = #(S_∞ ∩ Σ′), the element of Z_p[G]^- characterised by χ(x) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ^{-1}, 0)/2^t for odd χ exists (DKSW, using Deligne–Ribet Corollary 8.9); (d) On the full cyclotomic tower K_∞ = H(μ_{p^∞}), with S also containing the primes above p, put G_∞ = Gal(K_∞/k), κ the full cyclotomic character, and J_κ the closed ideal generated by σ − κ(σ) for σ ∈ G_∞. Then J_κ·θ_{K∞/k,S} ⊆ Λ_{K∞}. The Serre pseudomeasure is g = τ(θ^#), where τ(σ) = κ(σ)^{-1}σ: I(G_∞)·g ⊆ Λ_{K∞}. In general I(G_∞) does not clear θ itself.
hypotheses: k totally real, H/k finite abelian, S, T as stated; for (c), H CM and p arbitrary (p = 2 included). In (c), all conditions (A1)–(A5), not merely coverage of ramification, are required; archimedean smoothing is interpreted by its character L-values.
For (d), use the full tower containing μ_{p^∞}, so κ descends to G_∞; S contains p. Passage to a smaller tower uses restriction of this identity, not a new augmentation-pseudomeasure assertion for θ.
proofSteps: (a)–(b) are the integrality theorem of Deligne–Ribet and Cassou-Noguès, imported from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3/deligne-ribet-measure ((0.4), (8.4)) applied to the measures on ray class groups; the smoothing factor clears exactly the denominators coming from μ(H).

(c): the 2-adic refinement (8.11) of Deligne–Ribet gives integrality of odd measures up to 2^{[k:Q]−1}; Kurihara's argument in DK Lemma 3.4 passes to depleted and smoothed elements (DKSW-BSZ §1.2, after Theorem 1.2).

(d): import the Deligne–Ribet Serre pseudomeasure g with I(G_∞)g ⊆ Λ. Kurihara §4.1, equation (11), p. 23, gives g = τ(θ^#). The automorphisms τ and # preserve Λ and send the clearing factor σ−1, under #τ^{-1}, to κ(σ)σ^{-1}−1 = −σ^{-1}(σ−κ(σ)). Hence the clearing ideal for θ is J_κ. This distinguishes the Stickelberger and Serre normalizations.
acceptance: T = {2} for H = Q(μ_3) violates condition (1) (−1 ≡ 1 mod 2), and Θ_{S,{2}}(0) = (1 − 2c)(1 − c)/6 = (1 − c)/2 ∉ Z[G].

nodes.title: The Deligne–Ribet pseudomeasure in Iwasawa normalisation
nodes.statement: Let k be totally real, F/k finite abelian totally real, K_∞ = F_∞(μ_{2p}) = F(μ_{p^∞}), S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_p ∪ S_ram(F/k), and κ : Gal(K_∞/k) → Z_p^× the cyclotomic character. Transport the Deligne–Ribet pseudo-measure of AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 along the Artin map Cl^+_k(𝔣p^∞) → Gal(K_∞/k) (arithmetic Frobenius convention) to g_{K∞/k,S} ∈ Q(Λ_{K∞}). Then: (i) κ^n ψ(g_{K∞/k,S}) = L_S(1 − n, ψ) for every n ≥ 1 and every finite-order character ψ of Gal(K_∞/k); (ii) g_{K∞/k,S} is a pseudo-measure, and lies in Λ_{K∞} unless the trivial-character pole intervenes; (iii) it is unique with property (i); (iv) for v ∉ S, v ∤ p, g_{K∞/k,S∪{v}} = (1 − Nv^{-1}Frob_v) g_{K∞/k,S}; (v) restriction to Gal(F'_∞(μ_{2p})/k) for k ⊆ F' ⊆ F sends g_{K∞/k,S} to g_{K'∞/k,S}, and g_{F∞/k,S} is the image of g_{K∞/k,S} in Q(Λ_{F∞}), the even part; (vi) in the coordinate of iwasawa-algebra-coordinate, for an even character ψ of Gal(F/k) of type S (F_ψ ∩ k_∞ = k), the ψ-component of g_{F∞/k,S} is G_{ψ,S}(T)/H_ψ(T) with G_{ψ,S}(u^n − 1) = L_S(1 − n, ψω^{−n})·H_ψ(u^n − 1) and H_ψ(T) = ψ(γ)(1 + T) − 1 for ψ of type W, 1 otherwise; (vii) no abelian-over-Q hypothesis is imposed on k. The relation to the Stickelberger normalization is τ(θ^#)=g with τ(σ)=κ(σ)^{-1}σ; the augmentation clearing condition belongs to g, and transports to J_κθ⊆Λ as in smoothed-integrality.
hypotheses: k totally real, F/k finite abelian totally real, p any prime (p = 2 included), S as stated.
proofSteps: Transport AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3/deligne-ribet-pseudomeasure along the reciprocity isomorphism of Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 11, with arithmetic Frobenius.
(i): the moment formula ∫ε N^k dλ = L(1 − k, ε) with κ(Frob_v) = Nv for v ∤ p.
(iii): pseudo-measures are separated by their values κ^nψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L3 separation; interpolation-uniqueness).
(iv): compare the Euler factor (1 − ψ(v)Nv^{n−1}) with κ^nψ(1 − Nv^{-1}Frob_v).
(vi): write κ = ω⟨κ⟩ on Gal(K_∞/k) ≅ Δ × Γ and evaluate in the T-coordinate (Kolster Lecture 1, p. 8).
acceptance: Kurihara §4.1, p. 23: κ^nψ(g_{K∞/k,S}) = L_S(1 − n, ψ) for all n ≥ 1.
Kolster p. 8: L^S_p(1 − s, ψ) = G_{ψ,S}(κ(γ)^s − 1)/H_ψ(κ(γ)^s − 1).

sources.match: Defines g_{K∞/k,S} as the pseudo-measure with κ^nψ(g) = L_S(1 − n, ψ), its image g_{F∞/k,S}, and the relation τ(θ^#_{K∞/k,S}) = g_{K∞/k,S} of equation (11).

States the Deligne–Ribet interpolation L_p(1 − n, ψ) = L(1 − n, ψω^{−n})∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − ψω^{−n}(𝔭)N𝔭^{n−1}), the S-imprimitive version, and the power series G_{ψ,S}/H_ψ with H_ψ = ψ(γ)(1 + T) − 1 for type W.
Recalls Deligne–Ribet, Cassou-Noguès and Barsky: G_ψ(u^n − 1) = L_Σ(ψ, 1 − n) for nontrivial ψ and the pole for the trivial character, and Serre's pseudo-measure ζ ∈ Q(Λ(G)).

nodes.title: Kubota–Leopoldt, Bernoulli distributions and Stickelberger elements over Q
nodes.statement: For k = Q, m ≥ 1 prime to p, F_n = Q(μ_{mp^n}) and G_∞ = Gal(F_∞/Q) ≅ Z_{p,m}^× = (Z/m)^× × Z_p^× (a ↦ σ_a): (i) the limit Θ^{(1)}_∞ = (Θ^{(1)}_n)_n of the Bernoulli–Stickelberger elements Θ^{(1)}_n = Σ_{a mod mp^n, (a,mp)=1} E^{(1)}_n(a) σ_a^{-1} (E^{(1)}_n(a) = a/(mp^n) − 1/2) lies in Q_p[Δ][[T]], and (1 − c σ_c^{-1})Θ^{(1)}_∞ is integral for c ∈ Z_{p,m}^× (Sharifi Remark 5.3.7); (ii) for a primitive even Dirichlet character χ of conductor m or mq (of the first kind) the Iwasawa power series f_χ = −ω̃χ^{-1}(Θ^{(1)}_∞) satisfies f_χ(ξu^s − 1) = L_p(χρ, s) for χ ≠ 1, and f_1 = (1 − u(1 + T)^{-1})·F_1 with F_1 the Kubota–Leopoldt zeta function (pole at the trivial character), with ½f_χ ∈ Λ_χ; (iii) this agrees with the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure of DirichletPadicLFunctions L1–L2, with the Euler factor at p, L_p(χ, 1 − n) = −(1 − χω^{−n}(p)p^{n−1})B_{n,χω^{−n}}/n, and with g_{F∞/Q,S} of deligne-ribet-dictionary after the identification σ_a ↔ a; (iv) no second p-adic zeta carrier is constructed.
hypotheses: k = Q, p any prime, m prime to p, q = p or 4.
proofSteps: (i)–(ii): Sharifi Definition 5.3.5, Remark 5.3.10, Lemma 5.3.11, Proposition 5.3.12 and Theorem 5.3.13.

(iii): DirichletPadicLFunctions L1/arithmetic-pseudomeasure and L2 give the measure and its interpolation; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3/deligne-ribet-rational-comparison identifies it with Deligne–Ribet for k = Q.
acceptance: For p odd and even k ≢ 0 mod p − 1: L_p(1 − j, ω^k) = −(1 − p^{j−1})B_j/j when j ≡ k mod p − 1 (Sharifi Corollary 5.3.16).

sources.locator: §5.3, Proposition 5.3.3 to Theorem 5.3.13, pp. 138–142; Corollaries 5.3.15–5.3.16, p. 142
sources.match: Constructs the higher Stickelberger elements Θ^{(k)}_n, identifies the Iwasawa power series f_χ with the Kubota–Leopoldt function including the pole factor for χ = 1, and proves ½f_χ integral.
Normalises f_k = −Θ^{(k)}_∞ with f_k(υ^s − 1) = L_p(ω^k, s) for the main conjecture over Q.

nodes.title: Uniqueness and poles of interpolating pseudo-measures
nodes.statement: Let G be an abelian profinite group with an open subgroup isomorphic to Z_p and κ : G → Z_p^× a character with open image. (a) A pseudo-measure x ∈ Q(Z_p[[G]]) is determined by the values κ^nψ(x) for ψ ranging over finite-order characters and n over any infinite set of positive integers. (b) If x is a pseudo-measure then (g − 1)x ∈ Z_p[[G]] for every g ∈ G; x ∈ Z_p[[G]] iff its value at the trivial character is finite, i.e. iff the augmentation-pole vanishes. (c) An assignment of values to the κ^nψ does not by itself define an element: existence (Deligne–Ribet), uniqueness ((a)) and pole behaviour ((b)) are separate statements, and only their conjunction is used in I.5, I.8 and I.9.
hypotheses: G abelian profinite, Γ ⊆ G open with Γ ≅ Z_p; κ continuous with open image.
proofSteps: (a): reduce to measures by multiplying with a regular clearing factor 1 − c (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L3 independence of the clearing factor) and use separation of measures by positive moments twisted by finite characters (L3 positive-moment and character separation).
(b): the defining property of Serre's pseudo-measures (Kurihara §4.1) and the augmentation ideal generated by the g − 1.
acceptance: For G = Z_p^×, the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure is not a measure, while (1 − σ_c)·ζ_p is (DirichletPadicLFunctions L1/arithmetic-not-integral).

sources.match: Uses Serre's pseudo-measures, the submodule of Q(Λ_{K∞}) of x with x·I_{Gal(K∞/k)} ⊆ Λ_{K∞}, characterised by the interpolation property.
Proves uniqueness of the interpolating element and records the pole factor h_{1,u} = u(T + 1)^{-1} − 1 for the trivial character.

nodes.title: Arithmetic Iwasawa complexes of Tate twists
nodes.statement: Let k be totally real or arbitrary, F/k finite abelian, F_∞ the cyclotomic Z_p-extension of F, G = Gal(F_∞/k), Λ = Λ_{F∞} (equivariant-iwasawa-algebra), S ⊇ S_p ∪ S_∞ ∪ S_ram(F/k) finite, and T a finite free Z_p-module with a continuous G_{k,S}-action (in this roadmap T = Z_p(r), r ∈ Z, possibly twisted by a finite-order character). Define C^Iw_S(F_∞, T) := RΓ_Iw(O_{F∞,S}, T) = R lim_n RΓ(O_{F_n,S}, T) (corestriction transitions), the instance of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3 for this tower, and its compactly supported variant C^Iw_{c,S}(F_∞, T) := R lim_n RΓ_c(O_{F_n,S}, T) built from ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7. For p odd (or F totally imaginary) both are perfect complexes of Λ-modules with Λ-linear Galois action; for T = Z_p(1) the compactly supported cohomology vanishes outside degrees 2 and 3. Their cohomology for T = Z_p(1) is: H^1_Iw = E_{∞,S} (Kummer), 0 → X'_S(F_∞) → H^2_Iw → ker(⊕_{w ∈ S_f(F∞)} Z_p → Z_p) → 0, and H^2_c = 𝔛_S(F_∞), H^3_c = Z_p (Poitou–Tate). At p = 2 with real places the perfect model is the Burns–Flach complex of IntegralIwasawaTheory I.8, and every statement of I.4 is applied to it.
hypotheses: p a prime; S ⊇ S_p ∪ S_∞ ∪ S_ram(F/k) finite; T finite free over Z_p with continuous G_{k,S}-action.
Perfectness is asserted for p odd or F totally imaginary; for p = 2 with real places the I.8 model replaces it.
proofSteps: Instantiate SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3/iwasawa-cohomology and L3/infinite-selmer-complex with the tower F_n, using Shapiro's lemma to identify RΓ_Iw with RΓ(O_{k,S}, Λ ⊗ T^ι) (L3/iwasawa-shapiro).
Compact support: ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7/compact-support-cochains and derived Poitou–Tate duality D7/derived-global-duality.
Kummer sequence for μ_{p^m} on O_{F_n,S} and the limit over m, n (Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9; Sharifi Proposition 3.3.9).
acceptance: For F = k = Q, p odd and T = Z_p(1): H^1_Iw = lim_n (O_{Q_n}[1/p]^× ⊗ Z_p) along the layers Q_n of the cyclotomic Z_p-extension, and H^2_c = 𝔛_{{p,∞}}(Q_∞).

sources.match: Uses the inverse limit of RΓ_c(O_{F_n,S}, Z_p(1)) along the cyclotomic tower, a perfect complex of Λ_{F∞}-modules with H² = X_{F∞,S} and H³ = Z_p, valid at p = 2 in the Burns–Flach model.
Relates H¹(G_{F∞,S}, μ_{p^∞}) to S-units and class groups by Kummer theory and dualises it to the S-ramified Iwasawa module.

nodes.title: Descent to finite layers and the Tor spectral sequence
nodes.statement: For C = C^Iw_S(F_∞, T) (or its compactly supported variant, or the I.8 complex) and n ≥ 0: (a) C ⊗^L_{Λ} Z_p[Gal(F_n/k)] ≅ RΓ(O_{F_n,S}, T) (resp. RΓ_c), compatibly with restriction maps; (b) there is a convergent spectral sequence E_2^{i,j} = Tor^{Λ}_{−i}(H^j(C), Z_p[Gal(F_n/k)]) ⇒ H^{i+j}(O_{F_n,S}, T); (c) for G = Γ (F = k) this degenerates into exact sequences 0 → H^j(C)_{Γ_n} → H^j(O_{k_n,S}, T) → H^{j+1}(C)^{Γ_n} → 0 with Γ_n = Γ^{p^n}; (d) the kernels and cokernels of H^j(C)_{Γ_n} → H^j_n are given by these Tor terms and are never discarded before a finite-level statement is made; (e) for T = Z_p(1) and j = 2 compact support, (𝔛_S)_{Γ_n} → 𝔛_S(F_n) is injective with cokernel (H³_c)^{Γ_n} = Z_p, identified with Γ_n = Gal(F_∞/F_n) (Sharifi, proof of Theorem 3.3.3: 0 → (𝔛_∞)_{Γ_n} → 𝔛_n → Γ_n → 0).
hypotheses: As in arithmetic-iwasawa-complex.
proofSteps: (a): derived control for Iwasawa cohomology (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3/derived-control) with Shapiro's lemma.
(b): the Künneth/Tor spectral sequence for a perfect complex tensored with a module.
(c): Z_p[Γ/Γ_n] = Λ/(ω_n) has a length-one free resolution by multiplication by the non-zerodivisor ω_n (finite-level-kernel).
(e): Sharifi's computation in the proof of Theorem 3.3.3.
acceptance: For M = H^j(C) torsion with M^{Γ_n} finite, #H^j_n is computed from #M_{Γ_n} and #H^{j+1}(C)^{Γ_n}.

sources.match: Uses the exact sequence 0 → (𝔛_∞)_{Γ_n} → 𝔛_n → Γ_n → 0 to compute Z_p-ranks of coinvariants.
Descends the Iwasawa complex and Selmer modules from K_∞ to finite layers, keeping the finite kernels and cokernels.
Galois descent H¹(o'_{E∞}, Q_p/Z_p(n))^Γ = H¹(o'_E, Q_p/Z_p(n)) used to compare coinvariants of X with finite-level cohomology.

nodes.title: Euler characteristics at arithmetic characters
nodes.statement: Let O be a finite extension of Z_p, Λ_O = O[[T]] = O[[Γ]], and M a finitely generated torsion Λ_O-module with characteristic power series f = ϖ^μ f*. For an arithmetic point ρ_n,ψ = κ^nψ : Λ → O_ψ, the specialisation is computed through Γ-(co)invariants of the twist M(−n)_ψ: (a) M_Γ is finite iff M^Γ is finite iff f(0) ≠ 0, and then #M_Γ/#M^Γ = #(O/f(0)O); (b) if moreover M has no nonzero finite Λ_O-submodule then M^Γ = 0 and #M_Γ = #(O/f(0)O); (c) for the twist, char(M(−n)) is f(κ(γ)^n(1 + T) − 1) in the contragredient convention, so #M(−n)_Γ = #(O/f(u^n − 1)O) when f(u^n − 1) ≠ 0 and M has no nonzero finite submodule; Kolster's covariant convention (γφ)(x) = φ(γx) evaluates instead at u^{-n} − 1, and the two are compared by the involution ι; (d) at a trivial zero (f(u^n − 1) = 0, for instance M = Z_p and n = 0) the specialisation is not a finite Euler characteristic, and the statement passes to a leading term; away from it the augmentation factor is explicit: for M = Z_p (characteristic series T) and n ≠ 0, #Z_p(−n)_Γ = |u^n − 1|_p^{-1}, which equals #H⁰(F, Q_p/Z_p(n)) when κ^n factors through Γ = Gal(F_∞/F) (for instance μ_q ⊆ F), the trivial-character correction.
hypotheses: M finitely generated torsion over O[[T]]; n ∈ Z; ψ a finite-order character of the finite part.
proofSteps: (a): import the Euler quotient χ_n(M) of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4 (#M_{Γ_n}/#M^{Γ_n} via the resultant) at n = 0; it is Kolster Lemma 1.1.
(b): M^Γ is a finite submodule.
(c): Kolster Lemma 1.2 for the twist and iwasawa-algebra-coordinate for the two conventions.
(d): Z_p(n) as a Λ-module has characteristic series T − (u^n − 1) (iwasawa-algebra-coordinate test charIdeal_tate_twist).
acceptance: Kolster Proposition 3.2: #H²(o'_E, Z_p(n))_{χ^{-1}} = #X_ψ(−n)_Γ = |f(κ(γ)^n − 1)|_v^{-1} for ψ ≠ 1.
Kolster p. 14: #X(−n)_Γ^{-1} = κ(γ)^n − 1 for X = Z_p.

sources.locator: Lecture 1, Lemma 1.1, p. 6, and Lemma 1.2, p. 7
sources.match: For a finitely generated torsion Λ-module: M^Γ finite ⇔ M_Γ finite ⇔ f(0) ≠ 0, with |M^Γ|/|M_Γ| = |f(0)|_v; the characteristic polynomial of M(n) is f*(κ(γ)^{−n}(1 + T) − 1).
Uses absence of finite submodules to get M^Γ = 0 and computes the order of the twisted coinvariants, with the separate trivial-character computation κ(γ)^n − 1.

sources.match: At p = 2 and even n uses the same coinvariant computation, with X(−n)^Γ = 0 because X has no finite submodule.

nodes.title: Twisted coinvariants of the S-ramified module and étale cohomology
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p a prime, E/F finite abelian with E ⊇ μ_{2p} (so μ_{p^∞} ⊆ E_∞), S ⊇ S_p ∪ S_∞, X = 𝔛_S(E_∞), and n ∈ Z, n ≠ 0, with Γ = Gal(E_∞/E). Then: (a) Hom(X, Q_p/Z_p(n)) = H¹(G_S(E_∞), Q_p/Z_p(n)) as Λ-modules, Galois acting trivially on Q_p/Z_p(n) over E_∞; (b) Hochschild–Serre gives H¹(G_S(E), Q_p/Z_p(n)) ≅ H¹(G_S(E_∞), Q_p/Z_p(n))^Γ for n ≠ 0 (for p = 2 using that H^i(Γ, Q_2/Z_2(n)) vanish for i = 1, 2); hence the Pontryagin dual of X(−n)_Γ is H¹(O_E^S, Q_p/Z_p(n)); (c) assume p odd, n ≥ 2 and p ∤ [E:F]; on an eigenspace where H¹(O_E^S, Q_p/Z_p(n)) is finite (odd χ for odd n, even χ for even n, with χ = ψω^{−n}), its quotient by its maximal divisible subgroup identifies with H²(O_E^S, Z_p(n))_{χ^{-1},tors}; under the stated finiteness this is the whole group; so #H²(O_E^S, Z_p(n))_{χ^{-1}} = #X_ψ(−n)_Γ; (d) for F itself and p = 2, n even ≥ 2: #X(F)(−n)_Γ = #H²_et(O_F[1/2], Z_2(n)), where X(F) is the S-ramified module allowing ramification at the real places.
hypotheses: F totally real, E/F finite abelian with μ_{2p} ⊆ E, S ⊇ S_p ∪ S_∞ finite, n ≠ 0; in (c) the parity condition χ(−1) = (−1)^n. In (c), p odd, n ≥ 2, p ∤ [E:F], so the integral character idempotents exist.
proofSteps: (a): Q_p/Z_p(n) is a trivial G_S(E_∞)-module; H¹ of a profinite group with trivial divisible coefficients is Hom of its abelianisation, whose pro-p part is X.
(b): inflation–restriction / Hochschild–Serre for Γ ≅ Z_p of cohomological dimension 1 (Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 5).
(c): the torsion-of-H² identification H¹(Q_p/Z_p(n))/div ≅ H²(Z_p(n))_tors, and finiteness on the eigenspaces of the right parity (Kolster Corollary 2.2).
(d): Rognes–Weibel Appendix A, proof of Theorem A.1.

nodes.title: Local Euler factors under enlarging S
nodes.statement: Let F/k be finite abelian totally real, F_∞ cyclotomic, S′ = S ∪ {v} with S ⊇ S_p ∪ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, and v ∉ S (so v ∤ p, v unramified in F). Then: (a) there is an exact sequence of Λ_{F∞}-modules 0 → ⊕_{w | v} (inertia at w in 𝔛_{S'}) → 𝔛_{S'}(F_∞) → 𝔛_S(F_∞) → 0, where the inertia term is Λ_{F∞} ⊗_{Z_p[[D_v]]} lim_m μ_{p^∞}(k(w_m)) ≅ Λ_{F∞}/(Frob_v − Nv), with D_v ⊆ Gal(F_∞/k) the decomposition group of v (topologically generated by Frob_v) and k(w_m) the residue fields of F_m above v under norms; (b) its characteristic ideal (over each component) is generated by 1 − Nv^{-1}Frob_v, so Det(C_{S'})^{-1} = (1 − Nv^{-1}Frob_v)·Det(C_S)^{-1}, matching g_{S'} = (1 − Nv^{-1}Frob_v)g_S of IntegralIwasawaTheory I.3; (c) at a finite layer the corresponding factor is the Euler factor 1 − ψ(v)⟨Nv⟩^n/Nv at κ^nψ on a totally real procyclic tower; it equals 1 − ψ_0(v)Nv^{n−1} when ψ = ψ_0ω^n on Frobenius, which may vanish p-adically but never identically on Λ; (d) the identities hold integrally, so the finite S-local factor is kept in every finite-level formula (and in Kolster's imprimitive L^S_p).
hypotheses: v ∉ S, v ∤ p, v unramified in F/k; D_v ⊆ G the decomposition group, open by tower-ramification.
proofSteps: At each finite layer use the augmented ordinary-unit class-field sequence for S and S′. The two rows have the same global units and wide class groups; the extra local factor is the p-completion of the residue-unit group at v. Pass to compact norm limits, keeping the real sign factors in both rows. Weak Leopoldt identifies the global unit limits with their images already in the S-local product. An element of the new local factor lying in the diagonal image of E∞ would therefore have zero image in the old S-local product and must vanish. The snake lemma gives 0→U_{v,∞}→𝔛_{S′}→𝔛_S→0. This proves injectivity, rather than assuming tame inertia has no global-unit relation.

The inverse limit of the local p-primary roots of unity is the cyclic D_v-module with relation Frob_v − Nv; induction gives the displayed Λ-quotient. A unit relation gives the zero module. At p = 2 the criterion is absence of μ_2, not absence of μ_4. Since Nv is a p-adic unit, Frob_v − Nv and 1 − Nv^{-1}Frob_v generate the same ideal.
On the cyclotomic Z_p-quotient κ(Frob_v) = ⟨Nv⟩, so evaluate at κ^nψ with the Teichmüller adjustment displayed in (c). The full cyclotomic character need not factor through this quotient.
acceptance: For k = F = Q and v = ℓ ≠ p: char(𝔛_{{p,ℓ,∞}})/char(𝔛_{{p,∞}}) = (1 − ℓ^{-1}σ_ℓ).

nodes.title: Real-place corrections at p = 2
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, d=[F:Q], p=2, S=S_2∪S∞, K∞=F∞(i), J=Gal(K∞/F∞), D=Q_2/Z_2 and Λ=Z_2[[Γ]]. Let X=𝔛_S(F∞) allow real ramification, A^- be the ordinary norm-minus class direct limit of K∞, H=H¹(G_S(K∞),μ_{2∞}), Y=(H^{J=−1})^∨, and C_F the real-unit square-class dual of I.2/real-unit-radical. There are canonical exact sequences 0→(A^-)^∨→Y→C_F→0 and 0→Y→X(−1)→Z/2(−1)→0, with the contragredient dual convention. Consequently char_Λ(X(−1))=(2^d)·char_Λ((A^-)^∨). These sequences, including the finite descent cokernel, supply the dyadic correction; they do not identify the module split at infinity with the norm-minus class dual. Conditionally on the trivial-character 2-adic main conjecture, for every even n≥2 one also has ζ_F(1−n)∼_2 #H²_et(O_F[1/2],Z_2(n))/#H¹_et(O_F[1/2],Z_2(n)), where #H¹=w_n(F)_2. Finite real local cohomology groups and the tower module (Λ/2)^d are different objects.
hypotheses: F totally real, p=2; ordinary wide classes, S=S_2∪S∞, K∞=F∞(i).
All duals in the exact sequences are continuous Pontryagin duals with the contragredient action; the even-weight zeta consequence is conditional on the stated main conjecture.
proofSteps: Apply the ordinary-unit Kummer sequence 0→V→H→A∞→0, V=O_{K∞}^×⊗D. The CM-unit argument of real-unit-radical gives trivial J-action on V and V[2]≅W_F. Taking J=−1 is exact at A∞: after the sign twist its obstruction is H¹(J,V with sign)=V/2V=0. Thus 0→W_F→H^{J=−1}→A∞^{J=−1}→0 is exact. The norm-minus/negative-eigen comparison of cm-minus-class-modules identifies its last term with A^- at the direct limit, retaining the order-at-most-two transfer kernels before that passage.

Dualize this exact sequence to obtain 0→(A^-)^∨→Y→C_F→0. With trivial D, inflation–restriction for G_S(K∞)⊂G_S(F∞) has kernel H¹(J,D)=D[2]≅Z/2 and obstruction H²(J,D)=D/2D=0. Twist its dual by −1 to obtain the second exact sequence. This is also the comparison underlying Kurihara Lemma 4.2(1), pp. 25–26.

The new real-unit-radical target proves finite generation of C_F over F_2[[Γ]] and rank d by uniform capitulation, the unit theorem and dim W_F^{Γ_n}=d·2^n+O(1). Characteristic ideals multiply in the first sequence. The second sequence has finite cokernel, of characteristic ideal one, giving the asserted factor 2^d. This proof supplies the rank and the maps instead of inferring them from a quotient of sign modules.

For the conditional even-weight consequence apply twisted-coinvariant-descent and coinvariant-euler-characteristic to the assumed main conjecture. Its pole correction evaluated at κ(γ)^n−1 has order w_n(F)_2; the finite-prime factors at 2 are units. The local C_2 cohomology at infinity is computed with the actual parity: for trivial Z_2(n), positive even degrees give Z/2 and odd degrees give zero; for the sign action these roles interchange. Modified compact support retains these local terms (Rognes–Weibel Theorem A.1, pp. 45–47).
acceptance: F = Q: ζ(−1) = −1/12 ∼_2 #H²_et(Z[1/2], Z_2(2))/#H¹_et(Z[1/2], Z_2(2)) with #H¹ = w_2(Q)_2 = 8; this is the 2-part of the Birch–Tate formula for Q (K_2(Z) = Z/2).

nodes.title: The classical main conjecture for a totally real field
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p a prime, S ⊇ S_p ∪ S_∞ finite, and ψ an even one-dimensional p-adic Artin character of F of type S (F_ψ ∩ F_∞ = F). Let N = F_ψ, X_S(N) = 𝔛_S(N_∞) (I.2, ramification at real places allowed when p = 2), O_ψ = Z_p[ψ], X_S(N)_ψ = {x ∈ X_S(N) ⊗ O_ψ : δx = ψ(δ)x for δ ∈ Gal(N/F)}, g_{ψ,S} = ϖ^{μ(g)} g*_{ψ,S} its characteristic series (g* the characteristic polynomial of γ − 1 on X_S(N)_ψ ⊗ Q̄_p), and G_{ψ,S} = ϖ^{μ(G)} G*_{ψ,S}·u the Deligne–Ribet power series of IntegralIwasawaTheory I.3 (deligne-ribet-dictionary (vi)). MainConjecture(F, p, ψ, S) is the proposition g*_{ψ,S} = G*_{ψ,S}; the strong form adds μ(g) = μ(G), that is char(X_S(N)_ψ) = (G_{ψ,S}). Over Q for odd p, ψ = ω^k with k even and k ≢ 0 mod p−1, the strong form is equivalent to char(X_∞^{(ω^{1−k})}) = (f_k) for the unramified minus eigenspace, and to char(E_∞^{(k)}/C_∞^{(k)}) = char(X_∞^{(k)}) for units modulo cyclotomic units. Passing from the weak statement to these characteristic-ideal equalities uses the separately imported arithmetic and analytic Ferrero–Washington μ = 0 theorems. The exceptional branch k ≡ 0 has a pole and is treated separately.
hypotheses: F totally real; p prime; S ⊇ S_p ∪ S_∞; ψ even of type S, one-dimensional, finite order.
proofSteps: X_S(N)_ψ is finitely generated torsion over O_ψ[[T]] by weak-leopoldt (N totally real).

g* is unchanged when N is replaced by any finite abelian E ⊇ F_ψ with E ∩ F_∞ = F (Kolster p. 9, citing Greenberg); enlarging S multiplies both sides by the same local factors (I.4/s-enlargement-euler-factors).

Over Q: the equivalences of the three versions use I.2/global-local-unit-sequence, Kummer duality, and Iwasawa's isomorphism U_∞^{(k)}/C_∞^{(k)} ≅ Λ/(g_k) through Coleman power series (ColemanPowerSeries L4). The weak-to-strong passage additionally imports Ferrero–Washington; it is not a formal equivalence of distinguished polynomials and full ideals.
acceptance: Rognes–Weibel Appendix A, p. 46: G*_ψ(T) = g*_ψ(T) is Greenberg's formulation.
Sharifi AWS Theorems 2.5.1, 2.5.4, 2.5.7: the three equivalent versions over Q.
