nodes.title: Ordinary Hecke algebras and the Eisenstein ideal
nodes.statement: Over Q (tame level 1, p ≥ 5, k even with k ≢ 0 mod p − 1): let 𝔐 = 𝔐(1, Λ)^ord ⊇ 𝔖 = 𝔖(1, Λ)^ord be Hida's ordinary Λ-adic modular and cusp forms, ℌ and 𝔥 their Hecke algebras (inverse diamond operators), ℰ_θ the Λ-adic Eisenstein series of character θ = ω^{k−2} with constant term ½ the Kubota–Leopoldt power series. The Eisenstein ideal I_k ⊆ 𝔥 is generated by U_p − 1, T_ℓ − 1 − ℓ⟨ℓ⟩ (ℓ ≠ p) and ⟨j⟩ − ω^{k−2}(j) (j ∈ μ_{p−1}); 𝔪_k = I_k + (p, ⟨υ⟩ − 1) and 𝔥_k = 𝔥_{𝔪_k}. Then 𝔥_k ≠ 0 iff p divides B_{2,ω^{k−2}}, and (Mazur–Wiles) 𝔥_k/I ≅ Λ/(ξ_k) with ξ_k(v^s − 1) = L_p(ω^k, s − 1); the congruence module of 0 → 𝔖 → 𝔐 → Λ → 0 (nearly split by ℰ) is Λ/(ξ_k). This target is the Q construction. The all-prime totally real proof uses I.7 and I.9 instead; its Hilbert forms are imported there from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions, rather than supplied by this construction. More precisely, if c:𝔐→Λ is the normalized (involuted) constant-term map and Q(Λ)ℰ is the Eisenstein line, its congruence module is Λ/c(𝔐∩Q(Λ)ℰ). The first nonconstant coefficient of ℰ is one, so 𝔐∩Q(Λ)ℰ=Λℰ and c has image (ξ_k/2) on this lattice. This is Λ/(ξ_k), with the equivalent rational-splitting definition s(Λ)/(s(Λ)∩𝔐); it is not a formula for an arbitrary augmented finite-flat module.
hypotheses: Q, tame level 1, p≥5; k even and k not congruent to 0 modulo p−1; inverse diamond convention as stated.
proofSteps: Use the Q ordinary control and a₁-duality contract requested at PadicFamilies L1 Part II (Sharifi AWS Theorems 4.2.5, 4.2.7, 4.2.9 and Corollary 4.2.12, pp. 46–47). The current L5 quaternionic construction assumes even degree and is not a supplier over Q; the existing L1 symbol freeness also assumes residual irreducibility and cannot be applied at this Eisenstein ideal.
Hida duality between 𝔐 and ℌ; the Eisenstein series gives ℌ → Λ with kernel the Eisenstein ideal ℐ.
The constant-term functional gives T_0 ∈ ℌ with ℌ/(T_0) ≅ 𝔥 and image ½ξ in ℌ/ℐ ≅ Λ, hence 𝔥/I ≅ Λ/(ξ) (Emerton's proof, Sharifi AWS Theorem 4.3.3).

The pairing between the full ordinary forms and their Hecke algebra identifies the constant-term functional with T_0. The image of T_0 in the Eisenstein quotient ℌ/ℐ≅Λ is ξ/2; since 2 is a unit, quotienting by T_0 gives exactly Λ/(ξ). This proves the needed particular congruence module directly (Sharifi AWS Theorem 4.3.3, pp. 50–52), without using a generic codimension-zero Ψ_λ(M) comparison.
acceptance: p = 691, k = 12, level 1: Δ ≡ E_12 mod 691 (τ(ℓ) ≡ 1 + ℓ^{11}), so the Eisenstein maximal ideal of the ordinary Hecke algebra is proper.

Describes the Eisenstein homomorphism from the cuspidal Hecke algebra onto the Stickelberger quotient as the core of Ribet's method after Wiles.

nodes.title: Ribet's construction and the divisibility of characteristic ideals
nodes.statement: If ξ_k is a unit, the divisibility f_k | char(X∞^{ω^{1−k}}) is automatic and no Ribet representation is asserted. In the nonunit case, with 𝔥 = 𝔥_k, I and ξ = ξ_k as in hida-hecke-eisenstein-ideal: let ρ : G_Q → GL_2(Q(𝔥)) be the Galois representation on 𝒯 ⊗ Q(𝔥) in a basis adapted to the ordinary filtration at p (𝒯 the ordinary Λ-adic Tate module). Then a(σ) − det ρ(σ), d(σ) − 1 and b(σ)c(τ) lie in I; the 𝔥-spans B, C of b and c are faithful; ψ_c(σ) = det ρ(σ)^{-1}c(σ) mod IC is a cocycle whose restriction to G_{Q(μ_{p^∞})} is unramified everywhere and factors through X_∞^{(ω^{1−k})}, giving a surjection of Λ-modules X_∞^{(ω^{1−k})}(1) ↠ C/IC; and faithfulness gives Fitt_𝔥(C) = 0, hence Fitt_{𝔥/I}(C/IC) = 0; via 𝔥/I ≅ Λ/(ξ), this implies Fitt_Λ(C/IC) ⊆ (ξ) and therefore (ξ) divides char_Λ(C/IC), hence f_k | char(X_∞^{(ω^{1−k})}) with f_k(v^s − 1) = ξ(v^{s+1} − 1).
hypotheses: Q, tame level 1, p≥5, k as in hida-hecke-eisenstein-ideal.
For the representation and faithful coefficient modules, ξ_k is a nonunit, equivalently the Eisenstein local factor is nonzero. The unit case is the automatic divisibility stated separately.
proofSteps: Separate ξ_k a unit, when f_k is a unit and the divisibility is immediate. For the representation construction assume ξ_k a nonunit, as in Sharifi AWS Remark 4.3.2, p. 50.

Use the Q ordinary Tate-module contract requested at R21.3 Part II, not its even-degree Hilbert-family theorem. The trace limit of ordinary étale cohomology is Λ-free and rank two after total fractions; its connected–étale ordinary filtration has unramified quotient with Frobenius U_p (Sharifi AWS Theorems 4.2.13–4.2.15 and the construction following them, pp. 47–49). Localize at the nonzero Eisenstein factor and split the sequence as a sequence of Q(𝔥)-modules over total fractions; no G_Qp-equivariant splitting is asserted. No integral rank-two freeness or Gorenstein hypothesis at the Eisenstein ideal is asserted.
Ordinary local shape of ρ at p and the Čebotarev density of Frobenii give the congruences of Lemma 4.3.4 (Kurihara, Harder–Pink, Ohta) (Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10).
Faithfulness of B and C: BC ⊆ I contains a positive density of T_ℓ − 1 − ℓ⟨ℓ⟩.
Unramifiedness at p: the cocycle is unramified at p by the choice of basis adapted to the ordinary filtration; elsewhere ρ is unramified.

C is finite and faithful over 𝔥, so Fitt_𝔥(C) ⊆ Ann_𝔥(C) = 0. Base change gives Fitt_{𝔥/I}(C/IC) = 0. Since 𝔥/I ≅ Λ/(ξ), base change from Λ shows Fitt_Λ(C/IC) ⊆ (ξ). Localising at each height-one prime of the regular ring Λ turns this into the required length inequality (Sharifi AWS p. 52).
acceptance: Sharifi AWS p. 52: f_k | char(X_∞^{(1−k)}) for every even k, which with the analytic class number formula gives the main conjecture over Q.

sources.locator: §4.2–4.3, Theorems 4.2.13–4.2.15, pp. 47–49; Lemma 4.3.4 and the following argument, pp. 50–52
sources.match: Constructs ρ adapted to the ordinary filtration, proves the Eisenstein congruences of its matrix entries, the faithfulness of B and C, the unramified cocycle into C/IC and the divisibility f_k | char(X_∞^{(1−k)}).

Summarises Ribet's method as used by Wiles: a faithful Hecke module, a cohomology class unramified away from p and the Fitting ideal inclusion, and explains why ramification above p must be controlled.
Recalls that Ribet's method was used by Mazur–Wiles over Q and by Wiles over totally real fields, and gives the residually distinguishable proof sketch with the Fitting ideal inclusion.

nodes.title: Hecke-module and arithmetic-module actions
nodes.statement: The Λ-module structures used in ribet-extension-construction agree with those of IntegralIwasawaTheory I.1–I.2: (a) Λ acts on 𝔥 through inverse diamond operators ⟨a⟩^{-1}, so that the Galois action on C/IC through det ρ^{-1}c corresponds to the arithmetic conjugation action on X_∞ twisted by Z_p(1); (b) the module receiving the Ribet class is the unramified module X_∞ of I.2 (class-field-identification), not the S-ramified 𝔛_S, and the eigenspace is ω^{1−k}; (c) the comparison of the variables, f_k(v^s − 1) = ξ(v^{s+1} − 1), is the twist Tw_{±1} of I.1 and is kept explicit; (d) in the totally real case, the ψ-part of the S-ramified module and its relation with the odd parts of the unramified module of F_ψ(μ_p) is the Kummer duality of I.2/global-local-unit-sequence (d).
hypotheses: As in ribet-extension-construction.
proofSteps: Read off the twist from det ρ = ε_cyc·⟨ε_cyc⟩ on G_Q.
Use arithmetic-compact-action for the conjugation action and iwasawa-algebra-coordinate for the twist.
acceptance: Sharifi AWS Remark 4.3.2 and p. 52: Λ acts by inverse diamond operators, and ψ_c is Λ-linear from X_∞^{(1−k)}(1).

sources.match: Fixes the inverse-diamond convention and shows the cocycle factors through X_∞^{(1−k)} with the Tate twist.

nodes.title: One divisibility implies the main conjecture
nodes.statement: Over Q, for odd p, suppose f_k divides char(X∞^{ω^{1−k}}) for every nonexceptional even branch k. Then equality holds for every such k. The exceptional branch is treated by its pole-cancelled unit ideal. The analytic class number formula compares the product of the minus class-group orders with the product of generalized Bernoulli values. Ferrero–Washington gives μ=0 on both sides; the class number growth formula then equates the sums of λ-invariants. Each individual divisibility contributes a nonnegative degree difference, so all differences vanish. This target is the Q comparison; it makes no claim to supply Wiles’s original totally real proof.
hypotheses: p odd.
proofSteps: Over Q: Sharifi AWS Remark 2.5.2: the class number formula expresses h_n^- through generalised Bernoulli numbers, which gives the equality of total λ- and μ-invariants; a divisibility between monic polynomials of equal total degree for every character is an equality.
μ = 0 over abelian fields from IntegralIwasawaTheory L4/fw-arithmetic-mu-zero (μ for the analytic side from L4/fw-analytic-mu-zero).

Apply the class number identity at all sufficiently high layers, using the norm-control and bounded finite error terms from the class module growth theorem, to equate total λ. A quotient of monic distinguished polynomials with degree zero is one, so each branch gives equality (Sharifi AWS Remark 2.5.2, p. 23).

Include the exceptional branch in the degree sum: its pole-cancelled numerator is a unit, so f_0=1 divides its class characteristic ideal tautologically. Nonnegative degree differences over all branches, including that branch, then force its degree to be zero as well. When p=3 there are no nonexceptional even branches; the same class-number/Ferrero–Washington argument already gives the assertion, without applying the p≥5 Hecke construction (Sharifi AWS §§2.4–2.5, pp. 22–23).
acceptance: Sharifi AWS Remark 2.5.2: to prove the main conjecture it suffices to show one divisibility for all even k.

sources.match: Uses the analytic class number formula to equate λ(X^-) with Σ λ(Λ/(f_{2j})) and the μ-invariants, so one divisibility for all k gives the main conjecture.
Cites Wiles 1990 Theorem 1.4 for μ(X_ψ) = μ(G_ψ) when ψ has order prime to p.

nodes.title: The Eisenstein proof of the Mazur–Wiles main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime. For every even integer k, char_Λ(X_∞^{(ω^{1−k})}) = (f_k), where X_∞ is the unramified Iwasawa module of Q(μ_{p^∞}), f_k(v^s − 1) = L_p(ω^k, s) for k ≢ 0 mod p − 1 and f_k = 1 for k ≡ 0 mod p − 1; equivalently (main-conjecture-statement) char(𝔛_∞^{(k)}) = (g_k) and char(E_∞^{(k)}/C_∞^{(k)}) = char(X_∞^{(k)}). More generally, for a totally real abelian field F and an even character ψ of type S whose field F_ψ is abelian over Q, MainConjecture(F, p, ψ, S) holds in the strong form. Consequence: |A_{Q(μp)}^{(ω^{1−k})}| = p^{v_p(B_{1,ω^{k−1}})} for every even k ≢ 0 mod p − 1. The Q characteristic-ideal identity is the shared theorem at EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture L3; this node supplies its Eisenstein proof and the normalization interface. It does not import the Euler-system proof as a premise.
hypotheses: p odd; in the generalisation both F and F_ψ are abelian over Q.
proofSteps: Divisibility from ribet-extension-construction; equality from divisibility-to-equality (a).

The finite-level consequence: descend to n = 0 with coinvariant-euler-characteristic, using that X_∞^- has no nonzero finite submodule (I.2/cm-minus-class-modules) and f_k(0) ≡ −B_{1,ω^{k−1}} up to units.

For the broader totally real abelian-over-Q clause use the weak general theorem wiles-main-conjecture (and its type-S normalization) to compare distinguished factors. Ferrero–Washington gives μ=0 for the abelian class modules and for the abelian p-adic L-functions. The odd-prime Kummer comparison identifies the real p-ramified component with the corresponding minus class dual up to the explicit local Euler factors, which have μ=0. Thus equality of distinguished factors upgrades to the stated strong form. This argument is independent of the Q Eisenstein proof, which was scoped to tame level one; it makes no claim that that proof alone handles arbitrary abelian conductors.
acceptance: Sharifi AWS Theorem 2.5.13: |A^{(1−k)}| = p^{v_p(B_{1,ω^{k−1}})}.

sources.match: States the Mazur–Wiles main conjecture over Q, its equivalent forms and the refined Herbrand–Ribet formula, and proves the theorem in the style of Mazur–Wiles and Ohta.
States the Mazur–Wiles formula #A_K^{ω^i} = #Z_p/B_{1,ω^{−i}} for K = Q(μ_p) and odd i as a corollary of the main conjecture.
States the main conjecture over Q and its equivalent formulations.

nodes.title: Wiles's main conjecture for totally real fields
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real and p odd. For every even one-dimensional p-adic Artin character ψ of F of type S and every finite S ⊇ S_p ∪ S_∞, MainConjecture(F, p, ψ, S) holds: g*_{ψ,S} = G*_{ψ,S}. If moreover ψ has order prime to p, then μ(X_S(F_ψ)_ψ) = μ(G_{ψ,S}), so char(X_S(F_ψ)_ψ) = (G_{ψ,S}). For F = Q the statement also holds at p = 2.
hypotheses: F totally real, p odd (p = 2 allowed for F = Q), ψ even of type S.
proofSteps: Use I.10/nonequivariant-characteristic-ideal, proved from the all-prime determinant theorem I.9 and the keystone I.7 by Kurihara §4.2. Its proof does not use this Wiles node. For N=F_ψ with N∩F∞=F it gives char(X_S(N)_ψ-quotient)=(ψ(g)) for nontrivial ψ and ((γ−1)ψ(g)) for ψ=1.

The Deligne–Ribet dictionary gives ψ(g)=G_{ψ,S}/H_ψ. For a type-S character H_ψ=1 unless ψ is trivial; in the trivial case H_1=γ−1, cancelled by the cohomological factor. Thus the ψ-quotient has characteristic generator G_{ψ,S}.

If the chosen S omits a prime ramified in N/F, first enlarge to S₀ containing S_ram(N/F) to apply I.10. Remove the added primes using the induced local Euler modules. On the ψ-character quotient a ramified inertia group has zero invariants after inverting p, so it contributes no distinguished factor. For prime-to-p ψ, the integral inertia idempotent makes the same statement exactly, preserving μ as well. Thus the result has the stated finite-S range, instead of tacitly imposing the larger S₀ hypothesis.

If ψ has order prime to p, the integral idempotent identifies the quotient with the eigenspace, yielding the strong form including its μ-invariant. For arbitrary finite-order ψ, after inverting p the finite-group algebra is semisimple and quotient and eigenspace agree. Their distinguished polynomials therefore agree. Modules killed by a power of p cannot be discarded for the μ assertion, so no stronger integral eigenspace statement is inferred in that range.

This is an alternate proof of the theorem historically proved by Wiles, using Kurihara Theorem 4.1 and its second remark, pp. 24–27. It does not claim to reconstruct the unread Wiles original. The Q Eisenstein proof remains a separate target; arbitrary type-W twists are handled by going-up-induction.
acceptance: Kakde §3, p. 14: h_ψ(T) and G*_ψ(T) generate the same ideal (Wiles Theorem 1.3), and μ_ψ = 0 when p ∤ #Gal(F_ψ/F) (Wiles Theorem 1.4 under μ = 0).
The dependency chain is Wiles conclusion ← I.10 ← I.9 ← I.7. No I.7 or I.9 proof step imports the Wiles conclusion.

sources.match: Records that Wiles proved the main conjecture for odd p (and for p = 2 when F = Q) and that μ(X_ψ) = μ(G_ψ) for ψ of order prime to p.
Recalls Wiles's Theorems 1.3 and 1.4: h_ψ and G*_ψ generate the same ideal, and the μ-statement for p ∤ #Gal(F_ψ/F).
States that the main conjecture was proved by Wiles for odd p and all totally real fields, and for p = 2 over Q (also by Greither).
Notes that earlier progress on Brumer–Stark used the main conjecture for totally real fields proved by Wiles.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.1, Lemma 4.2 and proof, pp. 24–27; second remark, p. 27
sources.match: Proves the usual characteristic-ideal main conjecture from the all-prime keystone independently of Wiles. Integral prime-to-p idempotents and rational semisimplicity then give precisely the strong and weak forms stated here.

nodes.title: Going-up and induction for the main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let K be totally real and p any prime. Suppose the distinguished-polynomial MainConjecture(K,p,χ,S) holds for every even one-dimensional type-S Artin character χ over K. If F/K is finite totally real and ψ is an even one-dimensional type-S character over F whose character field F_ψ is abelian over K, then MainConjecture(F,p,ψ,S) holds. Here even means the character field is totally real, not that the values are real numbers. Over a common splitting coefficient field, inflation leaves the algebraic characteristic polynomial unchanged; induction and type-W twisting obey the same rules as the analytic distinguished factors. If e is defined by [F∩K∞:K]=p^e, the generator change is T_e=(1+T)^{p^e}−1. Analytic induction is an identity of G/H, with its pole factors H retained, rather than an unqualified product identity of numerators. For a type-W twist ρ, the substitutions on algebraic and analytic distinguished factors are T↦ρ(γ)(1+T)−1, followed by monic normalization. These conclusions concern distinguished factors, and do not assert a general μ comparison.
hypotheses: F/K finite totally real, p any prime, ψ even one-dimensional of type S over F, F_ψ/K abelian.
Use one finite coefficient field splitting the relevant finite groups; normalize distinguished factors to be monic and keep pole denominators.
proofSteps: Choose a common finite Galois extension containing the character fields and disjoint from the cyclotomic tower where type S applies. For inflation, pass to the quotient by the finite kernel of the larger Galois group. Restriction on maximal p-ramified groups has finite-index image; transfer and multiplication by the kernel order show that it is an isomorphism after tensoring Q_p. This proves equality of the algebraic polynomials (Greenberg Proposition 1, pp. 78–79).

For each generalized eigenspace of γ−1 over the common splitting field, the multiplicity of a root in the χ polynomial is its inner product with the character of that eigenspace. Frobenius reciprocity proves equality for induction (Greenberg Proposition 2, p. 79). When F∞ and K∞ start at different base layers, γ_F=γ_K^{p^e}; use T_e to compare the eigenvalues.

A type-W twist changes a chosen lift of γ by a central finite-order element. Its action on the character multiplicity space scales γ by ρ(γ), giving the stated substitution (Greenberg Proposition 3, pp. 79–80). The analytic substitution and induction follow from Artin formalism and the interpolation uniqueness of the Deligne–Ribet functions; retain G/H and its type-W denominator (Greenberg §2, pp. 80–83).

Since F_ψ/K is abelian, Ind ψ is a sum of one-dimensional characters after the chosen coefficient extension. Reduce each to type S by a type-W twist, apply the assumed main conjecture, and compare the same substitutions on both sides. If a cyclotomic base intersection is present, compare root multiplicities after T_e; this substitution is injective on rational functions, so equality descends. Greenberg Proposition 5, pp. 84–85, proves independence of this procedure by Frobenius reciprocity and nonnegative root multiplicities. Rognes–Weibel Theorem A.2, pp. 47–49, gives the explicit p=2 instance of the same argument.
acceptance: Rognes–Weibel Corollary A.3: the 2-adic formula of Theorem A.1 holds for all totally real abelian fields, by going-up from Q.

sources.locator: Appendix A (Kolster), Theorem A.2, Corollary A.3 and the proof of Theorem A.2, pp. 45–49
sources.match: Proves the going-up of the main conjecture to characters ψ over F with F_ψ abelian over K by factoring the p-adic L-functions under induction and comparing the roots of the distinguished polynomials.

sources.locator: Propositions 1–3, pp. 78–80; §2 induction and twist identities, pp. 80–83; Proposition 5, pp. 84–85
sources.match: Supplies the arbitrary-prime rational polynomial argument, coefficient extension, T_e substitution and the independence proof missing from the dyadic-only citation.

nodes.title: The Euler-characteristic endpoint of the main conjecture
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p odd, E = F(μ_p), Δ = Gal(E/F) (of order prime to p), S ⊇ S_p ∪ S_∞, X = 𝔛_S(E_∞) and n ≥ 2. For a one-dimensional even-or-odd character χ of F with F_χ ⊆ E and χ(−1) = (−1)^n, put ψ = χω^n (even, of order prime to p, hence of type S). Then X_ψ(−n)^Γ = 0, X_ψ(−n)_Γ is finite, and v_p(#X_ψ(−n)_Γ) = d_χ·v_p(L_S(1 − n, χ)) + v_p(#H⁰(E, Q_p/Z_p(n))_{χ^{-1}}), with d_χ = [O_χ : Z_p] and v_p the valuation of the fixed embedding Q̄ ⊆ Q̄_p, v_p(p) = 1; the H⁰ term is nonzero only when χ = ω^{−n} on Δ, i.e. ψ = 1. For χ = 1, n = 2 and S = S_p ∪ S_∞ this reads v_p(#X_{ω²}(−2)_Γ) = v_p(ζ_F(−1)) + v_p(w_2(F)): the equality of a finite Λ-module Euler characteristic with the p-adic valuation of ζ_F(−1), which SpecialValuesBirchTate B.4 converts into #H²_et(O_F[1/p], Z_p(2)) through IntegralIwasawaTheory I.4.
hypotheses: F totally real; p odd; n ≥ 2; χ with F_χ ⊆ F(μ_p) and χ(−1) = (−1)^n.
proofSteps: Apply wiles-main-conjecture to ψ (order prime to p, so the strong form holds), with the pole H_ψ(T) = ψ(γ)(1 + T) − 1 when ψ is of type W, i.e. ψ = 1 (Kolster p. 14 for the trivial character).
Evaluate the characteristic series of X_ψ(−n) at 0 with I.4/coinvariant-euler-characteristic; X has no nonzero finite submodule (I.2/weak-leopoldt (c)), so X_ψ(−n)^Γ = 0.

The Euler factors at v | p in L_S(1 − n, χ) = L(1 − n, χ)∏_{v|p}(1 − χ(v)Nv^{n−1}) are p-adic units for n ≥ 2, and |κ(γ)^n − 1|_p^{-1} accounts for H⁰(E, Q_p/Z_p(n))_{χ^{-1}}, nonzero only for χ = ω^{−n}·(trivial on Δ).
acceptance: Kolster Theorem 3.3: L_S(1 − n, χ)^{d_χ} ∼_p |H²_et(o^S_E, Z_p(n))_{χ^{-1}}| / |H⁰(E, Q_p/Z_p(n))_{χ^{-1}}|.

sources.locator: Lecture 2, §3, Propositions 3.1–3.2, Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4, pp. 13–15
sources.match: Combines the main conjecture with the coinvariant computation, treating the trivial character through H_1(T) = T and the group H⁰(E, Q_p/Z_p(n)), to relate L_S(1 − n, χ) to orders of étale cohomology and deduce ζ_F(1 − n) = ±h_n(F)/w_n(F) up to powers of 2.

nodes.title: Minus parts, the involution # and Pontryagin duals for CM extensions
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, H/F finite abelian with H CM, G = Gal(H/F) and c ∈ G complex conjugation. The integral minus ring is Z[G]^- := Z[G]/(1 + c), finite free over Z, and for any Z[G]-module M put M^- := M ⊗_{Z[G]} Z[G]^- = M/(1 + c)M; after inverting 2 this is also the −1-eigenspace {m : cm = −m}, but integrally at 2 the quotient, the eigenspace and the norm kernel are different functors and are never identified. The involution # of Z[G] is σ ↦ σ^{-1} (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6/sharp-involution). The Pontryagin dual of a finite Z[G]-module M is M^∨ = Hom_Z(M, Q/Z) (Mathlib CharacterModule) with the contragredient action (σf)(m) = f(σ^{-1}m). Then Ann_{Z[G]}(M^∨) = Ann_{Z[G]}(M)^# for finite M, Fitt(M^∨) = Fitt(M)^# when the p-Sylow subgroup of G is cyclic (p-adically), and in general only Fitt ⊆ Ann holds for each. The integral duality Hom_Z(M, Z) ≅ Hom_{Z[G]}(M, Z[G])^#, φ ↦ (m ↦ Σ_g φ(gm)[g^{-1}]), is equivariant when the left side has the contragredient action and the right side has its output-scalar action restricted along #; it identifies the lattice dual used for transposes; it differs from the finite dual M^∨ (for M = Z/p, Hom(M, Z_p[G]) = 0 while M^∨ ≅ Z/p).
hypotheses: F totally real, H/F finite abelian CM, c the complex conjugation in G.
proofSteps: c is central of order 2 because H is CM and G abelian; Z[G]/(1 + c) is torsion-free as c acts freely on G.
Ann of the dual: for finite M, x annihilates M^∨ iff x^# annihilates M, because (xf)(m) = f(x^#m).
Fitting ideals of duals for cyclic p-Sylow subgroups: Kurihara §2.5, proof of Corollary 2.9.

Integral duality: the stated map has inverse given by the coefficient of 1, and F(σφ)=σ^{-1}F(φ). Thus it is equivariant with the # scalar restriction on Hom_{Z[G]}(M,Z[G]), as in the dual convention used for DK Lemma A.8 and PMIL L6/contragredient-dual.
acceptance: DK §1.1, p. 6: Theorem 1.3 implies Theorem 1.2 through Fitt ⊆ Ann, Ann(M^∨) = Ann(M)^# and the action of c by −1 on Θ_{S,T}.

sources.match: Defines the Pontryagin dual with contragredient action, the involution #, minus parts M^- = M/(σ + 1) after inverting 2, and records Fitt ⊆ Ann and Ann(M^∨) = Ann(M)^#.
Defines the integral minus ring Z[G]^- = Z[G]/(1 + c), finite free over Z, and M^- = M/(1 + c)M, used at p = 2.
Uses lattice duality to compute the transpose; with the contragredient convention of §6, the group-ring Hom carries the # scalar restriction described here.
Uses Fitt_{Z_p[G]}(M)^# = Fitt_{Z_p[G]}(M^∨) for finite M when G_p is cyclic.

nodes.title: Smoothed and depleted class groups
nodes.statement: For H/F as above, a finite set T of finite places of F, T_H the places of H above T, and a set Σ of places: Cl^T(H) := I_T(H)/P_T(H), the ray class group of conductor ∏_{w ∈ T_H} w (Tau Ceti RayClassGroup for that modulus), where P_T(H) is generated by principal ideals (α) with α ≡ 1 mod every w ∈ T_H; Cl^T_Σ(H) is the quotient of Cl^T(H) by the classes of primes above Σ. These are finite Z[G]-modules. There is an exact sequence 1 → O_{H,Σ,T}^× → O_{H,Σ}^× → ∏_{w ∈ T_H} (O_H/w)^× → Cl^T_Σ(H) → Cl_Σ(H) → 0, and enlarging T by a prime v gives 0 → (∏_{w|v}(O_H/w)^×)/(image) → Cl^{T∪{v}} → Cl^T → 0, whose dual is the dual ray class sequence used for T-modification. Norm and extension maps for H ⊆ H' are compatible.
hypotheses: T disjoint from Σ; T ∩ S_ram arbitrary (DK allow ramified primes in the smoothing set Σ').
proofSteps: Instantiate Tau Ceti GlobalNumberFields ray class groups (TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup) with the squarefree modulus ∏_{w∈T_H} w and no infinite part.
The exact sequence is the ray class sequence of Tau Ceti GlobalNumberFields Layer 2 with units of the Σ-integers.
Galois action: G permutes T_H and Σ_H.
acceptance: For H = Q(μ_3) and T = {7}: Cl(H) = 1, ∏_{w|7}(O_H/w)^× ≅ (F_7^×)^2, μ_6 embeds as {(x, x^{-1})}, so Cl^T(H) ≅ F_7^× ≅ Z/6 with c acting trivially. Its integral minus quotient is Z/2; after tensoring with Z[1/2] that minus part is zero.

nodes.title: Smoothed Stickelberger elements of CM extensions and their integrality
nodes.statement: For H/F CM abelian and disjoint Σ ⊇ S_∞ (or, for DKSW, Σ ∪ Σ' ⊇ S_∞) and Σ' satisfying condition (1): (a) Θ_{Σ,Σ'} := Θ^{H/F}_{Σ,Σ'}(0) of IntegralIwasawaTheory I.3 lies in Z[G] when Σ ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, and in Z_p[G] for the depletion and smoothing sets Σ = S_∞ ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v | p}, Σ' = T ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} (DK (32), via the Sinnott–Kurihara ideal); (b) if Σ ⊇ S_∞ and #Σ ≥ 2, cΘ = −Θ, so Θ is determined by its image in Z[G]^- (after inverting 2); (c) under all (A1)–(A5) of keystone-fitting-theorem, for p = 2, with t = #(S_∞ ∩ Σ'), the element Θ_{Σ,Σ'}/2^t ∈ Z_2[G]^- characterised on odd characters exists; (d) on a character group ring R_Ψ of the minus part, Θ^# vanishes at every ψ with a trivial zero (ψ(G_v) = 1 for some v ∈ Σ), and on the trivial-zero-free quotient R_Ψ (Ψ = {ψ : ψ(v) ≠ 1 ∀ v ∈ Σ}) Θ^# is a non-zerodivisor; (e) for v ∤ p in S_ram, #I_v divides Nv − 1 in Z_p, so 1 − σ_v e_v Nv = (1 − σ_v e_v) + σ_v N I_v·(1 − Nv)/#I_v and Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} = Θ^#_{Σ,T} ∏_{v ∈ S_ram, v ∤ p}(1 − σ_v e_v Nv) lies in the p-modified Sinnott–Kurihara ideal SK^T_p(H/F) ⊆ Z_p[G] (DK Remark 3.6), although the individual factors need not be integral.
hypotheses: F totally real, H/F finite abelian CM, p a prime; Σ, Σ' as stated.
proofSteps: (a): I.3/smoothed-integrality, and Kurihara's Lemma 3.4 argument for the DK sets (DK Remark 3.6).
(b): I.3/stickelberger-functoriality (d).
(c): I.3/smoothed-integrality (c).

(d): ψ(Θ^#) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ, 0) = (1 − ψ(v))L_{Σ∖{v},Σ'}(ψ, 0) (DK Lemma 3.2); non-zerodivisor on R_Ψ by nonvanishing of L(ψ, 0) for odd ψ (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0/odd-character-l-zero-nonvanishing).
(e): the p-Sylow of tame inertia is a quotient of (O/v)^× (Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3).

nodes.title: The Sinnott–Kurihara ideal
nodes.statement: For H/F CM abelian, T satisfying condition (1) and S_ram the finite ramified places, with inertia I_v, decomposition G_v, e_v = (#I_v)^{-1}N I_v and σ_v ∈ G_v a Frobenius coset representative: SK^T(H/F) := (Θ^#_{S∞,T}) ∏_{v ∈ S_ram} (N I_v, 1 − σ_v e_v), a priori a fractional ideal of Z[G]. Equivalently SK^T(H/F) is generated by the elements ∏_{v ∈ J̄} N I_v·(Θ^{H_J/F}_{J,T})^#, S_∞ ⊆ J ⊆ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, J̄ = S_ram ∖ J, H_J the maximal subextension unramified at J̄. It lies in Z[G] (Kurihara). For an odd prime p, the p-modified ideal is SK^T_p(H/F) := (Θ^#_{Σ,T}) ∏_{v ∈ S_ram, v ∤ p}(N I_v, 1 − σ_v e_v) ⊆ Z_p[G] with Σ = S_∞ ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v | p}, and Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} ∈ SK^T_p.
hypotheses: As in smoothed-stickelberger; σ_v any Frobenius representative (1 − σ_v e_v is independent of the choice).
proofSteps: Independence of σ_v: e_v kills I_v − 1.
Integrality: expand the product and use (Θ^{H_J/F}_{J,T})^# ∈ Z[Gal(H_J/F)] (I.3/smoothed-integrality) with the multiplication by ∏ N I_v (DK (33)–(34)).

nodes.title: The T-smoothed analytic class number formula for minus parts
nodes.statement: Let H/F be CM abelian, H^+ its maximal real subfield, ε the nontrivial character of Gal(H/H^+), and T satisfying condition (1). Then L_{S∞,T}(H/H^+, ε, 0) ∈ Z, and up to a power of 2, #Cl^T(H)^- = L_{S∞,T}(H/H^+, ε, 0) = ∏_{ψ ∈ Ĝ odd} L_{S∞,T}(H/F, ψ, 0) = ∏_{ψ odd} ψ(Θ_{S∞,T}). The regulator relation R^T(H) = 2^{[H^+:Q]−1}R^T(H^+) is an exact analytic input. An exact dyadic class-group comparison also requires the norm kernel, cokernel and wide-class convention; the splitting after inverting 2 alone does not determine these. DKSW Lemma 2.13 supplies the required modified-class norm sequence in inclusion-implies-equality.
hypotheses: H/F CM abelian, F totally real, T satisfying condition (1).
proofSteps: The T-smoothed Dedekind class number formula at s = 0 for H and H^+ (leading terms of ζ_{H,S∞,T} and ζ_{H^+,S∞,T}, both of order [H^+ : Q] − 1) (AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4 Dedekind continuation and residue; DK (24)–(25)).
Condition (1) gives O_{H,S∞,T}^× = O_{H^+,S∞,T}^×, hence the regulator relation.
Artin formalism Ind_{G_{H+}}^{G_F} ε = ⊕_{ψ odd} ψ (AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4).
Integrality by Deligne–Ribet/Cassou-Noguès (I.3/smoothed-integrality).
acceptance: H = Q(μ_3), T = {7}: ∏_{ψ odd} ψ(Θ_{S∞,T}) = −2, and #Cl^T(H)^- = 1 up to a power of 2.

sources.locator: §2.1, Lemma 2.1 and its proof, equations (22)–(26), pp. 14–15
sources.match: Proves integrality of L_{S∞,T}(H/H^+, ε, 0) and the equality with #Cl^T(H)^- up to a power of 2, from the T-smoothed class number formula and the Artin formalism.

nodes.title: The Burns–Kurihara–Sano Selmer module
nodes.statement: For disjoint finite sets Σ ⊇ S_∞ and Σ' (Σ' satisfying condition (1)) of places of F, let H^×_{Σ'} = {x ∈ H^× : ord_w(x − 1) > 0 ∀ w ∈ Σ'_H} and Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H) := Hom_Z(H^×_{Σ'}, Z)/∏_{w ∉ Σ_H ∪ Σ'_H} Z, the image of (x_w) being Σ_w x_w ord_w, with contragredient G-action. Then: (a) 0 → Y_{H,Σ∖S∞} → Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H) → Sel^{Σ'}_{S∞}(H) → 0; (b) 0 → Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨ → Sel^{Σ'}_{S∞}(H) → Hom_Z(O^×_{H,S∞,Σ'}, Z) → 0, so Sel^{Σ'}_{S∞}(H)^- ≅ Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-} and 0 → Y^-_{H,Σ} → Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H)^- → Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-} → 0; (c) for S' ⊇ Σ with Cl^{Σ'}_{S'}(H) = 0, Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H) ≅ Hom_Z(O^×_{H,S',Σ'}, Z)/∏_{w ∈ S'_H ∖ Σ_H} Z; (d) Sel_p := Sel ⊗ Z_p is H² of the T-modified compactly supported complex RΓ_{c,T}(O_{H,S}, Z_p) when Σ = S, Σ' = T, and the triangle RΓ_c → RΓ_{c,T} → (⊕_{w∈T_H} Q_p/Z_p(1))^∨[−2] relates the modified and unmodified modules; (e) norm (corestriction) maps for H ⊆ H' make (Sel^T_S(H_n)_p)_n an inverse system along the cyclotomic tower; (f) for ψ ≠ 1 with ψ(G_v) = 1 for some v ∈ Σ, Fitt_{O_ψ}(Sel_ψ) = 0. The minus exact sequences and the identification with the class-group dual in (a)–(b) use Z[1/2] or Z_p for odd p. Integrally at 2, taking the quotient by 1+c is not exact and Y_{H,S∞}/(1+c) need not vanish. The all-prime transpose statement is supplied separately by Kurihara Theorem 2.12.
hypotheses: F totally real, H/F CM abelian; Σ ⊇ S_∞; Σ' with condition (1); for (d), S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, T = Σ'.
proofSteps: (a)–(b): the exact sequences of DK Lemma 3.1 and Burns' sequence; on minus parts Hom(O^×_{H,S∞,Σ'}, Z)^- = 0 because units of a CM field come from the real subfield up to torsion, killed by condition (1). This uses exactness of minus projection after inverting 2. At 2, a c-fixed free unit or place module has minus quotient M/2M, so this proof does not apply.
(c): Burns–Kurihara–Sano (12), cited by DK (31).
(d): Burns–Kurihara–Sano Proposition 2.4 (cited by Kurihara §4.2 p. 24) and ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 compact support.
(e): functoriality of ord_w under norms.
(f): (Sel ⊗ K)_ψ ⊇ (Ind_{G_v}^G K)_ψ ≅ K by Frobenius reciprocity (Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory InductionRestriction Layer 2).
acceptance: DK Lemma 3.1: 0 → Y^-_{H,Σ} → Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H)^- → Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-} → 0. Coefficients invert 2.

sources.locator: §3.1, definition (29), Lemma 3.1, equations (30)–(31) and the trivial-zero computation, pp. 19–20

nodes.title: Ritter–Weiss modules
nodes.statement: For H/F abelian (F a number field), disjoint finite sets S, T of places with S ∪ T ⊇ S_∞ (DKSW; S ⊇ S_∞ in Dasgupta–Kakde), auxiliary S' ⊇ S, and the Ritter–Weiss local and global data (local Weil-group extensions, the modules V_w, W_w, the semilocal J ⊆ V ↠ W, the global Tate extension 0 → C_H → 𝔒 → ΔG → 0 and the map θ of extensions), the module ∇^T_S(H) is the cokernel of V^θ → B^θ (Definition A.2). It satisfies: (P1) 0 → Cl^T_S(H) → ∇^T_S(H) → X → 0, with X = X_{H,S} (degree-zero divisors on places above S) when S ∪ T ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram (condition (A)/(A1)); its minus part is exact when some v ∈ S has c ∈ G_v. (P4) Under (B) (tame ramification in T) and (C) (O^×_{H,S,T} torsion-free), 0 → O^×_{H,S,T} → V^θ → B^θ → ∇^T_S(H) → 0 with V^θ, B^θ projective, a quadratic presentation under (A); for CM H and S ≠ ∅ a presentation of ∇^- by projective Z[G]^--modules; with (B_p) the same after ⊗ Z_(p). The construction is independent of S' up to canonical isomorphism (Lemma A.3). For the generalised DKSW construction with S not containing S_∞, its minus presentation uses a projective module V′ from Theorem 2.2; one must not identify it without proof with the original V^θ. Square projective or free presentations do not imply a nonzero determinant when trivial zeros occur.
hypotheses: H/F abelian; S, T disjoint, S ∪ T ⊇ S_∞; for the presentation, conditions (A), (B) or (B_p), and (C).
proofSteps: Local Weil-group extensions and the Ritter–Weiss modules V_w, W_w (local class field theory, Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layers 6 and 9).
The global Tate sequence extension from the global class formation (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 11) and the Ritter–Weiss map of extensions θ; surjectivity of V → 𝔒 (DK Lemma A.1).
Snake lemma for 0 → J → V → W → 0 against 0 → C_H → 𝔒 → ΔG → 0 gives 0 → O^× → V^θ → W^θ → Cl → 0 and then (P1).

Projectivity of V^θ: cohomological triviality of 𝔒, of induced local unit modules for unramified v, and of V_w (Ritter–Weiss), with Nakayama's criterion (cohomologically trivial and torsion-free ⇒ projective) (DK Lemma A.4).
Independence of S' (DK Lemma A.3 and §A.2).
acceptance: DK Remark A.7: over a Z_p[G]-algebra R, V^θ_R is free and ∇_R is quadratically presented for the sets (57), (59).

sources.locator: Appendix A, §A.1, equations (133)–(150), Definition A.2, Lemma A.1, Lemma A.3 and Lemmas A.4–A.5, pp. 78–86
sources.match: Constructs the local modules V_w, W_w, the semilocal sequence, the global Tate extension and the map θ, defines ∇^{Σ'}_Σ(H) as a cokernel, proves property (P1), independence of S' and the locally quadratic presentation.

States the properties of the generalised Ritter–Weiss modules ∇^T_S(H) with S ∪ T ⊇ S_∞: the class-group sequence, its minus part, and projective (quadratic) presentations under (A), (B) or (B_p), (C).
Lists the four properties of ∇ used in the proof and explains what is new relative to Ritter–Weiss and Burns–Kurihara–Sano.

nodes.title: Transpose, quadratic presentation and Fitting ideals of the Selmer module
nodes.statement: (a) (P3) Under (A2) (resp. (A2')), the transpose of ∇^{Σ'}_Σ(H) for the presentation V^θ → B^θ is Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H) (resp. after base change to R). (b) Hence for every character group ring quotient R of Z_p[G] (DK sets (57), (59)), Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_R is quadratically presented and Fitt_R(Sel_R) = Fitt_{R#}(∇_{R#})^#, a principal ideal. (c) With s excess generators, Fitt^0_{R#}(M^{tr}) = (Fitt^s_R(M))^#. (d) For S ⊇ S_ram and (O^T_{K,S})^× torsion-free, Sel^T_S(K)_p^- and ∇^T_S(K)_p^- have quadratic presentations over Z_p[G]^-, and Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(Sel^T_S(K)_p^-) = (Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(∇^T_S(K)_p^-))^#; these are the finite-presentation hypotheses of Kurihara's finite-level theorems.
hypotheses: As in ritter-weiss-module; R a character group ring quotient of Z_p[G].
proofSteps: (a): apply the contragredient integral duality Hom_Z(−,Z) ≅ Hom_{Z[G]}(−,Z[G])^# to 0 → W^θ → B^θ → Z^θ → 0 and compare with the presentation (31) of Sel (DK Lemma A.8). Keep the # scalar restriction from I.6/cm-minus-parts-and-duals when identifying the transpose.
(b): transposes of quadratically presented modules and their Fitting ideals (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6/transpose-fitting; DK Lemma 6.1, Corollary 6.2).
(c): PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6/transpose-higher-fitting (DK (175)).
(d): Kurihara §2.6 citing Burns–Kurihara–Sano Proposition 2.4(iv) and Lemma 2.8.
acceptance: DK Corollary 6.2: Fitt_R(Sel_R) = Fitt_{R#}(∇_{R#})^#.

sources.locator: §6.1, Lemma 6.1 and Corollary 6.2, p. 40; Appendix A.4, Lemma A.8, pp. 86–87
sources.match: Proves that the transpose of ∇ for its projective presentation is the Selmer module, and that transposes of quadratically presented modules have Fitting ideals related by #.
States that for S ⊇ S_ram(K/k) and torsion-free (O^T_{K,S})^×, Sel^T_S(K)^- and ∇^T_S(K)^- have quadratic presentations with principal Fitting ideals related by #.

nodes.title: Extension classes of Ritter–Weiss modules via Galois cohomology
nodes.statement: (a) (P2, Dasgupta–Kakde Lemma 6.4) Over Z[1/2] and on minus parts, with M = Cl^{Σ'}_Σ(H)^-, the extension class of 0 → M → ∇^- → X^-_{H,Σ} → 0 in Ext¹_{Z[G]^-}(X^-_{H,Σ}, M) ≅ ⊕_{v∈Σ} H¹(G_v, M) is the tuple (λ_v) of local restrictions of the class λ ∈ H¹(G_F, M) whose restriction to G_H is the Artin reciprocity map onto Gal(L/H) ≅ M; here restriction H¹(G_F, N) → H¹(G_H, N)^G is an isomorphism for every Z[G]^--module N. (b) (DKSW Theorem 2.3, all p) Assume (A) and (B) or (B_p), S ≠ ∅ and v_0 ∈ S. For a finite G-module N (a p-group under (B_p)), a 1-cocycle κ : G_F → N with κ(G_{F_{v0}}) = 0, κ unramified outside S ∪ T and tamely ramified at finite v ∈ T, and elements x_v (v ∈ S ∖ {v_0}) with κ(σ) = (σ − 1)x_v for σ ∈ G_{F_v}, there is a G-equivariant map ∇^T_S(H) → N whose image is generated by κ(G_F) and the x_v.
hypotheses: (a): F totally real, H CM, 2 inverted. (b): (A), (B) or (B_p), S ≠ ∅.
proofSteps: (a): H^i(G, N) = 0 for minus modules after inverting 2, since c acts as −1 and trivially on cohomology (DK Lemma 6.3; Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 5 inflation–restriction).
Compute the class of ∇^- through the cocycles γ_v(g) = gx − x for lifts x of ½(w − w̄) (DK (84)) and compare with the explicit Ritter–Weiss cocycle for λ (DK §A.5, Lemma A.9).
(b): DKSW §4.6 through their duality theorem for class formations (DKSW §5).
acceptance: DK Theorem 9.8 uses (a) to complete diagram (125) by a surjection ∇_{R#} ↠ B̄_p(𝛙^{-1}).

sources.locator: §6.2, Lemma 6.3, equations (82)–(84) and Lemma 6.4, pp. 41–42; §A.5, Lemma A.9, pp. 87–89
sources.match: Shows that restriction is an isomorphism on minus modules, defines the canonical class λ and its local components λ_v, and proves that the minus extension class of ∇ equals (λ_v).
Characterises maps from ∇^T_S(H) to finite G-modules by cocycles with prescribed local behaviour, valid for all p including p = 2.

nodes.title: Inclusion of Fitting ideals implies equality
nodes.statement: Fix p, a CM abelian H/F, an odd character χ of the prime-to-p part G' of G, R = O[G_p]_χ the corresponding component (for p = 2, the components of Z_2[G]^-), and the sets Σ = S_∞ ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v | p}, Σ' = T ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} (DK (57)–(59); for p = 2 the DKSW sets with an archimedean place moved and the factor 2^t). Suppose that in every such situation Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_R is quadratically presented and Fitt_R(Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_R) ⊆ (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) (resp. Fitt(∇_{p,−}) ⊆ (Θ_{Σ,Σ'}/2^t)). Then each inclusion is an equality.
hypotheses: All CM abelian extensions H/F of the given type and all components χ are considered simultaneously; p arbitrary (DK for p odd, DKSW §2.5 for p = 2).
proofSteps: Trivial zeros: on characters ψ with ψ(G_v) = 1 for some v ∈ Σ both sides vanish (I.6/smoothed-stickelberger (d); I.6/selmer-module (f)), so pass to the trivial-zero-free quotient.
Reduce by induction on the field: descend the R-component of the Selmer module to H_χ and to subfields (DK Lemmas 4.1–4.3, 5.2, 5.4).

Compare orders: a quadratically presented module with principal Fitting ideal (x) over a character group ring has order #O/∏ψ(x) (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6/quadratic-cardinality and character-group-ring-index).

Compute #Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨ components by the minus class number formula (I.6/minus-class-number-formula) together with Lemmas 5.5–5.7 for the norm element of the minimal inertia group, and conclude that the quotient of generators is a unit (DK §5; DKSW Theorem 2.7, Lemmas 2.11–2.13).
acceptance: DK §2.3, p. 18: in the conductor-one case, (11) and (12) force the inclusion of Fitting ideals to be an equality.

sources.locator: §5, Theorem 5.1 and Lemmas 5.2–5.7, Remark 5.8, pp. 31–39; §2.3, pp. 16–18
sources.match: Proves that an inclusion Fitt_R(Sel_R) ⊆ (Θ^#) in every situation implies equality, using the analytic class number formula, descent of components and the size of quadratically presented modules.
Proves the inclusion-implies-equality theorem at p = 2 for the generalised Ritter–Weiss modules with the factor 2^t.

nodes.title: A cuspidal group-ring family congruent to an Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: For p odd: Let R be the trivial-zero-free character group ring quotient of a component of O[G] (DK §7.1), 𝛙 the canonical character, n = cond(H/F)∏_{𝔩∈T}𝔩, P the p-part of n and x = Θ_{S∞}(1 − k)/Θ_{S∞}(0) ∈ R (a non-zerodivisor ≡ ∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − χ(𝔭)^{-1}) mod 𝔪_R). For k ≡ 1 mod (p − 1)p^N with N large there is a p-ordinary cuspidal group-ring family F_k(𝛙) ∈ S_k(nP', R, 𝛙)^{p-ord} with: case 1a (P = 1, some χ(𝔭) = 1): F_k(𝛙) ≡ x·W_1(𝛙, 1) − W_k(𝛙, 1_p) mod xΘ^#; case 1b (P = 1, all χ(𝔭) ≠ 1): F_k(𝛙) ≡ W_1(𝛙_p, 1) mod Θ^#; case 2 (P ≠ 1): F_k(𝛙) ≡ W_1(𝛙_{𝔓𝔓''}, 1) mod Θ^#; congruences are of all Fourier coefficients. For p = 2 use the separate DKSW construction: write d = [F:Q]. If no p-adic prime ramifies, take Σ = {ℓ}, with ℓ ∤ np unramified and Frob_ℓ = c; otherwise take Σ = {v ∈ S_ram : v | p}. In both cases Σ′ = T ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} ∪ S_∞, with T containing no p-adic prime. Work on the Galois-stable odd trivial-zero-free character quotient R_{Φ_0}. Choose m so large that Θ^#/2^d divides p^m and k > 1 odd with k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N and ε_cyc^{k−1} ≡ 1 mod p^m. DKSW Theorems 3.2–3.5 and Corollaries 3.6, 3.8 give the ordinary cusp congruences modulo xΘ^#/2^d, at the indicated raised level; the unramified case also uses the ℓ-old forms. These are not obtained by simply changing the modulus in the odd-prime τ-basis argument.
hypotheses: For the DK odd-prime construction, its component, level and weight hypotheses as stated.

For the dyadic construction, the disjoint minimal sets Σ, Σ′ and character quotient of DKSW Theorem 2.14; d = [F:Q]; m, N and k as stated. The auxiliary ℓ is chosen so its Frobenius is nonscalar on the finitely many relevant eigenform representations (DKSW Lemma 3.10).
proofSteps: Group-ring Eisenstein series E_k(𝛙, 1), the modified series W_k(𝛙, 1) with integral nonconstant coefficients, and the ordinary projector formula: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3/group-ring-eisenstein-families.
Constant terms at all cusps (DK Propositions 8.4, 8.6, 8.7): AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3/eisenstein-constant-terms.
Hida–Silliman forms V_k ≡ 1 mod p^m (DK Theorem 8.8) and Silliman's group-ring forms with prescribed constant terms (DK Theorem 8.9) and the cuspidal correction (DK Theorem 8.15).

Form x W_1 V_{k−1} − W_k − xΘ^#H_k (case 1) or e^ord_P(W_1 V_{k−1} − Θ^#H_k) (case 2), cuspidal by Theorems 8.17–8.18; apply e^ord and the factors (U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭)) (DK Corollaries 8.19, 8.21; PadicFamilies L0a ordinary projector).

For p = 2, use DKSW Theorem 2.14, pp. 17–18, to reduce to these minimal sets. Choose the auxiliary prime by Lemma 3.10, and use the separate ℓ-old cusp form construction and congruences in §3.2, pp. 24–26. Here t = #(Σ′ ∩ S_∞) = d; n in the ideal level is unrelated to d.

Invoke the exact APL L3 Part II contract for V_k, prescribed constants, cuspidal correction and integral expansions at these levels. DK Theorems 8.8, 8.9 and 8.15 provide these inputs with the ranges written in the request. The ordinary finite-weight construction and the separate ℓ-old formulas are read directly in DKSW §3.2; the p-odd Λ-adic Hilbert supplier is not used to justify them.
acceptance: DK Remark 8.20: the congruence (105) is a congruence of all Fourier coefficients c(m, ·).

sources.locator: §8, Lemma 8.1, Theorems 8.8–8.9, 8.15, 8.17–8.18, Lemma 8.16, Corollaries 8.19 and 8.21, pp. 50–62
sources.match: Constructs modified Eisenstein series, corrects them to cusp forms using Silliman's results, and obtains p-ordinary cuspidal group-ring families congruent to Eisenstein series modulo xΘ^# or Θ^#.
Adapts the construction to p = 2 with the auxiliary prime and the factor 2^n.

nodes.title: The Eisenstein homomorphism on the group-ring Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let T ⊆ T̃ be the Hecke algebras over R generated by T_𝔩 (𝔩 ∤ np) and S(𝔪) (resp. also U_𝔭 for 𝔭 | p) acting on the p-ordinary group-ring cusp forms of extra-congruence-cusp-form, 𝔐 the Eisenstein maximal ideal (kernel of the mod 𝔪_R eigencharacter of F_k(𝛙)), and, for p odd, T_𝔐 ⊆ T̃_𝔐 ⊆ ∏_{f∈M̄} O the completed finite coefficient orders (M̄ the ordinary newforms congruent to the Eisenstein system). Then there are a non-zerodivisor x ∈ R, an R/xΘ^#-algebra W and a surjective R-algebra map φ : T̃_𝔐 → W such that: R/xΘ^# → W is injective; on T_𝔐, φ(S(𝔪)) = 𝛙(𝔪), φ(U_𝔭) = 1 for 𝔭 | P and φ(T_𝔩) = ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) + 𝛙(𝔩); and for U = ∏_{𝔭|P'}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭)), φ(U)y = 0 with y ∈ R implies y ∈ (Θ^#). For p = 2, the coefficient algebra is instead a finite order in K = ∏_f K_f, with K_f a coefficient field or the finite quadratic algebra arising from U_ℓ on an ℓ-old space; K_f can be nonreduced. Put A = Θ^#/2^d with the minimal sets and d = [F:Q] of extra-congruence-cusp-form. The map φ : T̃_𝔐 → W induces T_𝔐/I ≅ R/(xA), so R → T_𝔐/I is surjective, and satisfies φ(Uy) = 0 ⇒ y ∈ (A) for y ∈ R, with U the specified product of U_v−𝛙(v). It is this cancellation statement, together with the local factors of hecke-galois-representation, that is required in DKSW Theorem 2.16.
hypotheses: As in extra-congruence-cusp-form; x as there in case 1a and x = 1 otherwise.
proofSteps: W is the image of the T̃-span of F_k(𝛙) in ∏_𝔞 R/xΘ^# under Fourier coefficients (DK proof of Theorem 8.23).
Hecke formulas (97) for group-ring forms show the map is Hecke-equivariant; Artin–Rees for the completions.
The last property uses the factor x in the congruence of case 1a (DK p. 77).

Use the precise quotient and cancellation statement in DKSW Theorem 3.9, pp. 26–27. In the ℓ-old case retain the quadratic U_ℓ algebra and its possible nilpotents; no embedding of T̃ into a product of fields is asserted.

The finite Hecke order is the image on these finite-weight integral cusp spaces. Use their faithful q-expansion pairing and finite coefficient extension from the APL L3 request. In the odd-prime construction the commuting characteristic-zero eigenforms give a reduced field product; in the dyadic ℓ-old construction retain the full quadratic principal algebra instead. No Hilbert Λ-adic reducedness or total-fraction-ring theorem is imported here.
acceptance: DK Theorem 8.23(ii): φ(T_𝔩) = ε^{k−1}_cyc(𝔩) + 𝛙(𝔩) for 𝔩 ∤ np.

sources.match: Defines the Hecke algebras of p-ordinary group-ring cusp forms, the Eisenstein maximal ideal and the surjection φ onto W with R/xΘ^# ↪ W and the stated values and cancellation property.
Gives the version with Θ^#/2^n and a possibly non-reduced Hecke algebra at p = 2.

nodes.title: The Galois representation of the Eisenstein-localised Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: For p odd: With K = Frac(T_𝔐) = ∏_{f∈M̄} E (the reduced odd-prime case), there is a continuous ρ = ∏_f ρ_f : G_F → GL_2(K) unramified outside np, with characteristic polynomial x² − T_𝔩 x + 𝛙(𝔩)ε^{k−1}_cyc(𝔩) at Frob_𝔩 for 𝔩 ∤ np (DK (113)), whose restriction to each decomposition group at 𝔭 | p has the ordinary shape (𝛙η_𝔭^{-1}ε^{k−1}_cyc ∗; 0 η_𝔭) with η_𝔭 unramified and η_𝔭(rec(ϖ^{-1})) = U_𝔭 (DK (114)); its characteristic polynomials lie in T_𝔐[x] and factor residually as (x − ε^{k−1}_cyc)(x − 𝛙); there is τ ∈ G_F with χ(τ) ≠ 1 moving every local ordinary line V_{𝔭,f} (Proposition 9.3), so in a basis of ρ(τ)-eigenvectors the off-diagonal entries satisfy A_{f,𝔭} ≠ 0 and C_{f,𝔭} ≠ 0 (key point (111)). The inputs are: Wiles's ordinary Hilbert representations, irreducibility on open subgroups for non-CM forms (Ribet; Balasubramanyam–Ghate–Vatsal), splitting of p in the CM field for p-ordinary CM forms (Hara–Ochiai), and the CM ordinary line moved by complex conjugation. For p = 2 use K = Frac(T̃_𝔐) with the finite local principal factors K_f of the preceding construction. Assemble ρ_f over these factors; the reduction in each field factor is irreducible. Its characteristic polynomial lies in T_𝔐[X] and is congruent to (X−χ)(X−𝛙) modulo I, χ = ε_cyc^{k−1}. On each v ∈ Σ ∪ P, P = {v | p : v ∉ Σ}, provide a local lower-triangular basis with characters (η_v, ξ_v), ξ_v ≡ 𝛙 on G_v for v ∈ Σ, and ξ_v ≡ χ on inertia for v ∈ P. The product ∏_{v∈P}(ξ_v(σ_v)−χ(σ_v)) agrees with the Hecke cancellation factor up to units as required by DKSW Theorem 2.16. A global basis with distinct residual eigenvalues is not assumed at 2. The exact finite-weight all-prime R19.2 Part II contract below supplies the representations in this range; current narrower R19.2 nodes are used only for the subcases their hypotheses cover.
hypotheses: As in group-ring-hecke-eisenstein-homomorphism; p odd in DK, p = 2 in DKSW with auxiliary prime.
proofSteps: Import the R19.2 Part II finite-weight/all-prime existence, coefficient and local-shape theorem with the exact hypotheses in requests. This is a supplier target, not a claim that current wiles-ordinary-hilbert-representation already has that range. For each eigenform use its finite coefficient field, then extend scalars to K_f when necessary.

Non-CM f: R19.2/virtual-reducibility-implies-cm gives irreducibility on open subgroups (DK Lemma 9.1). CM f: R19.2/ordinary-cm-primes-split and R19.2/cm-ordinary-line-complex-conjugation (DK Lemma 9.2).
For p odd choose τ by DK Proposition 9.3 and split its two distinct residual roots by Hensel’s lemma. This step is confined to the residually distinguishable component.

In the odd-prime case assemble the representations over the product of coefficient fields. For p = 2, retain the ℓ-old quadratic algebras, use nonscalar Frobenius from Lemma 3.10, and the simultaneous local statements of DKSW Theorem 3.14, pp. 27–30. Check each local congruence and the unit factors against Theorem 2.16.
acceptance: DK (111): A_{f,𝔭} ≠ 0 and C_{f,𝔭} ≠ 0 for every f ∈ M̄ and every 𝔭 | p.

sources.match: Attaches to each ordinary eigenform its Galois representation with the ordinary local shape, proves the needed irreducibility and the existence of τ moving all local eigenspaces, and assembles ρ over the total ring of fractions.
Constructs ρ at p = 2 when the Hecke algebra is not reduced because of old forms at the auxiliary prime.

nodes.title: The Ribet module and cohomology class of the Eisenstein ideal
nodes.statement: For p odd in the distinct-residual setting: In a basis of ρ(τ)-eigenvectors write ρ(σ) = (a(σ) b(σ); c(σ) d(σ)). Let Ĩ = ker φ ⊆ T̃_𝔐 and I = Ĩ ∩ T_𝔐. Then tr ρ(σ) ≡ ε^{k−1}_cyc(σ) + 𝛙(σ) mod I, a(σ) ≡ ε^{k−1}_cyc(σ) and d(σ) ≡ 𝛙(σ) mod I. Let B_0 be the T_𝔐-module generated by the b(σ), B = (B_0, A_𝔭/C_𝔭 : 𝔭 ∈ Σ ∖ S_∞), B' = B(I_p) the submodule generated by b of inertia at the primes above p not in Σ, and B̄_p = B/(IB, B', p^m B) with submodule B̄_0. Then κ(σ) = b(σ)𝛙(σ)^{-1} defines a class κ ∈ H¹(G_F, B̄_p(𝛙^{-1})) (with ε_cyc^{k−1} ≡ 1 after the choice of k) that is unramified away from Σ', tamely ramified at Σ', locally trivial at Σ, and whose cocycle values generate B̄_0. The general algebra (Ribet modules with local conditions, the cocycle and its Fitting bound) is IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.6; this node verifies its hypotheses for the Hilbert–Eisenstein representation. For p = 2 replace the τ-eigenbasis construction by the all-residual local weighted IHG.6 Part II existence theorem. Apply it to T_𝔐 ⊂ T̃_𝔐, χ = ε_cyc^{k−1} and ψ = 𝛙, with the local triangular data above. This supplies a finite T_𝔐-module N_0, a continuous cocycle κ_0 ∈ Z¹(G_F,N_0(χψ^{-1})), and elements y_v for v ∈ Σ ∖ {v_0}. They satisfy κ_0(G_{v_0}) = 0, κ_0(σ) = (χψ^{-1}(σ)−1)y_v on G_v, and κ_0(I_v) = 0 for v ∈ P. The module is generated by the cocycle values together with these y_v. Put N̄ = N_0/(IN_0+p^mN_0). Because χ ≡ 1 mod p^m and R → T/I is surjective, κ_0 reduces to a cocycle with values in N̄(ψ^{-1}), satisfying DKSW Theorem 2.3 and generating N̄ together with the local y_v. A class-group map alone need not generate N̄. Use the all-residual local weighted existence theorem requested from IHG.6 Part II. The current local_ribet supplies its coincident-residual branch; the b-coefficient branch of DKSW-RIBET Remark 2.2 supplies distinct residues. The latter is requested with all the same local generators, weighted Fitting and topology conclusions, without identifying its module with the narrower theorem’s canonical quotient.
hypotheses: As in hecke-galois-representation; m ≥ ord_p(#G_p).
proofSteps: For p odd, obtain the trace congruence by Hecke eigenvalues and Chebotarev; the τ argument gives diagonal congruences because the residual roots are distinct. This argument is not used at p = 2.

For the odd-prime distinct-residual branch matrix multiplication gives the upper-right cocycle modulo IB. At p=2 use the IHG.6 Part II all-residual local existence contract: the current difference-matrix theorem proves its coincident branch, while the distinct branch uses the b-coefficient method with adjoined local generators. No division by a vanishing residual eigenvalue gap is used.

Ramification: unramified at 𝔩 ∤ np by ρ; tame at Σ' by pro-p cohomology of tame inertia (DK Proposition 9.4); unramified above p outside Σ by quotienting by B'; locally trivial at Σ by (116) and φ(U_𝔭) = 1 (DK Proposition 9.5).

Verify the extra current-upstream topology hypothesis as follows. Each field-valued ρ_f has a stable coefficient lattice, and the finitely many K_f are finite-dimensional p-adic algebras, including the quadratic nonreduced factors. Compactness bounds all matrix entries in a finite O-lattice. Enlarge that lattice to contain the two difference modules and their products, and close it under the finite O-algebra T; this is still finite. The induced topology and the m_T-adic topology agree on this lattice by the finite-module adic topology theorem (T is a finite local O-algebra). Supply this lattice to local_ribet. If a packaging supplier does not expose that topology theorem, it must be included in the IHG.6 contract.

At p = 2 reduce modulo I and p^m only after obtaining the local generators and weighted Fitting bound. The ramification outside Σ ∪ Σ′ ∪ P comes from ρ, inertia at P is killed by the local theorem, and finite places in Σ′ have residue characteristic different from p, giving the tame condition (DKSW Theorem 2.16, pp. 20–21).

Split the supplier proof by residual coincidence. Check hres before applying current local_ribet. If ψ has nontrivial odd-order residual part, use the distinct-residual branch of the Part II request, justified by DKSW-RIBET Remark 2.2. Both branches output precisely the same existence interface needed here, so the arithmetic proof treats every residual component.
acceptance: DK Corollary 9.6: a canonical R^#-surjection α : Cl^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_{R#} ↠ B̄_0(𝛙^{-1}).

sources.match: Defines the Eisenstein ideals, the modules B_0, B, B' and B̄_p, the cohomology class κ and proves its ramification properties and the surjection from the class group.
Constructs the module N and the cocycle with local conditions in the general GL_2 setting, without residual distinguishability.

States that the local theorem also holds without residual coincidence and points to the b-coefficient method. The current IHG.6 local_ribet signature is narrower, so its extension remains an explicit supplier request.

uses.how: κ and the vectors A_𝔭/C_𝔭 give the extension classes matched with ∇
Fitt_R(B̄_p) is bounded by (Θ^#)
