api.statement: κ ∈ H¹(G_F, B̄_p(𝛙^{-1})), κ(σ) = b(σ)𝛙(σ)^{-1}. In the dyadic branch use the all-residual local cocycle κ_0 reduced in N̄(ψ^{-1}).

api.name: IntegralIwasawaTheory.ribetClass_unramified
api.statement: κ is unramified away from Σ', tame at Σ' and locally trivial at Σ. At 2 the representative is zero at v_0 and a specified coboundary with generator y_v at each other v ∈ Σ.

api.name: IntegralIwasawaTheory.ribetClass_generates
api.statement: The values κ(G_F) generate B̄_0 over R. This upper-right statement is for p odd. At 2 the cocycle values and y_v together generate N̄.

api.name: IntegralIwasawaTheory.ribetClass_classGroup
api.statement: Class field theory turns κ into a surjection Cl^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_{R#} ↠ B̄_0(𝛙^{-1}). This is the distinct-residual odd-prime branch; the dyadic target uses ∇ and its local generators directly.

api.name: IntegralIwasawaTheory.dyadicRibet_quotient
api.statement: The quotient N_0 → N̄ carries the cocycle and every local y_v to the corresponding reduced data; these data, rather than cocycle values alone, determine the generating map.

nodes.title: A surjection from the Ritter–Weiss module
nodes.statement: For p odd: There is an R^#-module surjection β : ∇^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_{R#} ↠ B̄_p(𝛙^{-1}) completing the diagram whose rows are 0 → Cl^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_{R#} → ∇_{R#} → (X_{H,Σ})_{R#} → 0 and 0 → B̄_0 → B̄_p → B̄_1 → 0, with outer maps α (from eisenstein-cohomology-class) and γ : (X_{H,Σ})_{R#} ↠ B̄_1(𝛙^{-1}) (DK Proposition 9.7). At p = 2 apply DKSW Theorem 2.3 to N̄(ψ^{-1}), the representative κ and all y_v to obtain ∇^{Σ′}_Σ(H)_R ↠ N̄(ψ^{-1}). Surjectivity uses their joint generation from local_ribet, not a claimed surjection from the class-group term alone. Use the all-residual local weighted existence theorem requested from IHG.6 Part II. The current local_ribet supplies its coincident-residual branch; the b-coefficient branch of DKSW-RIBET Remark 2.2 supplies distinct residues. The latter is requested with all the same local generators, weighted Fitting and topology conclusions, without identifying its module with the narrower theorem’s canonical quotient.
hypotheses: As in eisenstein-cohomology-class.
proofSteps: Compare the two extension classes in Ext¹_{R#}((X_{H,Σ})_{R#}, B̄_0(𝛙^{-1})) after pushout by α and pullback by γ; by I.6/ritter-weiss-galois-cohomology (P2) the class of ∇ is the tuple of local classes λ_v, which match the local values of κ (DK proof of Theorem 9.8).
Equal extension classes give the completing map; surjectivity from surjectivity of α and γ.

At p = 2 verify every condition of DKSW Theorem 2.3 from the reduced local_ribet data: zero at v_0, specified local coboundaries elsewhere in Σ, ramification only in Σ ∪ Σ′ and tameness at finite Σ′. Its image contains κ(G_F) and the y_v, so it is all of N̄(ψ^{-1}).
acceptance: DK Theorem 9.8.

sources.match: Constructs γ from the elements A_𝔭/C_𝔭 and proves that the extension class of ∇ maps to that of B̄_p, yielding the surjection β.
Applies Theorem 2.3 to obtain a surjection ∇^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_R → N from the cocycle.

nodes.title: The Fitting-ideal bound
nodes.statement: For p odd, Fitt_R(B̄_p) ⊆ (Θ^#), hence the corresponding ∇ and Selmer bounds follow by the surjection and transpose. For p = 2 put A = Θ^#/2^d in the DKSW minimal-set case. The local Ribet theorem gives the weighted bound P_loc·Fitt_T(N_0) ⊆ Ĩ, where P_loc = ∏_{v∈P}(ξ_v(σ_v)−χ(σ_v)). It does not assert Fitt_T(N_0) ⊆ I. The Hecke cancellation property, R → T/I surjective, and A | p^m then yield Fitt_R(N̄) ⊆ (A). Twisting and the dyadic ∇ surjection give Fitt(∇_{p,−}) ⊆ (Θ/2^d); inclusion-implies-equality and change of depletion/smoothing sets give the general t = #(Σ′ ∩ S_∞) formulation. Use the all-residual local weighted existence theorem requested from IHG.6 Part II. The current local_ribet supplies its coincident-residual branch; the b-coefficient branch of DKSW-RIBET Remark 2.2 supplies distinct residues. The latter is requested with all the same local generators, weighted Fitting and topology conclusions, without identifying its module with the narrower theorem’s canonical quotient.
hypotheses: As in surjection-from-nabla.
proofSteps: Generate B̄_p by c_i = b(σ_i)𝛙(𝔭_i)ε^{1−k}_cyc(σ_i) (one for each 𝔭_i | P') and non-zerodivisor generators b_j (Lemma 9.9).

Rewrite each relation row as an identity in B with factors (U_{𝔭_j} − 𝛙(𝔭_j) + I); the matrix M' over K has determinant 0, cancel the non-zerodivisors A_j/C_j and b_j, and apply φ: 0 = φ(U)(det M + p^m R) in W (DK proof of Theorem 9.10).
By group-ring-hecke-eisenstein-homomorphism, det M ∈ (Θ^#) since Θ^# | p^m (DK Lemma 8.1).

At 2 use IHG.6 local_ribet with its finite lattice/topology input, not merely global_ribet. Given y ∈ Fitt_R(N̄), lift its Fitting relation modulo I and p^m to get y+i+p^mr ∈ Fitt_T(N_0), with i ∈ I and r ∈ R. Multiplying by P_loc gives P_loc(y+p^mr) ∈ Ĩ. The Hecke cancellation property implies y+p^mr ∈ (A), and A | p^m implies y ∈ (A) (DKSW Theorem 2.16, pp. 20–21).
Pass from B̄_p to ∇ and Sel by surjection-from-nabla and I.6/ritter-weiss-transpose (DK Corollary 9.11).
acceptance: DK Corollary 9.11: Fitt_R(Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_R) ⊆ (Θ^#).

sources.match: Computes the Fitting ideal of B̄_p through relation matrices and the extra factor x, giving Fitt_R(B̄_p) ⊆ (Θ^#) and hence the bound for the Selmer module.

The local theorem includes the y_v and a product of local character differences multiplying Fitt_T(N); it applies without residual distinguishability. IHG.6 supplies the explicit finite-lattice/topology version used here.
Reduces the p = 2 case of the keystone theorem to the construction of (T̃, φ, ρ) and applies the residually indistinguishable Ribet lemma.

nodes.title: The keystone Fitting-ideal theorem
nodes.statement: (a) (Dasgupta–Kakde, p odd) With Σ = S_∞ ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v | p} and Σ' = T ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p}, the Z_p[G]^--module Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_p^- is quadratically presented and Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(Sel^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_p^-) = (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}). (b) (Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang, all p) For disjoint Σ, Σ' with (A1) Σ ∪ Σ' ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, (A2) O^×_{H,S∞,Σ'} torsion-free, (A3) Σ ≠ ∅, (A4) Σ ⊇ {v ∈ S_ram : v | p}, (A5) Σ' ⊇ {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p}: ∇^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_{p,−} is quadratically presented over Z_p[G]^- and Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(∇^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_{p,−}) = (Θ_{Σ,Σ'}/2^t), t = #(S_∞ ∩ Σ').
hypotheses: F totally real, H/F CM abelian, T with condition (1); p odd in (a), any p in (b).
proofSteps: Quadratic presentation: I.6/ritter-weiss-transpose (b), (d).
Inclusion: fitting-ideal-calculation for every component R, after passing to the trivial-zero-free quotient (DK Lemma 7.1).
Equality: inclusion-implies-equality.
For (b) at p = 2: DKSW §2 with the generalised Ritter–Weiss module whose depletion set need not contain S_∞.
acceptance: DK Theorem 1.7 = Theorem 3.3.
DKSW-BSZ Theorem 1.2.

sources.match: States the keystone result: the minus p-part of the Selmer module for the sets (20) is quadratically presented with Fitting ideal (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}).
Proves Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(∇^{Σ'}_Σ(H)_{p,−}) = (Θ_{Σ,Σ'}/2^t) for every prime p, the case p = 2 being new.

nodes.title: Kurihara's Theorem 2.12: Fitting ideals of modified Selmer and Ritter–Weiss modules
nodes.statement: Let K/k be a finite abelian CM extension of a totally real field, p any prime, S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram(K/k) and T a finite set of places disjoint from S with (O^T_{K,S})^× torsion-free. Then Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(∇^T_S(K)_{p,−}) = θ^T_{K/k,S}·Z_p[G]^- and Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(Sel^T_S(K)_p^-) = (θ^T_{K/k,S})^#·Z_p[G]^-. Both modules admit square finite free presentations. Their determinant can be zero on trivial-zero character components: if S contains a completely split finite prime, θ^T_{K/k,S} = 0. The intrinsic module maps and the Fitting identities are compatible with change of field; the cited sources do not choose coherent norm-compatible free bases and matrices. The I.9 consumer uses its derived module-control theorem together with the controlled Fitting/quadratic-presentation contract requested from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6. That contract needs no choices of compatible finite-level bases; the finite theorem here remains independent of I.9.
hypotheses: k totally real, K/k CM abelian, p any prime (p = 2 included), S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram(K/k), T disjoint with (O^T_{K,S})^× torsion-free.
proofSteps: Deduce from keystone-fitting-theorem (b) by moving the places of S_ram ∖ S_p and of S ∖ S_ram between depletion and smoothing sets, using the Euler-factor identities of I.3/stickelberger-functoriality and the depletion sequence for Selmer modules (Kurihara §2.6, after Lemma 6 of Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman's ETNC paper).
The Selmer statement follows by transpose (I.6/ritter-weiss-transpose (d); Burns–Kurihara–Sano Lemma 2.8).

DK Appendix B.1, Lemmas B.1–B.3, pp. 90–92, gives intrinsic functorial module maps compatible with the local maps. At p=2 take derived coefficient change by Z_p[G]⁻ and use right exactness only for the highest cohomology; minus projection is not exact. For the I.9 application, its T-modified cohomology model has highest H² equal to the modified Selmer module and no H³ under the torsion-free T hypothesis (BKS Proposition 2.4, pp. 571–574). I.9’s derived control then gives M/I_nM≅M_n, not coherent free matrices. Its limit Fitting identity and quadratic presentation follow from the separate generic L6 contract. This is a consumer interface and creates no I.7→I.9 proof dependency.
acceptance: Kurihara Theorem 2.12 with S ⊇ S_ram: the case used for the equivariant main conjecture.

sources.locator: §2.6, Theorem 2.12 and the surrounding discussion, pp. 12–15
sources.match: States that for S ⊇ S_ram and (O^T_{K,S})^× torsion-free, Fitt(∇^T_S(K)_{p,−}) = θ^T_{K/k,S}Z_p[G]^- and Fitt(Sel^T_S(K)^-_p) = (θ^T)^#, deduced from the keystone theorem of Dasgupta–Kakde (p > 2) and Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang (p = 2). Square presentation here does not imply a regular determinant; no coherent norm-compatible matrices are asserted.
Proves the functoriality of the presentation V^θ → B^θ of ∇ under passage to fixed fields, compatible with the maps α_v, β_v.

The intrinsic T-modified complex has Selmer H², torsion-unit dual H³, and canonical field-change/coefficient maps. This supplies the finite cohomology identification for I.9’s derived-control interface, not a choice of norm-compatible free bases.

uses.how: intrinsic norm maps and finite square presentations; I.9 derives M/I_nM≅M_n from its cohomological control model, without compatible bases
Fitting ideals commute with controlled quotient base change; L6 continuity and a bounded-relation argument give the limit square presentation
the unconditional abelian minus main theorem over the Iwasawa algebra

tests.name: quadratic_determinant_can_vanish
tests.statement: Add to S a finite prime split completely in K/k. Every character Euler factor is zero, so θ_S^T = 0 and a square presentation has zero determinant; quadratic does not imply torsion over every character component.

nodes.title: The p-modified Kurihara formula and Strong Brumer–Stark
nodes.statement: (a) For every odd prime p, Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(Sel^T_Σ(H)_p^-) = SK^T_p(H/F)^- with Σ = S_∞ ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v | p}. (b) (Strong Brumer–Stark, Kurihara's conjecture) Θ^#_{S,T} ∈ Fitt_{Z[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^{∨,-}) (2 inverted in Z[G]^-). (c) At p = 2: Θ^#_{S,T}/2^{n−1} annihilates (Cl^T(H)^-)^∨ over Z[G]^-, equivalently Θ_{S,T}/2^{n−1} annihilates Cl^T(H)^-, n = [F : Q].
hypotheses: F totally real, H/F CM abelian, S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, T with condition (1).
proofSteps: (a): from keystone-fitting-theorem (a) by changing smoothing sets: the Euler factors (1 − σ_v e_v Nv) are combinations of the generators (N I_v, 1 − σ_v e_v) (DK Remark 3.6, proof of Theorem 3.7, Lemma 3.9 on exterior powers).
(b): Sel^T_Σ(H)^- ↠ Cl^T(H)^{∨,-} (I.6/selmer-module), Fitting ideals grow under surjections, and Θ^#_{S,T} ∈ SK^T_p (I.6/sinnott-kurihara-ideal) (DK Corollary 3.8).
(c): DKSW Theorem 2.4 from keystone-fitting-theorem (b), the p = 2 version of (a) and Appendix B of Dasgupta–Kakde, and the dual exact sequence of their Lemma 4.21.
acceptance: DK Theorem 1.3 = Corollary 3.8.
DKSW-BSZ Theorem 2.4.

sources.match: Proves the p-modified Kurihara formula from the keystone theorem and deduces the Strong Brumer–Stark conjecture.
Proves the annihilation statement with Θ_{S,T}/2^{n−1} at p = 2 and deduces the Brumer–Stark conjecture over Z.

nodes.title: Kurihara's conjecture: the Fitting ideal of the dual class group
nodes.statement: For F totally real, H/F CM abelian and T with condition (1): Fitt_{Z[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^{∨,-}) = SK^T(H/F)^-. Equivalently, with s = #S_ram, Fitt^s_{Z[G]^-}(∇^T_{S∞}(H)^-) = (∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v·Θ_{J,T}(H_J/F) : S_∞ ⊆ J ⊆ S_∞ ∪ S_ram).
hypotheses: As stated; the equality is in Z[G]^- with 2 inverted (Dasgupta–Kakde).
proofSteps: Lemma B.4: the transpose of ∇^T_{S∞}(H) is Sel^T_{S∞}(H), with s excess generators, and Sel^T_{S∞}(H)^- ≅ Cl^T(H)^{∨,-} (I.6/ritter-weiss-transpose (c), I.6/selmer-module (b)).
Lemma B.6: descent formula for Fitt^{s−j} of ∇^T_J(H)_p through the functoriality of DK Appendix B.1 (2×2 determinants of (α_v, β_v)-values vanish, Lemma B.5).
Lemma B.7 from partial-kurihara-and-strong-brumer-stark (a), and Theorem B.8 by recombining over the partition J = Σ_0 ∪ J_0.
acceptance: DK Theorem 1.4 = Theorem 3.5.
For H = Q(μ_3), T = {7}: SK^{T,-} is the unit ideal after inverting 2 and Cl^T(H)^{∨,-} = 0.

sources.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1.4, p. 7; §3.3, Theorem 3.5, p. 21; Appendix B, Lemmas B.1–B.7 and Theorem B.8, pp. 89–97
sources.match: States Kurihara's conjecture and proves it by bootstrapping from the p-modified formula through the functoriality of ∇ and higher Fitting ideals.
Restates the Dasgupta–Kakde theorem as Fitt_{Z_p[G]^-}(((A^T_K)^-)^∨) = (Θ(K/k)^T_p)^# and draws the Strong Brumer–Stark consequence.

nodes.title: The Brumer–Stark theorem
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real of degree n, H/F finite abelian CM, S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram and T disjoint satisfying condition (1). Then Θ_{S,T} ∈ Ann_{Z[G]}(Cl^T(H)) (Brumer–Stark conjecture in Tate's form). Moreover, for every prime 𝔭 ∉ S ∪ T of F splitting completely in H and 𝔓 | 𝔭 in H, there is u ∈ H^× with |u|_w = 1 for every place w of H not above 𝔭 (including the complex places), Σ_{σ∈G} χ(σ) ord_{σ^{-1}(𝔓)}(u) = L_{S,T}(χ, 0) for every character χ, and u ≡ 1 mod 𝔮O_H for every 𝔮 ∈ T. Over Z[1/2] this is Dasgupta–Kakde; integrally it is Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang, who show that Θ_{S,T}/2^{n−1} annihilates Cl^T(H)^- (DKSW-BSZ Theorem 2.4) and for n ≥ 2 obtain the unit form with Θ_{S,T}/2^{n−2} in place of Θ_{S,T}. For n = 1, the integral Brumer–Stark unit statement uses the classical Q-case; it is not deduced by replacing Θ with 2Θ.
hypotheses: F totally real, H/F CM abelian, S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, T with condition (1).
proofSteps: Over Z[1/2]: from partial-kurihara-and-strong-brumer-stark (b) using Fitt ⊆ Ann, Ann(M^∨) = Ann(M)^# and cΘ = −Θ (I.6/cm-minus-parts-and-duals; DK p. 6).
At 2: partial-kurihara-and-strong-brumer-stark (c) and the construction of u from 𝔓^{Θ_{S,T}/2^{n−1}} = (z)𝔞^{1+c} (DKSW proof of Theorem 1.1, p. 9).

The cited Brumer–Stark unit theorem supplies a T-congruent anti-unit with the prescribed principal ideal. Annihilation alone supplies a principal ideal and does not imply all these constraints; no converse equivalence is claimed. For degree one use the classical Stickelberger case as in DKSW §2.2, pp. 8–10.
acceptance: For H = Q(μ_3), S = {∞, 3}, T = {7}: Θ_{S,T} = −(1 − c), and Cl^T(H) ≅ Z/6 with c acting trivially, so (1 − c) annihilates Cl^T(H).

sources.locator: §1, Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.2, pp. 4–5; equation (5), p. 5; §1.1, p. 6
sources.match: States the Brumer–Stark conjecture, proves it away from 2 and explains the equivalent formulation by Brumer–Stark units.

sources.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1.1, p. 4; §2.2, Theorem 2.4 and proof of Theorem 1.1, pp. 8–10
sources.match: Proves the Brumer–Stark conjecture over Z, in the unit form, with the refinement by 2^{n−2}.

nodes.title: Rubin's higher-rank Brumer–Stark conjecture away from 2
nodes.statement: Let S_0 ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram(H/F) be fixed, T disjoint satisfying condition (1), and V = {v_1,…,v_r} a set of finite primes outside S_0 ∪ T splitting completely in the CM abelian extension H/F; choose w_j | v_j. Let U_{V,T} consist of T-congruent elements of H^× with zero finite valuation outside V_H. On its minus rational part, the determinant of the valuations at w_j defines ord_G : ∧^r_{Q[G]} QU^-_{V,T} ≅ Q[G]^−. Define u_RBS by ord_G(u_RBS) = Θ_{S_0,T}, with the fixed set S_0, not V, on the right. Then u_RBS belongs to Rubin’s lattice after tensoring with Z[1/2]. The exterior bidual, lattice and order map are imported from EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.6; this target is the deduction from Kurihara’s formula (DK Theorem 1.6 and §3.4, pp. 8, 25–27).
hypotheses: F totally real, H/F CM abelian; S_0 contains infinity and ramification; V consists of distinct finite split primes outside S_0 ∪ T; T satisfies condition (1).
proofSteps: Express ϕ(u_{RBS}) = det(ϕ_i(u_j)) through the Fitting ideal of Cl^T(H)^{∨,-} computed by kurihara-fitting-formula, and apply the exterior-power annihilation lemma (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6/exterior-cokernel-annihilator; DK Lemma 3.9).

Use the integral lattice duality after inverting 2 and taking minus parts, with the # scalar restriction on the group-ring Hom and the contragredient action on the Z-linear Hom (I.6/cm-minus-parts-and-duals). This is the same dual convention as in the transpose and its Fitting formula.
Keep S_0 and V separate throughout. Putting a completely split v_j in the depletion set of Θ would multiply every character value by 1−1 and force the proposed right side to zero.
acceptance: DK Theorem 1.6: u_{RBS} ∈ 𝓛 ⊗_Z Z[1/2]; for r = 1 it is the Brumer–Stark theorem.

sources.locator: §1.2, the definitions (8)–(10), Conjecture 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp. 8–9; §3.4, pp. 25–27
sources.match: Recalls Rubin's lattice and the Rubin–Brumer–Stark element and deduces the prime-to-2 part of Rubin's conjecture from the Fitting ideal formula.

nodes.title: The nonequivariant main conjecture at every prime
nodes.statement: Let k be totally real, F/k finite abelian totally real, p any prime (p = 2 included), S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_p ∪ S_ram(F/k), and X = X_{F∞,S} = 𝔛_S(F_∞) with ramification at real places allowed. (a) At the augmentation prime 𝔭 = I(Gal(F_∞/k)) of Λ_{F∞}: Fitt_{Λ_{F∞,𝔭}}(X_𝔭) = (γ − 1)g_{F∞/k,S}Λ_{F∞,𝔭}, with γ a topological generator of Gal(k_∞/k); at every other height-one prime 𝔭, Fitt(X_𝔭) = g_{F∞/k,S}Λ_{F∞,𝔭}. (b) Assume F ∩ k_∞ = k, so that Gal(F_∞/k) = Gal(F/k) × Gal(F_∞/F) with Gal(F_∞/F) ≅ Gal(k_∞/k). For a character ψ of Gal(F/k), the ψ-quotient X_ψ = X ⊗_{Z_p[Gal(F/k)]} O_ψ is a finitely generated torsion O_ψ[[Gal(k_∞/k)]]-module with char(X_ψ) = (ψ(g_{F∞/k,S})) for ψ ≠ 1 and char(X_1) = ((γ − 1)·g_{F∞/k,S}) for ψ = 1. (c) For F = k and p = 2 this reads char_{Z_2[[T]]}(X_{F∞,S}) = ((γ − 1)g_{F∞/F,S}). (d) For p odd and ψ of order prime to p and of type S, (b) is Wiles's strong main conjecture of IntegralIwasawaTheory I.5; for p | ord ψ the ψ-quotient and the ψ-eigenspace may differ by modules killed by #Gal(F/k)_p, which are recorded and not discarded.
hypotheses: k totally real, F/k finite abelian totally real, p any prime, S as stated.
proofSteps: Apply IntegralIwasawaTheory I.9/integral-determinant-main-conjecture, Det(C_{F∞,S})^{-1} = g_{F∞/k,S}Λ_{F∞}, with H²(C) = X and H³(C) = Z_p (I.8/compact-complex-cohomology). Use the I.9 controlled-limit replacement specified in the handoff and the L6 Part II request: quotient control on the untwisted T-modified Selmer module, closed-ideal Fitting continuity and bounded-relation lifting of its square presentation. Apply the twist/minus-to-plus comparison after this step; a Tate twist sends I_n to its image ideal and must not be silently identified with the same finite-layer quotient.
Localise at height-one primes (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L5): (Z_p)_𝔭 = 0 unless 𝔭 is the augmentation prime, where Det(Z_p) contributes γ − 1 (Kurihara §4.2, first remark, p. 27).

Apply the same smoothed-Selmer proof after ψ coefficient change, not only a formal tensor of the height-one equality: use its projective presentation, the T-local Euler modules, and the derived base-change triangle. The quotient has characteristic ideal ψ(g) for ψ≠1 and (γ−1)ψ(g) for ψ=1 (Kurihara §4.2, second remark, p. 27). For prime-to-p ψ this is an exact idempotent summand; in the p-power part retain Tor terms until the presentation comparison.
Compare with I.5/main-conjecture-statement for p odd using I.3/deligne-ribet-dictionary (vi).
acceptance: Kurihara §4.2, p. 27: char(X_{F∞,S})_ψ is generated by the image of g for ψ ≠ 1 and by (γ − 1) times it for ψ trivial.
SpecialValuesBirchTate B.6/kurihara-main-conjecture-over-f is the instance F = k, p = 2.

sources.locator: §4.1–4.2, Theorem 4.1, the proof and the three remarks, pp. 24–27
sources.match: Proves the equivariant main conjecture Det(RΓ_c)^{-1} = gΛ for all p and derives the characteristic ideals of X_{F∞,S} and of its ψ-quotients, with the factor γ − 1 at the trivial character.
Uses the 2-adic main conjecture for the trivial character over a totally real field, with ramification at the real places allowed.

planet.name: Nonequivariant main conjecture at all primes

nodes.title: The Kurihara–Kolster module dictionary at p = 2
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p=2, d=[F:Q], S=S_2∪S∞, K∞=F∞(i), Γ=Gal(F∞/F), γ a generator and u=κ(γ). Put X=𝔛_S(F∞) with real ramification allowed. Let A^- be the ordinary norm-minus class direct limit of K∞, and define N=Hom(A^-,Q_2/Z_2) with the covariant action (γφ)(a)=φ(γa). Choose a generator f_F(γ) of char_Λ(N), including its 2-power content; its distinguished polynomial alone is insufficient when μ(N)≠0. Then char_Λ(ι_u X)=(2^d f_F), where ι_u(γ)=uγ^{-1}, equivalently T↦u(1+T)^{-1}−1. The actual maps are the filtration 0→(A^-)^∨→Y→C_F→0 and 0→Y→X(−1)→Z/2(−1)→0 of I.4/dyadic-real-place-correction. Also Y=(Sel_S(K∞)_2)^−, so its twist by 1 injects into X with cokernel Z/2 as in I.9/dyadic-selmer-comparison. In the Burns–Flach compact-support convention H²(C_{F∞,S})=X and H³(C)=Z_2. Enlargement of S uses the local Euler modules of I.4, with finite and height-one errors kept separate. The abelian going-up comparison is I.5/going-up-induction.
hypotheses: F totally real, p = 2, S = S_2 ∪ S_∞.
proofSteps: Use the two exact sequences proved in I.4/dyadic-real-place-correction, whose correction module is the dual of real unit square classes and has characteristic ideal (2^d). Kurihara Lemma 4.2 identifies Y with the minus quotient of the inverse-limit Selmer module, since its dual is H^{J=−1}. The descent cokernel has order two; it is not the module C_F.

The standard contragredient dual (A^-)^∨ has γ acting by precomposition with γ^{-1}, so char((A^-)^∨)=ι(f_F), where ι(γ)=γ^{-1}. The exact filtration gives char(X(−1))=2^d ι(f_F). With the explicit Tate convention M(j):γm=u^jγ_Mm, a characteristic series h of M changes to h(u^{-j}γ). Apply ι to h_X(uγ)=2^d f_F(γ^{-1}): this is h_X(uγ^{-1})=2^d f_F(γ), which is the stated ι_u formula.

This derivation fixes the dual/twist convention before using Kolster Lemma 2, p. 250. In these coordinates the scalar specialization is f_F(u^{-1}), or f_F(u^{-1}−1) if f_F is written as a series in T. A different convention for Hom reverses γ and must change the substitution too.

nodes.title: The weight-two finite Euler characteristic with all factors
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p = 2, S = S_2 ∪ S_∞ and X = X_{F∞,S} (real places may ramify). Then: (a) X(−2)^Γ = 0 and X(−2)_Γ is finite, with v_2(#X(−2)_Γ) = v_2(ζ_F(−1)) + v_2(w_2(F)); (b) #X(−2)_Γ = #H²_et(O_F[1/2], Z_2(2)) and #H¹_et(O_F[1/2], Z_2(2)) = w_2(F)_2; hence ζ_F(−1) ∼_2 #H²_et(O_F[1/2], Z_2(2))/#H¹_et(O_F[1/2], Z_2(2)); (c) the derived specialisation C_{F∞,S} ⊗^L_{Λ, κ²} Z_2 has finite cohomology, its Euler characteristic is computed by (a)–(b), and the Tor terms, the order-two cokernel of kurihara-kolster-module-dictionary (a) and the factor 2^{[F:Q]} at p = 2 appear explicitly in the comparison with Kolster's |(T ⊗ A^-_∞)^Γ| and |K_2(O_F)(2)| = 2^{[F:Q]}|(T ⊗ A^-_∞)^Γ|; (d) the identities are compatible with enlarging S. For odd p, the twist κ² does not factor through Gal(F_∞/F) unless ω² is trivial on Gal(F(μ_p)/F), and the corresponding statement is I.5/special-value-endpoint over F(μ_p). The implication to K_2 and W_2 is owned by SpecialValuesBirchTate B.6. In the compact-support convention H² after specialisation is X(−2)_Γ and H³ is Z_2(−2)_Γ of order w_2(F)_2, giving Euler quotient #H²/#H³. The two exact sequences of I.4 supply the map-level comparison with Kolster’s norm-kernel module. All finite errors are retained in the associated derived specialisation triangles before their Euler quotients cancel.
hypotheses: F totally real; p = 2; S = S_2 ∪ S_∞.
proofSteps: (a): evaluate char(X) = ((γ − 1)g) (nonequivariant-characteristic-ideal (c)) at κ(γ)² − 1 after the twist, use that X has no nonzero finite Λ-submodule (I.2/weak-leopoldt (c)) and the interpolation κ²(g) = L_S(−1, 1) = ζ_F(−1)∏_{v|p}(1 − Nv) (I.3/deligne-ribet-dictionary (i); κ² factors through Γ at p = 2 because ω² = 1), the Euler factors 1 − Nv for v | 2 being odd, and v_2(κ(γ)² − 1) = v_2(w_2(F)) (I.4/coinvariant-euler-characteristic).
(b): I.4/twisted-coinvariant-descent (d), together with H¹(O_F[1/2], Z_2(2)) ≅ H⁰(F, Q_2/Z_2(2)) for F totally real (Kolster Lecture 1, §2; Rognes–Weibel p. 47).

For the modified compact-support complex the derived coinvariant spectral sequence has H²=X(−2)_Γ and H³=Z_2(−2)_Γ; possible invariant Tor terms vanish here by finiteness and absence of finite submodules. To compare to classes, use the two exact sequences of I.4 before specializing. A finite error E contributes #E_Γ/#E^Γ=1 because both groups have the same order, so its Tor term cannot be dropped separately. The contragredient dual of the discrete (Tate module Z_2(1)⊗A^-) has series f_F(u^{-1}γ^{-1}); its coinvariants are dual to the discrete Γ-invariants. Their order is |f_F(u^{-1})|_2^{-1}, using no finite submodules of (A^-)^∨ and finiteness at this specialization. The dictionary gives |h_X(u²)|_2^{-1}=2^d|f_F(u^{-1})|_2^{-1}. Hence #X(−2)_Γ=2^d#(Z_2(1)⊗A^-)^Γ, agreeing with Kolster Theorem 1. This calculation includes μ through the full series f_F.
(d): I.4/s-enlargement-euler-factors.

Part II: an all-residual local weighted Ribet existence theorem, with the following contract. Let T⊂T̃ be commutative noetherian rings, T local, both complete for m_T; in this application T̃ is finite over T. Let 0≠Ĩ≠T̃, I=Ĩ∩T, K=Frac(T̃) an Artinian principal ideal ring (finite product of local principal rings, allowed nonreduced). Let G be compact, ρ:G→GL₂(K) continuous and irreducible after every field quotient; χ,ψ:G→T× continuous. Require every characteristic polynomial to lie in T[X] and reduce to (X−χ(g))(X−ψ(g)) modulo I. Give finite local data S=Σ⊔P, G_v and I_v⊂G_v, a lower triangular basis over K with diagonal η_v,ξ_v:G_v→T̃×, ξ_v≡ψ on G_v for v∈Σ and ξ_v≡χ on I_v for v∈P; choose v₀∈Σ when nonempty and σ_v∈G_v for v∈P. Include a finite T-lattice in M₂(K) containing Δχ,Δψ whose induced topology is m_T-adic. Output a finite T-module N, continuous κ∈Z¹(G,N(χψ⁻¹)), and y_v for v∈Σ\{v₀}, jointly generating N with κ(G), with κ(G_v₀)=0, κ(g)=(χψ⁻¹(g)−1)y_v on the other G_v, κ(I_v)=0 for v∈P, and the cohomology class unramified wherever ρ is. Require (∏_{v∈P}(ξ_v(σ_v)−χ(σ_v)))·Fitt_T(N)T̃⊂Ĩ. No residual coincidence hypothesis. Source: DKSW-BSZ Theorem 2.15, pp. 18–19; DKSW-RIBET Theorem 2.1 and Remark 2.2, pp. 7–9. Proof route: use current local_ribet with its actual hres when χ≡ψ mod m_T; for distinct residues use the b-coefficient lattice proof cited by Remark 2.2 with the same adjoined local generators and weighted relation-matrix determinant calculation. Only existence of N is required in this branch, not an unproved identification with the current canonical difference quotient. The existing hres theorem alone does not fulfill this Part II request.

Part II: finite-weight ordinary Hilbert eigenform representations for every totally real F, every p including 2, and parallel integer weight k>1. For a cuspidal eigenform of level n, nebentypus ψ and coefficient field E, supply a continuous irreducible ρ_f:G_F→GL₂(E), unramified outside np, with trace c(q,f) and determinant ψ(q)κ(q)^{k−1} at arithmetic Frob_q for q∤np. At each p-adic ordinary place give a lower triangular basis with η unramified, η(Frob_p)=U_p, and ξ=ψκ^{k−1}η⁻¹. Include coefficient descent to a finite field extension and extension of scalars to the finite quadratic principal algebra E[U_ℓ]/(U_ℓ²−c(ℓ,f)U_ℓ+ψ(ℓ)Nℓ^{k−1}); repeated roots are allowed. At an auxiliary ℓ, a newform needs the Steinberg local description; an ℓ-old form needs unramified nonscalar Frobenius, its minimal polynomial equal to the Hecke polynomial, and the companion-matrix triangularization over this quadratic algebra. Source: DKSW-BSZ §3.3, Lemmas 3.10–3.12, equations (46)–(47) and Theorem 3.14, pp. 27–30. R19.2 owns the general finite-weight existence and local representation statements; I.7 owns their assembly over the finite Hecke order and the congruence checks. Its present odd-p/even-degree wiles-ordinary-hilbert-representation is only a subcase, and is not cited as the full supplier.

Part II: all-prime finite-weight Hilbert modular forms over the character coefficient orders used by DK and DKSW, with arbitrary totally real degree and the indicated p-power and auxiliary-ℓ raised levels. (1) For every m and sufficiently large N, a parallel-weight k multiple of (p−1)p^N admits V_k∈M_k(1,Z_p), all its normalized cusp expansions integral and V_k≡1 mod p^m (DK Theorem 8.8, p. 54; DKSW-BSZ Theorem 3.2, p. 24). (2) For sufficiently large odd weights, supply the group-ring forms with prescribed total constant terms on C∞(n) and vanishing on C∞(P,n)\C∞(n), with the narrow-class/sign normalization of DK Theorem 8.9, p. 54. (3) Given a finite character family f_ψ with constants divisible by p^m, m≥v_p(#G_p), supply h over the character group-ring order such that f_ψ−(p^m/#G_p)h_ψ has zero constants on C∞(P,n); it is cuspidal for P=1 and becomes cuspidal after e_P^ord otherwise (DK Theorem 8.15, p. 58). (4) Supply integral q-expansion faithfulness and coefficient change, the finite ordinary projector, Hecke and degeneracy formulas for these precise finite-weight spaces and coefficient orders, including p=2 and ℓ-old quadratic U_ℓ algebras. These inputs give DK Theorems 8.17–8.18, pp. 59–60, and the separate DKSW-BSZ Theorem 3.3, Theorem 3.5 and Corollaries 3.6, 3.8, pp. 24–26; I.7 combines them into its specified cusp congruences and Hecke map. APL remains the owner of the Hilbert-form/Eisenstein suppliers and uses AutomorphicBundles B5 for the needed integral expansion extension. No p-odd Λ-adic control theorem or reduced Hecke algebra is assumed in the all-prime finite-weight branch.

Part II, controlled Fitting/quadratic-presentation limit: R is a complete noetherian semilocal O-order finite free over O[[Γ]], such as an abelian tower group algebra or its torsion-free minus quotient, with I_n=(γ^{p^n}−1), I_n eventually contained in every power of the Jacobson radical. Let M be a finitely generated R-module and give compatible isomorphisms M/I_nM≅M_n. Then Fitt_R(M)R/I_n=Fitt_{R/I_n}(M_n), and Fitt_R(M)=∩_n preimage(Fitt_{R/I_n}(M_n)); ideals are closed by noetherian completeness. For genuinely profinite inverse limits one also uses (p^a,I_n), not a claim that the I_n alone form an adic neighborhood basis. If every M_n has a square free presentation, M has one as well: decompose the semilocal ring into local factors, take a minimal finite free cover R^r→M with kernel K, and cancel surplus free generators in finite presentations (or apply Schanuel) to bound the number of generators of its finite relation image by r. Artin–Rees and I_n⊂Jac(R)^N for large n give K∩I_nR^r⊂Jac(R)K, so a sufficiently deep relation image detects K/Jac(R)K. Nakayama supplies at most r relations for K; pad by zero columns to obtain a square matrix. Minors and closed ideals give the Fitting limit identity with no compatible finite bases. If a compatible θ∞ generates every finite Fitting ideal, it generates Fitt_R(M); prove θ∞ is a non-zerodivisor separately by nonvanishing in every characteristic-zero character component before inferring injectivity or projective dimension one. Source/application: Kurihara §4.2, pp. 24–25; the stated bounded-relation proof is the generic algebraic interface supplied here to the existing owner. Current TauCeti.fittingIdeal already provides the all-index carrier; this request only concerns the additional continuity/control theorem. Apply this contract before Tate twisting, or transport the ideals I_n by the twist automorphism; a twist does not preserve the ordinary finite-layer quotient ideal.

Part II: for a number field K, finite S⊇S_p∪S∞ and ordinary restricted-ramification G_S(K), finite-dimensional H^i(G_S,F_p) for i≤2, truncated Euler sum χ₂=−r₂(K), and H₂(G_S,Z_p) torsion-free (equivalently H²(G_S,Q_p/Z_p) divisible), including p=2 and real K. Supply the finite-unit Poitou–Tate identification with augmented real μ₂ terms, and compact-homology/discrete-cohomology duality and their corestriction/restriction tower compatibility. Sources: NSW 8.3.20, 8.7.5, 8.7.7 as used explicitly in Theorem 10.3.22, pp. 639–640; the unit sequence is 10.3.13, pp. 630–632. I.2 owns the arithmetic unit map and the resulting weak-Leopoldt argument. This is a truncated ordinary Euler statement, not the false assertion cd₂(G_S)≤2 in the real case; the current D7 compact-support Euler theorem has the narrower hypothesis (P) and is not a supplier for this extension.

Part II, Q ordinary forms and Hecke control including Eisenstein components: p≥5, N=1 (or tame N prime to p), O a finite coefficient DVR and Λ=O[[1+pZ_p]]. Supply the full and cuspidal ordinary Λ-adic form modules and their Hecke algebras with the a₁-duality, finite Λ-freeness, and Hecke-equivariant classical weight/level quotients by ω_{k,r}=(1+T)^{p^{r−1}}−υ^{(k−2)p^{r−1}}. Retain the boundary term at an Eisenstein localization; do not assume residual irreducibility or integral Gorensteinness. Use the actual integral q-expansion lattices and distinguish the module allowing a fractional constant term when needed. This extends L1’s existing ordinary modular-curve tower; L5’s even-degree definite quaternionic construction is not the Q object. Proof route: ordinary projectors commute with the modular-curve transition maps; Hida control identifies their finite quotients; the first Fourier-coefficient Hecke pairing identifies the dual lattice and its Hecke specialization. Source: Sharifi AWS Definitions 4.2.1–4.2.6, Theorems 4.2.5, 4.2.7, 4.2.9 and Corollary 4.2.12, pp. 45–47. I.5 proves only its particular Eisenstein congruence quotient from this input.

Part II, Q ordinary Tate module at Eisenstein components: p≥5, tame N=1, h the cuspidal ordinary Hecke algebra from PadicFamilies L1 Part II. Let T=lim_r H¹_et(X₁(Np^r),Z_p(1))^ord with trace transition maps. Supply its continuous G_Q-action, finite Λ-freeness and rank two over the total quotient algebra Q(h), the arithmetic-Frobenius polynomial X²−T_ℓX+ℓ⟨ℓ⟩ for ℓ∤Np, and unramifiedness outside Np. Over G_Qp supply 0→T_sub→T→T_quo→0: the quotient is Λ-torsion-free and unramified, with Frobenius U_p, and the submodule has inertia action h^ι(1); T_quo identifies with the ordinary cusp-form module as an h-module. As a sequence of Q(h)-modules the filtration splits over total fractions, where both pieces have rank one; no G_Qp-equivariant splitting is asserted. Do not require residual irreducibility, a free rank-two integral h-lattice, or the even-degree hypothesis of the current Hilbert-family node. Proof route: form the ordinary trace limit and its classical control; the connected–étale sequence of the ordinary Jacobian p-divisible groups gives the local quotient. Identify its cotangent module with ordinary cusp forms after unramified scalar extension, then descend the module identification; the U_p-adjusted, Atkin–Lehner-modified Weil pairing determines the submodule and makes the trace maps compatible. Specialization and density give the Frobenius identities. Sources: Sharifi AWS Theorems 4.2.13–4.2.15 and the following construction, pp. 47–49. I.5 separately proves the Eisenstein matrix congruences, faithfulness and unramified Ribet class.

sourceIssues.locator: Lecture 1, §1, p. 6, in the author PDF read (Maine–Québec site; the notes are formatted for the IAS/Park City Mathematics Series)
sourceIssues.printed: For a number field F and a prime p, the notes write Gal(F(μ_{p^∞})/F) as Γ × Δ with Δ isomorphic to Gal(F(ζ_{2p})/F), and define ω on Δ.
sourceIssues.correction: This holds for odd p, and for p = 2 when F has a real place or contains i. In general at p = 2 the torsion of Gal(F(μ_{2^∞})/F) need not be Gal(F(i)/F): the decomposition holds with Δ the torsion subgroup, and ω must be defined on the whole group through the projection Z_2^× → {±1}.
sourceIssues.reason: For F = Q(√−2), the σ_a with a ∈ Z_2^× fixing √−2 = ζ_8 + ζ_8^3 are those with a ≡ 1 or 3 mod 8; this subgroup has index 2 in Z_2^× and contains no torsion, so Gal(F(μ_{2^∞})/F) ≅ Z_2, while [F(i) : F] = 2.
searched: a web search for the notes and a published version (Arithmetic of L-functions, IAS/Park City Mathematics Series), whose text was not obtained

review.reason: The stated general dyadic product with Δ = Gal(F(i)/F) fails for F = Q(√−2): the cyclotomic image is a ≡ 1 or 3 mod 8, is torsion-free, and nevertheless F(i)/F has degree 2. The correct torsion subgroup and whole-group Teichmüller projection are used in I.1. Checked Kolster Lecture 1 §1, p. 6.

sourceIssues.printed: The local value condition in the theorem uses the scalar χψ⁻¹−1 multiplying its named vector. The construction then imposes the same relation with the opposite scalar 1−χψ⁻¹ and says these named vectors satisfy the theorem.
sourceIssues.correction: Either impose the relation with χψ⁻¹−1 in the construction, or use the negatives of the construction’s free vectors as the theorem’s local vectors.
sourceIssues.reason: In the constructed quotient the displayed relation gives κ(σ)=(1−χψ⁻¹(σ))y_v. Replacing y_v by −y_v produces the theorem’s convention. This changes neither generation nor the Fitting bound and does not invalidate the existence theorem. The roadmap uses the theorem convention, as current IHG.6 already does.

review.reason: The local relation and the theorem use opposite signs for the same named generator. Renaming that generator by its negative reconciles them without changing the result.
